_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-03 01:11:43Z)**_

## Summary

**Root cause:** The `dist plan` job failed (exit 255) on the consistency check, not anything wrong with your code. cargo-dist's `dist plan` verifies that the committed `.github/workflows/release.yml` matches the workflow it would auto-generate. But your `release.yml` is **intentionally hand-maintained** for the Release Trust pipeline (custom `release-policy` job, fail-closed lanes, signing/provenance/notarization) and has fully diverged from the dist template. The error said the file *"has out of date contents and needs to be regenerated"* — dist wanted to overwrite all your hardening work back to its boilerplate.

**Fix:** Added `allow-dirty = ["ci"]` to the `[dist]` section of `dist-workspace.toml`. This is the documented cargo-dist setting that says "this CI file is hand-edited on purpose — skip the generate-and-check step." Plan check now won't try to validate `release.yml` against the template.

```toml
ci = ["github"]
allow-dirty = ["ci"]   # release.yml is hand-maintained for Release Trust
installers = ["shell", "powershell", "homebrew"]
```

**A couple notes:**
- I couldn't run `dist plan` to verify locally — `dist` isn't installed on this machine. The TOML parses cleanly and `allow-dirty = ["ci"]` is the standard, long-supported fix for exactly this error, so I'm confident, but the true confirmation will be the next CI run.
- There were also non-blocking warnings worth a future cleanup: a Homebrew `homepage` is missing from `Cargo.toml`, and Node.js 20 actions (`actions/checkout@v4`, `actions/upload-artifact@v4`) are deprecated as of June 16. Neither caused this failure.

I haven't committed or pushed (per the goal's "no git push by the agent" posture). Want me to commit this change to a branch, or would you like to review and push it yourself?

```text
#!/usr/bin/env node

import { spawnSync } from "node:child_process";
import crypto from "node:crypto";
import fs from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";

const OFFICIAL_REPO = "gdc/deadreckon";
const TARGETS = [
  "aarch64-apple-darwin",
  "x86_64-apple-darwin",
  "aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu",
  "x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu",
  "x86_64-pc-windows-msvc",
];

const command = process.argv[2];
const args = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(3));

try {
  switch (command) {
    case "lane":
      writeJson(classifyRelease(args));
      break;
    case "validate":
      validateRelease(args);
      break;
    case "preflight":
      preflight(args);
      break;
    case "sbom":
      writeSbom(args);
      break;
    case "checksums":
      writeChecksums(args);
      break;
    case "manifest":
      writeManifest(args);
      break;
    case "verify-manifest":
      verifyManifest(args);
      break;
    case "verify-homebrew":
      verifyHomebrew(args);
      break;
    default:
      throw new Error(
        "usage: release-trust.mjs <lane|validate|preflight|sbom|checksums|manifest|verify-manifest|verify-homebrew>",
      );
  }
} catch (error) {
  console.error(error.message);
  process.exit(1);
}

function parseArgs(values) {
  const parsed = {};
  for (let index = 0; index < values.length; index += 1) {
    const value = values[index];
    if (!value.startsWith("--")) {
      continue;
    }
    const withoutPrefix = value.slice(2);
    const equals = withoutPrefix.indexOf("=");
    if (equals !== -1) {
      parsed[withoutPrefix.slice(0, equals)] = withoutPrefix.slice(equals + 1);
      continue;
    }
    const next = values[index + 1];
    if (next && !next.startsWith("--")) {
      parsed[withoutPrefix] = next;
      index += 1;
    } else {
      parsed[withoutPrefix] = true;
    }
  }
  return parsed;
}

function option(name, envName, fallback = "") {
  return args[name] ?? process.env[envName] ?? fallback;
}

function classifyRelease(localArgs = args) {
  const ref = localArgs.ref ?? process.env.GITHUB_REF ?? "";
  const repo = localArgs.repo ?? process.env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY ?? "";
  const officialRepo = localArgs["official-repo"] ?? process.env.DEADRECKON_OFFICIAL_REPO ?? OFFICIAL_REPO;
  const isTag = ref.startsWith("refs/tags/");
  const tag = isTag ? ref.slice("refs/tags/".length) : (localArgs["ref-name"] ?? process.env.GITHUB_REF_NAME ?? "");
  const stable = /^v(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)$/.exec(tag);
  const rc = /^v(\d+)\.(\d+)\.(\d+)-rc\.(\d+)$/.exec(tag);
  let lane = "branch";
  let version = null;
  let rcNumber = null;
  if (isTag && stable) {
    lane = "stable";
    version = `${stable[1]}.${stable[2]}.${stable[3]}`;
  } else if (isTag && rc) {
    lane = "rc";
    version = `${rc[1]}.${rc[2]}.${rc[3]}`;
    rcNumber = Number.parseInt(rc[4], 10);
  } else if (isTag) {
    lane = "invalid_tag";
  }

  const official_repo = repo === officialRepo;
  const releaseLane = lane === "stable" || lane === "rc";
  const officialRelease = official_repo && releaseLane;
  return {
    schema_version: 1,
    lane,
    tag: releaseLane ? tag : null,
    version,
    rc_number: rcNumber,
    ref,
    repository: repo,
    official_repo,
    build_artifacts: releaseLane,
    publishes: officialRelease,
    publish_github_release: officialRelease,
    publish_homebrew: official_repo && lane === "stable",
    publish_npm: official_repo && lane === "stable",
    release_notes_mode: lane === "rc" ? "prerelease" : lane === "stable" ? "stable" : "none",
    requires_macos_signing: officialRelease,
    requires_windows_signing: official_repo && lane === "stable",
    requires_attestation: officialRelease,
    requires_homebrew_token: official_repo && lane === "stable",
    requires_npm_provenance: official_repo && lane === "stable",
  };
}

function validateRelease(localArgs = args) {
  const lane = classifyRelease(localArgs);
  if (lane.lane === "invalid_tag") {
    throw new Error(`invalid release tag: ${lane.ref}`);
  }
  if (!lane.build_artifacts) {
    writeJson(lane);
    return;
  }

## How a release is triggered

There's no button — the workflow keys entirely off **the git tag shape** you push. The classifier (`release/trust/release-trust.mjs`) parses the tag:

| Tag you push | Lane | Regex |
|---|---|---|
| `v1.2.3` | `stable` | `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+$` |
| `v1.2.3-rc.1` | `rc` | `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+-rc\.\d+$` |
| anything else (`v1.2`, `1.2.3`, `release-1`) | `invalid_tag` → **fails the run** |
| no tag (branch/PR push) | `branch` → plan check only (what we just fixed) |

So a real build is: bump version → tag `vX.Y.Z[-rc.N]` → `git push origin <tag>`.

## ⚠️ The gate that will surprise you: this isn't the "official" repo

The classifier hardcodes `OFFICIAL_REPO = "gdc/deadreckon"`, but your remote is **`gregce/deadreckon`**. Everything that *distributes* is gated on `official_repo = (repo === "gdc/deadreckon")`, which is **false here**. So what each lane does **on `gregce/deadreckon`**:

| Step | rc tag | stable tag |
|---|---|---|
| Build all 5 targets + installers + Homebrew formula | ✅ | ✅ |
| Trust bundle (SBOM, SHA256SUMS, manifest) as **run artifacts** | ✅ | ✅ |
| macOS signing / notarization | ⛔ skipped | ⛔ skipped |
| Attestation / provenance | ⛔ | ⛔ |
| **GitHub Release published** | ⛔ | ⛔ |
| Homebrew tap / npm publish | ⛔ | ⛔ |

**Net:** on this repo, tagging gives you a *fully-built, downloadable artifact set attached to the Actions run* — but nothing gets published to a Release page or package manager. That's the pipeline's intended "forks stay usable without secrets" behavior.

**A) Exercise the pipeline now (safe dry run)** — push an RC tag:

```
This builds everything across all targets and uploads the artifacts to the run. No secrets needed, nothing published. Best way to prove the build/sign/trust machinery works end-to-end.

**B) Actually distribute officially** — the design targets `gdc/deadreckon`. To publish from `gregce/deadreckon` you'd need to:
1. Make this repo "official" — set `DEADRECKON_OFFICIAL_REPO=gregce/deadreckon` (env in the `release-policy` job) or fix the constant; also update the hardcoded `gdc/deadreckon` in the attestation-verify doc (`release.yml:426`).
2. Configure the secrets, or the **preflight fails closed**. Required for a stable tag:
   - macOS: `APPLE_CERT_P12`, `APPLE_CERT_PWD`, `APPLE_ID`, `APPLE_TEAM_ID`, `APPLE_APP_PWD`
   - Homebrew: `HOMEBREW_TAP_TOKEN`
   - npm: `NPM_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING=true` or `NPM_TOKEN`
   - Windows: `WINDOWS_CERT_PFX`, `WINDOWS_CERT_PWD`
3. Keep versions in sync — stable additionally requires the npm wrapper `package.json` version to match **and** a `CHANGELOG.md` section for that version, or `validate` throws.

The dry run did its job — it **surfaced a real bug** in the pipeline's RC version model. Here's the failure:

```
× This workspace doesn't have anything for dist to Release!
  help: --tag=v0.1.0 will Announce: deadreckon
```

**Root cause — two gates with contradictory expectations for RC tags:**

The rc lane runs `dist host --steps=create --tag=v0.1.0-rc.1`. cargo-dist treats the **full tag** as the version, so it looks for a package versioned `0.1.0-rc.1` — but `Cargo.toml` is `0.1.0`, so it finds nothing to release. cargo-dist's rule is: **the package version must exactly equal the tag**, prerelease suffix included (you'd set `Cargo.toml` to `0.1.0-rc.1` and tag `v0.1.0-rc.1`).

But your trust pipeline's `validate` does the opposite — it *strips* `-rc.N` and asserts `Cargo.toml == 0.1.0` (`release-trust.mjs:97,143`). So:

- To satisfy **`dist host`**: `Cargo.toml` must be `0.1.0-rc.1`
- To satisfy **`validate`**: `Cargo.toml` must be `0.1.0`

These can't both hold. **No RC tag can pass both gates as currently written** — a genuine gap in the Release Trust slice, not something the `allow-dirty` fix touched.

    raw: &str,
    temp: &Path,
    home: &Path,
    root: &Path,
    cwd: &Path,
    run_id: &str,
    scope: &str,
) -> String {
    let mut text = raw.to_string();
    for (from, to) in [
        (root, "<IMPORT_ROOT>"),
        (home, "<HOME>"),
        (cwd, "<CWD>"),
        (temp, "<TEMP>"),
    ] {
        if let Ok(canonical) = from.canonicalize() {
            text = text.replace(&canonical.display().to_string(), to);
        }
        text = text.replace(&from.display().to_string(), to);
    }
    text = text.replace(run_id, "<RUN_ID>");
    text = text.replace(scope, "<SCOPE>");
    text = normalize_wrapped_import_show_paths(&text);
    let mut normalized = text
        .lines()
        .map(normalize_import_show_line)
        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
        .join("\n");
    normalized.push('\n');
    normalized
}

fn normalize_wrapped_import_show_paths(text: &str) -> String {
    text.replace("<HOME>/ru\n            nstate/", "<HOME>/runstate/")
        .replace("<TEMP>\n            /workspace", "<CWD>")
}

#![allow(
    clippy::expect_used,
    clippy::needless_pass_by_value,

use std::path::Path;

const AUDIT: &str = concat!(
    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"),
    "/../../docs/AUDIT-2026-05-11.md"
);
const REPORT: &str = "/Users/gdc/stoa/docs/research/2026-05-10-unmet-needs/REPORT.md";

#[test]
fn audit_doc_lists_all_25_needs_with_status() {
    let audit = read_audit();
    let rows = audit_rows(&audit);
    let needs = report_need_titles();

    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 25, "audit rows:\n{rows:#?}");
    for (idx, need) in needs.iter().enumerate() {
        let row = rows
            .iter()
            .find(|row| row.columns[0] == (idx + 1).to_string())
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing row {}", idx + 1));
        assert_eq!(row.columns[1], *need);
        assert!(!row.columns[2].trim().is_empty(), "missing status: {row:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn audit_doc_status_values_are_closed_enum() {
    let audit = read_audit();
    for row in audit_rows(&audit) {
        assert!(
            matches!(
                row.columns[2].as_str(),
                "Resolved" | "Partial" | "Unmet" | "V1"
            ),
            "invalid status in row: {row:?}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn audit_doc_evidence_paths_resolve_under_repo() {
    let audit = read_audit();
    let repo = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
        .parent()
        .and_then(Path::parent)
        .expect("repo root");
    for row in audit_rows(&audit) {
        let evidence = &row.columns[3];
        let path = evidence
            .split(['`', ' ', '('])
            .find(|part| {
                part.starts_with("crates/")
                    || part.starts_with("docs/")
                    || part.starts_with("README.md")
                    || part.starts_with("HOWTO.md")
                    || part.starts_with("CHANGELOG.md")
                    || part.starts_with("demo.cast")
            })
            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing evidence path in row: {row:?}"))
            .trim_end_matches([',', ')', ';']);
        let path = path.split(':').next().expect("path before line");
        assert!(
            repo.join(path).exists(),
            "evidence path does not exist: {path} in row {row:?}"
        );
    }
}

#[test]
fn audit_doc_closures_map_lists_p2_through_p10() {
    let audit = read_audit();
    for phase in 2..=10 {
        let needle = format!("P{phase} ");
        assert!(audit.contains(&needle), "missing closure phase {needle}");
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
struct AuditRow {
    columns: Vec<String>,
}

fn read_audit() -> String {
    std::fs::read_to_string(AUDIT).expect("docs/AUDIT-2026-05-11.md should exist")
}

fn audit_rows(audit: &str) -> Vec<AuditRow> {

        .collect()
}

fn report_need_titles() -> Vec<String> {

        .expect("REPORT.md")
        .lines()
        .filter_map(|line| line.strip_prefix("## Need: "))

        .collect()

            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "https://api.github.com/repos/gdc/deadreckon/releases".to_string());
        let releases = client
            .get(url)
            .header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, "deadreckon-update")
            .send()
            .await
            .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?
            .error_for_status()
            .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?
            .json::<Vec<GithubRelease>>()
            .await
            .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
        let Some(release) = releases.into_iter().next() else {
            return Err("no releases found".to_string());
        };
        return Ok(release.into_latest_update());
    }

    let url = std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_RELEASES_URL").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
        "https://api.github.com/repos/gdc/deadreckon/releases/latest".to_string()
    });
    client
        .get(url)

Now I see the real issue. The formula has `url` lines (nested per-platform) but **no `sha256` lines at all** — cargo-dist only populates formula checksums at *host/publish* time, not during `dist build --artifacts=global`. So at the `release trust artifacts` stage the formula legitimately has no `sha256`, and `verifyHomebrew` wrongly requires them. The single-match regex is also weak (only checks the first url/sha256 of a 4-platform formula).

Let me confirm the artifacts the formula references exist in SHA256SUMS, so I write the right check:

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

repo="${DEADRECKON_REPO:-gregce/deadreckon}"
tag="${DEADRECKON_TAG:-v0.1.0-rc.1}"
asset="${DEADRECKON_INSTALLER_ASSET:-deadreckon-installer.sh}"
base_url="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/${tag}"
tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/deadreckon-install.$$"

die() {
  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

download() {
  url="$1"
  out="$2"
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$out"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -qO "$out" "$url"
  else
    die "install curl or wget, then rerun this installer"
  fi
}

cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}

trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM

(umask 077 && mkdir "$tmp") || die "could not create temp dir: $tmp"

printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: ${repo} ${tag}"
download "${base_url}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}" || die "could not download ${base_url}/${asset}"

if download "${base_url}/SHA256SUMS" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS"; then

tag="${DEADRECKON_TAG:-v0.1.0-rc.1}"
asset="${DEADRECKON_INSTALLER_ASSET:-deadreckon-installer.sh}"
base_url="https://github.com/${repo}/releases/download/${tag}"
tmp="${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/deadreckon-install.$$"

die() {
  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: $*" >&2
  exit 1
}

download() {
  url="$1"
  out="$2"
  if command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    curl -fsSL "$url" -o "$out"
  elif command -v wget >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    wget -qO "$out" "$url"
  else
    die "install curl or wget, then rerun this installer"
  fi
}

cleanup() {
  rm -rf "$tmp"
}

trap cleanup EXIT HUP INT TERM

(umask 077 && mkdir "$tmp") || die "could not create temp dir: $tmp"

printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: ${repo} ${tag}"
download "${base_url}/${asset}" "${tmp}/${asset}" || die "could not download ${base_url}/${asset}"

if download "${base_url}/SHA256SUMS" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS"; then
  if grep "  ${asset}\$" "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS" > "${tmp}/SHA256SUMS.${asset}"; then
    if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && shasum -a 256 -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      (cd "$tmp" && sha256sum -c "SHA256SUMS.${asset}") \
        || die "checksum verification failed for ${asset}"
    else
      printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: shasum/sha256sum not found; skipping checksum verification" >&2
    fi
  else
    printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: ${asset} was not listed in SHA256SUMS" >&2
  fi
else
  printf '%s\n' "deadreckon install: warning: could not download SHA256SUMS; skipping checksum verification" >&2
fi

sh "${tmp}/${asset}" "$@"

installed="${DEADRECKON_BIN:-${HOME}/.local/share/deadreckon/bin/deadreckon}"
if [ -x "$installed" ]; then
  bin="$installed"
elif command -v deadreckon >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  bin="deadreckon"
else
  bin="$installed"
fi

printf '\n%s\n' "deadreckon install: next"
printf '  %s\n' "${bin} doctor"
printf '  %s\n' "${bin} try"
printf '  %s\n' "${bin} start \"make a small safe change\""
=== site domain (astro.config) ===
import { defineConfig } from 'astro/config';

export default defineConfig({
  output: 'static',
  build: {
    format: 'directory',
  },
  site: 'https://deadreckon.sh',
  vite: {
    build: {
      assetsInlineLimit: 0,
    },
  },
});
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-04 22:57:08Z)**_

Two root causes found:
1. **`dist-plan` job has no `permissions:` block** → inherits top-level `contents: read`, so its `dist host --steps=create` **can't create a release** (no write access) — it exits 0 but does nothing, leaving `hosting: null`.
2. The publish job's `dist host --steps=upload,release,announce` never includes **`create`**, so it expects a release that was never made.

The fix matches cargo-dist's actual design: the `create` step belongs in the write-permissioned job. The publish job already has `contents: write`, so I'll have it create the release too — `create,upload,release,announce` in one shot:

Both questions now have evidence-backed answers — and the **full pipeline succeeded**: the signed, attested prerelease is live with all 21 assets.

## 1. macOS signing — ✅ Yes, your Apple config works (independently verified)

I downloaded the **actual published binary** and ran Apple's own tools on it:

```
Authority=Developer ID Application: Gregory Ceccarelli (4GRQMF5T5U)
Authority=Developer ID Certification Authority
Authority=Apple Root CA
TeamIdentifier=4GRQMF5T5U

codesign --verify --deep --strict:
  valid on disk
  satisfies its Designated Requirement
```

So the binary is genuinely signed with **your** Developer ID, the cert chains to Apple Root CA, and the signature is cryptographically valid. The pipeline's trust manifest agrees: `signed: true`, `signature_kind: "Developer ID Application"`, `notarized: true` for both `aarch64` and `x86_64`.

**Two outputs that look alarming but are normal for a CLI tool:**
- `spctl: rejected (the code is valid but does not seem to be an app)` — `spctl -a -t exec` assesses **.app bundles**; a bare CLI executable always gets this even when correctly signed. Note it still reports `origin=Developer ID Application: Gregory Ceccarelli`.
- `stapler: does not have a ticket stapled` — Apple's `stapler` **can't staple tickets to bare Mach-O executables** (only .app/.dmg/.pkg). The artifact *was* notarized (submitted + accepted by Apple's notary service → `notarized: true`); Gatekeeper just verifies that **online** on first launch instead of from a stapled ticket. This is expected for a tarball'd CLI, not a failure.

**Bottom line:** signing + notarization are working as configured.

## 2. Windows — builds and packages, but ⚠️ unsigned (rc) and runtime-unverified

The zip contains real binaries: `deadreckon.exe` (24 MB) + `dr-gate.exe` (2.6 MB), built natively on the `x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` runner. But two honest caveats:

- **Unsigned for the RC.** Every Windows signing step **skipped** (`Check Windows stable signing secrets`, `Decode Windows signing certificate`, `Sign and verify packaged Windows artifacts`) — Authenticode signing is gated to **stable** releases (`requires_windows_signing = official && stable`). So this rc `.exe` is unsigned → users hit **SmartScreen "Windows protected your PC"** warnings.
- **No evidence it actually runs.** The pipeline proves it **compiles and links**, nothing more. There is **no Windows runtime test anywhere** — `release-verify` only builds on Ubuntu, and the test suite never executes on Windows (it's macOS-coupled). Given DeadReckon leans on Unix-specific pieces (the `nix` crate for signals/process, sandbox backends), the Windows binary could build cleanly yet have real functional gaps at runtime. **We don't know it works on Windows** — only that it builds.

If Windows is a real target, the next step would be (a) wiring up the Windows signing secrets so a stable release signs, and (b) adding at least a smoke run (`deadreckon --version` / `deadreckon doctor`) on a `windows-latest` runner to prove the binary executes.

# Goal & Rider Author

A two-document pattern for briefing an autonomous coding agent
(Claude Code, Codex CLI, or any agentic harness) on the next round of
work. The **goal**
is the ≤4000-char spine: what to do, what to read first, the posture,
the verification, the stop conditions. The **rider** holds the
prescriptive detail: data schemas, phase plans, depth-test names,
verb signatures, error footers, out-of-scope lists.

The pattern's superpower is that the goal stays small enough to paste
into a Codex `/goal` or a Claude run prompt, while the rider can be
arbitrarily detailed without bloating the executor's working memory.

This skill is project-agnostic. It works for any codebase that has a
`docs/goals/` (or equivalent) directory, conventional commits, and
some form of AS-BUILT / architecture doc. Substitute the project's
own toolchain commands wherever the templates say
`<project's ... command>`.

## When to invoke

The user is about to start a new round of agentic work and wants
goal+rider files written into a project's `docs/goals/` directory.
Triggers include "draft a goal that addresses X", "write a goal+rider
for Y", "new goal for the next agentic turn", "rider for X".

## Pre-work — do not skip

Before drafting, gather context. Read in this order, skipping items
the project doesn't have:

1. **Project architecture doc** — `AS-BUILT-ARCHITECTURE.md`,
   `ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, or whatever the project
   uses. Look for a "what's shipped vs thin" section if one exists;
   it grounds the goal in reality.
2. **Prior goal+rider pairs** in `docs/goals/` (or wherever the
   project keeps them). Their invariants compose forward; do not
   duplicate verbatim. Skim the most recent two pairs to absorb
   voice and section conventions.
3. **Recent commits**: `git log --oneline -30 -- docs/goals/` and
   `git log --oneline -30`. Reveals delivery cadence and the
   conventional-commit format the project uses.
4. **Source code at HEAD** for any data structures, file paths, or
   function names you'll quote in the rider. Verify they match HEAD
   before citing.
5. **Research or pain-point reports** the project has (e.g.,
   unmet-needs, user-research, retro docs). They ground the
   ergonomics in real pain.

If you can't find prior pairs or an architecture doc, **ask the user**
for a pointer — don't invent one.

## Goal document recipe (≤4000 chars)

**Path:** `<project>/docs/goals/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>-<project-slug>-<topic>-goal.md`

The `<HHMM>` is the local 24-hour clock time when the file is created
(e.g., `1444` for 2:44 PM). It makes `ls docs/goals/` sort in true
authoring order rather than alphabetical by topic. When two pairs land
within the same minute, secondary alphabetical sort handles the tiebreak;
that's fine.

**Hard cap:** `wc -c <file>` must be ≤4000 (prior precedents: 3929–4112).
Re-check after every edit pass. Note the `-HHMM-` insert costs ~5 chars
per internal rider reference, so leave a small buffer when riders cross-cite.

**Skeleton** — fill each section, cut to fit:

```markdown
GOAL: <one-sentence headline>. <one paragraph: current pain → what the goal lands → headline word (Friendliness / Multi-agent / Self-documenting / Default mode / …)>.

**Read first.**

- `<absolute path to project architecture doc>` — substrate; one line.
- `<absolute path to the rider being written>` — schemas, signatures, depth tests.
- `<absolute paths to exemplars or research reports>` — grounding.
- Prior riders in `<absolute path to docs/goals/>` — invariants hold.

**Posture.** Stays `<tier>`. No `<struct>` schema changes (if applicable). No `git push`. Edits inside `<project root>`. Major architectural decisions → `<V1-CANDIDATES path>`.

<DOMAIN BODY — one or two of these, depending on the goal:>

**<N> modes / verbs / artifacts, auto-resolved.**

- **`<name>`** — <one line of behavior>.

**New verbs.**

- `<verb> <args>` — <one line>.

**Friendliness as a verifiable contract.**

- Auto-detect, don't ask (the obvious case is the default).
- Preflight + preview before any state change.
- Refuse with `try: <command>` lines.
- Rollback is one command.
- Lifecycle hints after every action.

**Phases.** Eleven (P1–P11) in the rider. Each: depth test first → implement → `<project's build+test+lint+fmt command>` green → conventional-commit → CHANGELOG. P11 adds a `<new section>` to the project architecture doc.

**Verification.**

- Commands green every commit; every rider depth test present and passing.
- <Smoke 1>: <verifiable command + assertion>.
- <Smoke 2>: <verifiable command + assertion>.
- No edits outside `<project>`. No `git push`. No schema changes.

**Stop when** verification passes, AS-BUILT updated, CHANGELOG has a "<Milestone name> (alpha)" section, committed locally.
```

**Trim priority when over budget:**

1. Drop parenthetical detail that's already in the rider.
2. Shorten Read-first descriptions to bare absolute paths.
3. Compress Posture to one or two lines.
4. Cut verification smoke bullets to two.
5. Drop cross-rider "do not preempt" notes; those live in the rider.

## Rider document recipe (no char cap; typically 10–35K)

**Path:** `<project>/docs/goals/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>-<project-slug>-<topic>-rider.md`

Use the **same** `<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>` prefix as the matching goal so
the pair sorts together. Author the goal first, then mirror its
timestamp on the rider — never split them across minutes.

**Skeleton:**

```markdown
# <project> — <Slug> Rider (<short framing>)

This rider holds the prescriptive constraints for the goal at
`<absolute path to goal>`. It supersedes nothing in prior riders
(<list dated rider filenames>) — their invariants still apply.
This rider adds <one-line summary of what's new>.

**All paths absolute.** Source `<project root>`, runtime `<runtime root>`.

## Posture (decided — do not redesign)

- **Maturity stays `<tier>`** (alpha / beta / stable; mirrors what
  the project calls the current milestone).
- **No `<struct>` schema changes** (if applicable). State lives in
  files at `<path>`.
- **<Other domain-specific invariants — be explicit>.**
- **No `git push`.** Phased local commits only.
- **No V1 / next-tier invention.** If a phase reveals a major
  architectural decision, log it in `<V1-CANDIDATES path>` (or
  equivalent) and continue.
- **Edits stay inside `<project root>`.**

## Data model (files, not fields)

<JSON schemas for any new file-based state. One block per file.
Inline-comment each field if the meaning isn't obvious.>

## <Algorithms / Mode resolution / Detection rules>

<Pseudocode for non-obvious logic. The rider IS the spec — match it
in the implementation.>

## Verb signatures

```
<verb> <args>
    [--flag]                  # description
    [--other-flag <type>]     # description
```

For each verb: refusal cases table.

## Phases (eleven)

Each phase: write the named depth test(s) **first** and watch them
fail; implement; green on
`<project's build+test+lint+fmt command, green on each commit>`;
conventional-commit local commit; one-line CHANGELOG entry.

### P1 — <name>

- <bulleted prescriptions>

Depth tests (in `<test path>`):
- `snake_case_descriptive_name_that_would_have_caught_the_thin_behavior`
- `another_named_test`

### P2 — <name>

...

### P11 — Architecture doc update + CHANGELOG (doc only; no depth test)

- Insert a new top-level section into `<architecture doc path>`:
  ```
  ## NN. <Section title>

  NN.1 <subsection>
  NN.2 <subsection>
  ...
  ```
- If the architecture doc has a "what's shipped vs thin" section,
  update it:
  - Add to the "shipped" side: <items this rider lands>.
  - Note explicitly whether this rider closes prior thin items or
    only adds capability.
- Append to `<CHANGELOG path>`:
  ```
  ## <Milestone name> (<tier>) — <YYYY-MM-DD>

  - <bullet>
  ```

## Integration matrix (when multi-mode or multi-verb)

| <axis> | <feature 1> | <feature 2> | … |
|---|---|---|---|
| ... | ... | ... | ... |

## Error-footer canonical pairs

| Error | `try:` |
|---|---|
| `<terse description>` | `<one specific command or fix>` |

(Parameterized over a depth test so every error case is exercised.)

## Config additions (when relevant)

```toml
[defaults]
<new_knob> = "<default>"
```

- <one bullet per V1-candidate scope item>
- <…>

Tier 1 (utility, free): <list with one-line justification each>.
Tier 2 (architectural, log to `DEPENDENCIES.md`): <list or "none expected">.
Tier 3 (blocked): same blocks as prior riders.

## Engineering invariants (do not violate)

- **No `<struct>` schema changes.**
- **One depth test before each phase implementation.** A phase whose
  tests were never red is suspect.
- **<Domain-specific invariants>.**
- **No silent expansion.** Anything beyond P1–P11 goes into
  `V1-CANDIDATES.md`.
- **<Spec-pinning invariants>**: e.g., "the preview block format is
  depth-tested; changing whitespace changes the spec."

## Process invariants

- Phased local commits only. No `git push`.
- Each phase ends with the relevant depth tests passing and a
  CHANGELOG entry naming the SHA.
- After P11, optionally capture a demo (asciinema cast / screenshots /
  short video) under `<project>/<demo-path>`. Skip when the change
  isn't user-visible.
- If a phase reveals a V1-architecture decision, stop and log it in
  `V1-CANDIDATES.md`; do not silently expand scope.
```

## Discipline checklist (the invariants this skill carries)

1. **Two documents, two budgets.** Goal ≤4000 chars; rider unbounded.
   Run `wc -c` on the goal before declaring done.
2. **Timestamped filenames.** Both goal and rider are named
   `<YYYY-MM-DD>-<HHMM>-<project-slug>-<topic>-{goal,rider}.md`. The
   `<HHMM>` is the local 24-hour authoring time (e.g., `1444`). The
   pair shares one timestamp so they sort together; never split them
   across minutes. This makes `ls docs/goals/` chronological.
3. **Phased local commits only.** Never tell the executor to `git push`.
4. **Files-not-fields.** When the project has persistent state
   structs (DB schema, config struct, state machine), durable
   per-feature state should live in files inside the working tree
   (`<some>/<name>.json`) rather than as new struct fields. Schema
   changes are last-resort. Skip this invariant for projects without
   such structs.
5. **Depth tests first.** Each phase's named tests are written and
   watched fail before implementation. List them by name in the rider
   so a `grep -c '^    fn '` enforces presence.
6. **Architecture-doc discipline.** P11 always updates whatever
   architecture / as-built doc the project keeps, plus CHANGELOG. If
   there's a "what's shipped vs thin" section, the thin list is
   honest — only remove items the rider actually closes.
7. **V1 candidates.** Anything out of scope goes to
   `docs/V1-CANDIDATES.md`, not silently expanded scope.
8. **Conventional commits, scoped.** `docs(goals): add <topic> goal+rider`
   for the goal-rider commit itself. `feat(<scope>):` / `fix(<scope>):`
   / `chore(<scope>):` for execution commits.
9. **Frontmatter mirrors the project's own convention** for any
   human-readable artifacts. If the project has prior impl docs
   under `docs/implementation/` or similar, match their frontmatter
   shape (Date / Status / Commit span / Owner / …). If not, propose
   a minimal frontmatter and stick to it across riders.
10. **Friendliness is verifiable.** Auto-detect, preflight + preview,
    refuse with `try: <command>`, one-command rollback, lifecycle
    hints. Each is exercised by a depth test.
11. **Judgment in markdown, invariants in code.** When the project
    has a skill / prompt-template / config-driven prompt mechanism,
    prefer that over a hardcoded const so users can tune voice or
    behavior without a rebuild. (Project-specific; skip if no such
    mechanism exists.)

## Anti-patterns to avoid

- Inventing V1 architecture inside an alpha rider.
- Schema changes without a stated strong reason.
- Backwards-compatibility shims for code that no caller uses.
- Comments explaining WHAT the code does (well-named identifiers
  already do that).
- Half-finished implementations ("we'll finish in P12").
- Duplicating invariants from prior riders verbatim — just say
  "invariants hold" and reference them.
- Depth tests written after implementation.
- Stop conditions that don't tie to verification ("stop when it
  feels done" is not a stop condition).
- Inventing CLI verbs not in the goal.
- Adding emojis to written artifacts.
- "TODO: maybe add X" lines — either it's in scope (P-numbered) or
  it's a V1 candidate.

## Standard 11-phase shape

A typical rider has these phases (adapt the names; eleven is a target,
not a hard rule — fewer or more is fine if the structure earns it):

- **P1**: Data model / plumbing — new module / file path / frontmatter
  helpers. No behavior change yet.
- **P2–P3**: Foundation — new primitive types, base mechanism.
- **P4–P8**: Feature implementation — one phase per major slice; each
  phase ships with end-to-end depth tests.
- **P9**: Integration with prior verbs / modes / state machines.
- **P10**: Cross-cutting friendliness pass — flags like `--quiet` /
  `--plain`, error-footer routing, post-action hints, help-text
  grouping.
- **P11**: Architecture-doc update + CHANGELOG + (optional) demo
  capture (doc-only; no depth test).

## Commit message for the goal-rider pair itself

```
docs(goals): add <topic> goal+rider (<one-line headline>)

<2–3 sentence summary: what the goal is for; what the rider prescribes;
what's explicitly out of scope. Mention named depth-test discipline,
files-not-fields posture (if applicable), V1 invention guard.>
```

Add the project's standard `Co-Authored-By:` footer if it uses one.

## Validation steps (run before declaring done)

```bash
PROJECT=<absolute path to project root>
DATE=$(date +%Y-%m-%d)
HHMM=$(date +%H%M)
PROJECT_SLUG=<short project name>
TOPIC=<short topic slug>
GOAL=$PROJECT/docs/goals/$DATE-$HHMM-$PROJECT_SLUG-$TOPIC-goal.md
RIDER=$PROJECT/docs/goals/$DATE-$HHMM-$PROJECT_SLUG-$TOPIC-rider.md

# 1. Goal must be under 4000 chars
wc -c "$GOAL"   # expect ≤4000

# 2. Rider must have ≥11 phase headers
grep -c '^### P[0-9]' "$RIDER"   # expect = 11

# 3. Rider must have the standard top-level sections
for section in "Posture" "Phases" "Out of scope" "Dependencies" \
               "Engineering invariants" "Process invariants"; do
  grep -q "^## $section" "$RIDER" || echo "MISSING: $section"
done

# 4. Both files cite each other's absolute paths
grep -F "$RIDER" "$GOAL"  || echo "goal does not reference rider"
grep -F "$GOAL"  "$RIDER" || echo "rider does not reference goal"

# 5. Stage and commit
cd "$PROJECT" && git add "$GOAL" "$RIDER" && git status
```

# DeadReckon - Release Trust Rider (signed artifacts, provenance, fail-closed publishing)

This rider holds the prescriptive constraints for the goal at `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-06-01-1523-deadreckon-release-trust-goal.md`. It supersedes nothing in the 2026-05-11 distribution rider; that rider made DeadReckon installable and self-updatable. This rider hardens the official release path so published artifacts are complete, signed where the platform supports it, provenance-backed, and refused when trust material is missing.

**All paths absolute.** Source root is `/Users/gdc/deadreckon`. Runtime state under `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon` is not part of this goal. Release artifacts are created by CI under `target/distrib` and by local tests under tempdirs only.

## Posture (decided - do not redesign)

- **Maturity stays production-release track.** This is release trust hardening, not a new install channel or CLI UX redesign.
- **No DeadReckon durable runtime schema changes.** Do not change `PipelineState`, plans, campaigns, chains, library artifacts, run markers, or install receipts unless an existing release script already owns that file.
- **Official releases fail closed.** On the canonical repository, RC and stable tags must not publish if required signing/provenance/checksum steps fail or required secrets are absent.
- **Forks and PRs remain usable.** Pull requests, branches, and forked repos can run `dist plan` and non-publishing checks without Apple/npm/Homebrew/Windows secrets.
- **No agent-driven publishing.** The agent must not run `git tag`, `git push`, `gh release upload`, `npm publish`, or Homebrew tap pushes outside tests/dry-runs.
- **No new package manager channel.** Stay with cargo-dist installers, GitHub Releases, Homebrew, npm wrapper/platform packages, and the existing update channel model.
- **No secret material in git.** Docs may name secret keys and commands, but not actual values, certificates, passwords, or team identifiers.
- **Edits stay inside `/Users/gdc/deadreckon`.**

## Current baseline and gaps

Current files to inspect:

- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.github/workflows/release.yml`
  - Builds five cargo-dist targets.
  - Runs macOS codesign/notarytool before `dist build`.
  - Skips macOS signing with warnings if Apple secrets are missing.
  - Publishes GitHub Release, Homebrew formula, and npm packages on any tag.
- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/.github/workflows/publish-npm.yml`
  - Uses `NPM_TOKEN`.
  - Repackages GitHub release artifacts into wrapper/platform packages.

- `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/dist-workspace.toml`

  - Names Apple/npm/Homebrew secrets and says the operator pushes a tag.
  - Does not yet define RC vs stable behavior, fail-closed policy, provenance, or exact Apple Developer ID setup steps.

Important gap: signing before `dist build` is suspicious. If `dist build` rebuilds the binary after the manual signing step, the uploaded artifact may not be the signed binary. The implementation must prove the artifact inside each macOS archive is signed after packaging, or move signing to a position that signs the exact artifact contents.

This rider holds the prescriptive constraints for the goal at `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/docs/goals/2026-06-04-1951-deadreckon-release-trust-closure-goal.md`. It supersedes nothing in the parent Release Trust rider (`2026-06-01-1523-deadreckon-release-trust-rider.md`) or the distribution rider (`2026-05-11-2343-deadreckon-distribute-rider.md`); their invariants still apply. This rider closes the three loose ends that surfaced when the pipeline first published a real artifact (`v0.1.0-rc.1`): the test suite never ran in CI, the Windows artifact is unproven, and the `gdc`→`gregce` re-home is partial.

**All paths absolute.** Source root is `/Users/gdc/deadreckon`. Runtime state under `/Users/gdc/.deadreckon` is not part of this goal. CI artifacts live under `target/distrib`; local tests use tempdirs only.

## Posture (decided — do not redesign)

- **Maturity stays production-release track.** Hardening and CI reclamation, not a new install channel or CLI UX redesign.
- **Canonical repository is `gregce/deadreckon`.** That is where `v0.1.0-rc.1` published; `OFFICIAL_REPO` in `release-trust.mjs` already says `gregce/deadreckon`. The re-home completes to it. Do not reintroduce `gdc/deadreckon` except as historical references in CHANGELOG/runbook prose.
- **No DeadReckon durable runtime schema changes.** Do not change `PipelineState`, plans, campaigns, chains, library artifacts, run markers, or install receipts. Path/home *resolution* may change; the persisted shapes may not.
- **Official releases stay fail-closed.** Stable Windows must not publish unsigned; missing Authenticode secrets block stable Windows artifacts, never silently ship them.
- **Forks and PRs remain usable.** The new test CI runs without any release secret. Windows smoke needs no signing secret.
- **No agent-driven publishing or signing.** The agent must not run `git tag`, `git push`, `gh release upload`, `npm publish`, Homebrew tap pushes, or real Authenticode signing outside tests/dry-runs.

## Portability rules (the spec for "machine-coupled")

- **Home resolution.** A shipped default that points at a home directory must resolve at runtime from, in order: an explicit env override (e.g. `DEADRECKON_HOME`), then the OS home (`std::env::var_os("HOME")` / `dirs`-style), then a documented fallback. No absolute `/Users/<name>` literal may remain in shipped `src/`.
- **Source root.** `SOURCE_ROOT` is a development convenience; if it must stay, derive it (e.g. `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`-relative or env) rather than hardcoding one machine. If nothing in shipped code paths reads it at runtime, move it behind `#[cfg(test)]` or delete it.
- **PTY tests.** Replace direct `Command::new("script")` BSD-syntax invocations with one shared helper that either (a) uses a portable pty crate, or (b) dispatches per-OS (`#[cfg(target_os = ...)]`) to the correct `script` syntax (macOS `script -q /dev/null cmd ...` vs Linux `script -qec "cmd" /dev/null`). _**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 00:19:53Z)**_

Here's the honest picture. "Proving Windows runs" is a ladder, and the rung you stop at determines what you've actually proven. The codebase already has `cfg(windows)`/`cfg(unix)` splits (`lock.rs`, `sleep.rs`, `notify.rs`, `sandbox`, `doctor`, `main.rs`), so it's *Windows-aware* at compile time — but that says nothing about runtime.

## The proof ladder

| Rung | Command | Proves | Strength |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0. Builds | `cargo build --release` on windows-msvc | links, no compile-time cfg gaps | ⬜ have it; proves nothing at runtime |
| 1. Loads | `deadreckon --version` | binary loads, no missing DLL, runtime inits, arg-parse works | weak |
| 2. Introspects | `deadreckon doctor` | env detection runs without panicking on Windows paths/process APIs | weak-medium |
| 3. **Exercises the gate** | `deadreckon run "hello" --smoke --sandbox none` | the **whole harness loop + dr-gate watchdog signing** works end-to-end against a faked provider, no sandbox | **this is the real bar** |
| 4. Suite | `cargo test --workspace` on windows-latest | broad correctness | strongest, biggest effort |

**Rung 3 is the bar that matters**, and here's why: DeadReckon's entire value prop is "a separate watchdog process holds a secret the agent can't read and signs the result." That mechanism — `dr-gate` as a separate process, the secret handoff, the signature verification — is exactly the kind of thing that's quietly Unix-coupled (process spawning, IPC, signal handling, `/tmp`-style paths). `--version` and `doctor` can both pass while `dr-gate` is completely broken on Windows. Only a real `run` that completes and produces an **accepted, signed verdict** proves the product actually works there.

So the assertion isn't "exit 0" — it's "the smoke run reached an accepted state with a valid gate signature." That's checkable from the run's exit code + the verdict in its output/state.

## Concrete CI job

```yaml
windows-smoke:
  runs-on: windows-latest
  steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v4
    - run: rustup target add x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
    - run: cargo build --release --workspace --locked
    - name: Binary loads and introspects
      run: |
        ./target/release/deadreckon.exe --version
        ./target/release/deadreckon.exe doctor
    - name: Gate runs end-to-end (the real proof)
      run: ./target/release/deadreckon.exe run "hello" --smoke --sandbox none
      # fail closed: non-zero exit, or a run that didn't reach an accepted/signed verdict, fails the job
```

## Build-from-source vs. the published artifact

Two different things worth proving, both cheap:
- **Build + smoke on `windows-latest`** (above) — fast per-push signal that *current code* runs.
- **Download the published `deadreckon-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip` and smoke *that*** — proves the **exact bytes users get** run after packaging (and, once stable signing lands, after Authenticode signing didn't corrupt anything). This is a post-release job.

## What a green job does *not* prove

Be honest about the ceiling:
- **CI runner ≠ a clean user machine.** `windows-latest` has the MSVC runtime + dev tooling preinstalled. A real user's machine may lack the VC++ redistributable → "missing DLL." Truly proving that needs a clean Windows VM/container, which CI runners aren't.
- **`--sandbox none` skips the most Unix-coupled subsystem.** So a green smoke proves the *core loop + gate* work, not that sandboxing works on Windows (it almost certainly doesn't — document that).
- **Smoke ≠ suite.** It exercises one path. Rung 4 (the full suite on Windows) is the real correctness bar, and it needs the same portability work the Linux suite needs, plus Windows path/PTY specifics.

## This sharpens the goal I just wrote

The rider's **P9 currently stops at rung 1–2** (`--version` / `doctor`). Given the above, that's too weak — it could go green while the gate is broken. I'd strengthen P9 to require the **rung-3 gate smoke** and assert an accepted+signed verdict, and add the published-artifact smoke as the post-release check.

Want me to update P9 in the rider to that stronger bar? It's a small edit and makes the "prove Windows runs" phase actually prove it.

304	            vec![

307	                ("supported narrative targets", "run, plan, plan child"),
308	            ],
309	        ),
310	        vec![("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
311	        vec![
312	            ("Secondary", "deadreckon attach <run-id> --view narrative"),
313	            ("Secondary", "deadreckon attach <plan-id> --view narrative"),
314	        ],
315	    )
316	    .expect("chain narrative refusal surface must be valid")

318	
319	async fn attach_campaign_tui(
320	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
321	    mut state: commands::campaign::CampaignAttachState,
322	    show_hints: bool,
323	    initial_view: AttachViewMode,
324	    initial_visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
325	    narrative_config: NarrativeAttachConfig,
326	) -> Result<()> {
327	    enable_raw_mode()?;
328	    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
329	    execute!(stdout, EnterAlternateScreen, EnableMouseCapture)?;
330	    let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout);
331	    let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
332	    let mut feed = commands::campaign::CampaignEventFeed::new(
333	        paths.clone(),
334	        state.campaign_dir.clone(),
335	        state.campaign.campaign_id.clone(),
336	    );
337	
338	    let result = loop {
339	        let mut tick = AttachTickTiming::new(AttachSurface::Campaign, AttachTickBudget::default());
340	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
341	        let events = feed.refresh(Duration::ZERO).await;
342	        state.apply_feed_events(events);
343	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::EventFeed, stage_started);
344	
345	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
346	        if let Err(error) = state.refresh(paths) {
347	            state
348	                .feed
349	                .push_back(commands::campaign::CampaignFeedEvent::Warning {
350	                    message: format!("campaign refresh failed: {error}"),
351	                });
352	        }
353	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::LoadState, stage_started);
354	
355	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
356	        terminal.draw(|frame| render_campaign_attach(frame, &state))?;
357	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::Draw, stage_started);
358	
359	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
360	        let input_ready = event::poll(Duration::from_millis(250))?;
361	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::InputPoll, stage_started);
362	        drop(tick.slow_sync_stages());
363	        drop(tick.slow_stage_labels());
364	        let _ = tick.frame_exceeded();
365	
366	        if input_ready && let Event::Key(key) = event::read()? {
367	            match handle_campaign_key(&mut state, key) {
368	                CampaignAttachKeyAction::None | CampaignAttachKeyAction::Refresh => {}
369	                CampaignAttachKeyAction::Back | CampaignAttachKeyAction::Quit => break Ok(()),
370	                CampaignAttachKeyAction::DrillInto { sub_id, plan_id } => {
371	                    if load_plan(paths, &plan_id).is_err() {
372	                        state
373	                            .feed
374	                            .push_back(commands::campaign::CampaignFeedEvent::Warning {
375	                                message: format!("sub-plan {sub_id} unavailable: {plan_id}"),
376	                            });
377	                        continue;
378	                    }
379	                    suspend_tui(&mut terminal)?;
380	                    let parent_campaign = AttachCampaignParent {
381	                        campaign_id: state.campaign.campaign_id.clone(),
382	                        sub_id,
383	                    };
384	                    let child_result = attach_plan_tui(
385	                        paths,
386	                        &plan_id,
387	                        show_hints,
388	                        initial_view,
389	                        initial_visual,
390	                        narrative_config.clone(),
391	                        Some(parent_campaign),
392	                    )
393	                    .await;
394	                    if let Err(err) = &child_result {
395	                        print_error(err);
396	                        let _ = prompt::open("press Enter to return to campaign attach...", None);
397	                    }
398	                    resume_tui(&mut terminal)?;
399	                }
400	            }
401	        }
402	    };
403	
404	    disable_raw_mode()?;
405	    execute!(
406	        terminal.backend_mut(),
407	        DisableMouseCapture,
408	        LeaveAlternateScreen
409	    )?;
410	    terminal.show_cursor()?;
411	    result
412	}
413	
414	async fn attach_plan_tui(
415	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
416	    plan_id: &str,
417	    show_hints: bool,
418	    initial_view: AttachViewMode,
419	    initial_visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
420	    narrative_config: NarrativeAttachConfig,
421	    parent_campaign: Option<AttachCampaignParent>,
422	) -> Result<()> {
423	    enable_raw_mode()?;
424	    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
425	    execute!(stdout, EnterAlternateScreen, EnableMouseCapture)?;
426	    let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout);
427	    let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
428	    let mut selected = 0_usize;
429	    let mut plan = load_plan(paths, plan_id)?;
430	    let mut messages: Vec<PlanMessage>;
431	    let mut plan_events = Vec::<PlanEvent>::new();
432	    let mut feed_events = Vec::<PlanFeedEvent>::new();
433	    let mut feed = PlanEventBus::file_tail(paths.clone(), plan_id.to_string());
434	    let mut view = initial_view;
435	    let mut visual = initial_visual;
436	    let mut narrative_notice = None;
437	    let mut quiet_tracker = NarrativeQuietRefreshTracker::new(Utc::now());
438	    let mut narrative_refresh_job: Option<AttachPlanNarrativeRefreshJob> = None;
439	    let mut narrative_projection_cache = AttachNarrativeProjectionCache::default();
440	
441	    let result = loop {
442	        let mut tick = AttachTickTiming::new(AttachSurface::Plan, AttachTickBudget::default());
443	        let now = Utc::now();
444	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
445	        let new_feed_events = feed.refresh(Duration::ZERO).await;
446	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::EventFeed, stage_started);
447	        let event_refresh = plan_narrative_refresh_trigger(&new_feed_events);
448	        quiet_tracker.observe_event_trigger(event_refresh, now);
449	        for event in new_feed_events {
450	            match event {
451	                PlanFeedEvent::Plan { event } => {
452	                    plan_events.push(event.clone());
453	                    feed_events.push(PlanFeedEvent::Plan { event });
454	                }
455	                PlanFeedEvent::Snapshot { plan: snapshot } => {
456	                    plan = (*snapshot).clone();
457	                    feed_events.push(PlanFeedEvent::Snapshot { plan: snapshot });
458	                }
459	                other => feed_events.push(other),
460	            }
461	        }
462	        if plan_events.len() > 1_000 {
463	            let drain = plan_events.len().saturating_sub(1_000);
464	            plan_events.drain(0..drain);
465	        }
466	        if feed_events.len() > 1_000 {
467	            let drain = feed_events.len().saturating_sub(1_000);
468	            feed_events.drain(0..drain);
469	        }
470	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
471	        messages = read_plan_messages(paths, plan_id).unwrap_or_default();
472	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::PlanMessages, stage_started);
473	        if let Some(notice) = poll_plan_narrative_refresh_job(&mut narrative_refresh_job).await {
474	            narrative_projection_cache.invalidate();
475	            narrative_notice = Some(notice);
476	        }
477	        if selected >= plan.tasks.len() {
478	            selected = plan.tasks.len().saturating_sub(1);
479	        }
480	        let auto_refresh = event_refresh.or_else(|| {
481	            if view.is_narrative() {
482	                quiet_tracker.maybe_trigger(
483	                    plan.status == PlanStatus::Forked,
484	                    narrative::NarrativeCadence::default().quiet_seconds,
485	                    now,
486	                )
487	            } else {
488	                None
489	            }
490	        });
491	        if let Some(kind) = auto_refresh
492	            && view.is_narrative()
493	        {
494	            let stage_started = Instant::now();
495	            let refresh_input = PlanNarrativeRefreshInput {
496	                paths,
497	                plan: &plan,
498	                messages: &messages,
499	                plan_events: &plan_events,
500	                feed_events: &feed_events,
501	                selected,
502	                config: &narrative_config,
503	            };
504	            narrative_notice = Some(start_or_coalesce_plan_narrative_refresh_job(
505	                &mut narrative_refresh_job,
506	                plan_narrative_refresh_request(&refresh_input, kind),
507	                now,
508	            ));
509	            tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::ProviderNarrativeRefresh, stage_started);
510	        }
511	        let narrative_projection = if view.is_narrative() {
512	            let input = narrative::PlanNarrativeInput {
513	                paths,
514	                plan: &plan,
515	                messages: &messages,
516	                plan_events: &plan_events,
517	                feed_events: &feed_events,
518	                selected,
519	            };
520	            narrative_projection_cache
521	                .refresh_plan(&input)
522	                .or_else(|_| Ok::<_, CliError>(narrative::build_plan_projection(&input)))
523	                .ok()
524	        } else {
525	            None
526	        };
527	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
528	        terminal.draw(|frame| {
529	            render_plan_attach(
530	                frame,
531	                paths,
532	                &plan,
533	                &PlanAttachRenderState {
534	                    messages: &messages,
535	                    plan_events: &plan_events,
536	                    feed_events: &feed_events,
537	                    selected,
538	                    show_hints,
539	                    view,
540	                    visual,
541	                    campaign_parent: parent_campaign.as_ref(),
542	                    narrative_notice: narrative_notice.as_deref(),
543	                    narrative_projection: narrative_projection.as_ref(),
544	                },
545	            )
546	        })?;
547	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::Draw, stage_started);
548	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
549	        let input_ready = event::poll(Duration::from_millis(250))?;
550	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::InputPoll, stage_started);
551	        drop(tick.slow_sync_stages());
552	        drop(tick.slow_stage_labels());
553	        let _ = tick.frame_exceeded();
554	        if input_ready {
555	            match event::read()? {
556	                Event::Key(key) if attach_should_quit(key) => break Ok(()),
557	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Char('n') && key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
558	                    view = toggle_attach_view(view);
559	                }
560	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Char('v') && key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
561	                    visual = visual.next();
562	                }
563	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Char('r') && key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
564	                    view = AttachViewMode::Narrative;
565	                    let stage_started = Instant::now();
566	                    let refresh_input = PlanNarrativeRefreshInput {
567	                        paths,
568	                        plan: &plan,
569	                        messages: &messages,
570	                        plan_events: &plan_events,
571	                        feed_events: &feed_events,
572	                        selected,
573	                        config: &narrative_config,
574	                    };
575	                    narrative_notice = Some(start_or_coalesce_plan_narrative_refresh_job(
576	                        &mut narrative_refresh_job,
577	                        plan_narrative_refresh_request(
578	                            &refresh_input,
579	                            NarrativeRefreshKind::Manual,
580	                        ),
581	                        Utc::now(),
582	                    ));
583	                    tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::ProviderNarrativeRefresh, stage_started);
584	                    let stage_started = Instant::now();
585	                    terminal.draw(|frame| {
586	                        render_plan_attach(
587	                            frame,
588	                            paths,
589	                            &plan,
590	                            &PlanAttachRenderState {
591	                                messages: &messages,
592	                                plan_events: &plan_events,
593	                                feed_events: &feed_events,
594	                                selected,
595	                                show_hints,
596	                                view,
597	                                visual,
598	                                campaign_parent: parent_campaign.as_ref(),
599	                                narrative_notice: narrative_notice.as_deref(),
600	                                narrative_projection: narrative_projection.as_ref(),
601	                            },
602	                        )
603	                    })?;
604	                    tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::Draw, stage_started);
605	                }
606	                Event::Key(key)
607	                    if matches!(
608	                        key.code,
609	                        KeyCode::Right | KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Tab | KeyCode::Char('j')
610	                    ) =>
611	                {
612	                    selected = (selected + 1).min(plan.tasks.len().saturating_sub(1));
613	                }
614	                Event::Key(key)
615	                    if matches!(key.code, KeyCode::Left | KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k')) =>
616	                {
617	                    selected = selected.saturating_sub(1);
618	                }
619	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Enter => {
620	                    if let Some(run_id) = plan
621	                        .tasks
622	                        .get(selected)
623	                        .and_then(|task| task.child_run_id.as_deref())
624	                    {
625	                        if load_run(paths, run_id).is_err() {
626	                            continue;
627	                        }
628	                        let parent_plan = plan.tasks.get(selected).map(|task| AttachParentPlan {
629	                            plan_id: plan.plan_id.clone(),
630	                            task_id: task.task_id.clone(),
631	                            campaign_parent: parent_campaign.clone(),
632	                        });
633	                        if cancel_plan_narrative_refresh_job(&mut narrative_refresh_job) {
634	                            narrative_notice = Some(
635	                                "plan refresh cancelled while opening child attach".to_string(),
636	                            );
637	                        }
638	                        suspend_tui(&mut terminal)?;
639	                        let child_result = attach_tui_with_parent(
640	                            paths,
641	                            run_id,
642	                            show_hints,
643	                            parent_plan,
644	                            view,
645	                            visual,
646	                            narrative_config.clone(),
647	                        )
648	                        .await;
649	                        if let Err(err) = &child_result {
650	                            print_error(err);
651	                            let _ = prompt::open("press Enter to return to plan attach...", None);
652	                        }
653	                        resume_tui(&mut terminal)?;
654	                    }
655	                }
656	                _ => {}
657	            }
658	        }
659	    };
660	
661	    cancel_plan_narrative_refresh_job(&mut narrative_refresh_job);
662	    disable_raw_mode()?;
663	    execute!(
664	        terminal.backend_mut(),
665	        DisableMouseCapture,
666	        LeaveAlternateScreen
667	    )?;
668	    terminal.show_cursor()?;
669	    result
670	}
671	
672	async fn attach_tui(
673	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
674	    run_id: &str,
675	    show_completion_actions: bool,
676	    initial_view: AttachViewMode,
677	    initial_visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
678	    narrative_config: NarrativeAttachConfig,
679	) -> Result<()> {
680	    attach_tui_with_parent(
681	        paths,
682	        run_id,
683	        show_completion_actions,
684	        None,
685	        initial_view,
686	        initial_visual,
687	        narrative_config,
688	    )
689	    .await
690	}
691	
692	async fn attach_tui_with_parent(
693	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
694	    run_id: &str,
695	    show_completion_actions: bool,
696	    parent_plan: Option<AttachParentPlan>,
697	    initial_view: AttachViewMode,
698	    initial_visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
699	    narrative_config: NarrativeAttachConfig,
700	) -> Result<()> {
701	    let initial_state = load_run(paths, run_id)?;
702	    let mut event_feed =
703	        tui_events::TuiEventFeed::file_tail(initial_state.run_root.join(RUN_EVENTS_JSONL));
704	    let mut events = event_feed.refresh(std::time::Duration::ZERO).await?;
705	    enable_raw_mode()?;
706	    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
707	    execute!(stdout, EnterAlternateScreen, EnableMouseCapture)?;
708	    let backend = CrosstermBackend::new(stdout);
709	    let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend)?;
710	    let mut tui_state = AttachTuiState {
711	        show_completion_actions,
712	        parent_plan,
713	        view: initial_view,
714	        visual: initial_visual,
715	        ..AttachTuiState::default()
716	    };
717	    let mut quiet_tracker = NarrativeQuietRefreshTracker::new(Utc::now());
718	    let mut acceptance_tracker = NarrativeAcceptanceRefreshTracker::default();
719	    let mut narrative_refresh_job: Option<AttachRunNarrativeRefreshJob> = None;
720	    let mut spend_tail =
721	        AttachJsonlTail::<SpendRecord>::new(initial_state.run_root.join("spend.jsonl"));
722	    let mut trace_tail =
723	        AttachJsonlTail::<TraceRecord>::new(initial_state.run_root.join("traces.jsonl"));
724	    let mut provider_activity_cache = AttachProviderActivityCache::new(&initial_state);
725	    let mut narrative_projection_cache = AttachNarrativeProjectionCache::default();
726	
727	    let result = loop {
728	        let mut tick = AttachTickTiming::new(AttachSurface::Run, AttachTickBudget::default());
729	        let now = Utc::now();
730	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
731	        let state = load_run(paths, run_id)?;
732	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::LoadState, stage_started);
733	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
734	        spend_tail.reset_to_path(state.run_root.join("spend.jsonl"));
735	        trace_tail.reset_to_path(state.run_root.join("traces.jsonl"));
736	        let spend = spend_tail.refresh()?;
737	        let traces = trace_tail.refresh()?;
738	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::ReadJsonl, stage_started);
739	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
740	        let new_events = event_feed.refresh(std::time::Duration::ZERO).await?;
741	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::EventFeed, stage_started);
742	        let run_event_refresh = run_narrative_refresh_trigger(&new_events);
743	        events.extend(new_events);
744	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
745	        let provider_activity = provider_activity_cache.refresh(&state);
746	        let live = collect_attach_live_with_provider_activity(&state, provider_activity);
747	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::LiveCollect, stage_started);
748	        let event_refresh =
749	            run_event_refresh.or_else(|| acceptance_tracker.observe(&live.acceptance));
750	        quiet_tracker.observe_event_trigger(event_refresh, now);
751	        if let Some(notice) = poll_run_narrative_refresh_job(&mut narrative_refresh_job).await {
752	            narrative_projection_cache.invalidate();
753	            tui_state.record_narrative_refresh(notice);
754	        }
755	        tui_state.narrative_projection = if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
756	            let input = RunNarrativeRenderInput {
757	                state: &state,
758	                spend,
759	                traces,
760	                events: &events,
761	                live: &live,
762	                tui_state: &tui_state,
763	            };
764	            narrative_projection_cache
765	                .refresh_run(&input)
766	                .or_else(|_| Ok::<_, CliError>(build_run_narrative_projection(&input)))
767	                .ok()
768	        } else {
769	            None
770	        };
771	        let terminal_size = terminal.size()?;
772	        let terminal_area =
773	            ratatui::layout::Rect::new(0, 0, terminal_size.width, terminal_size.height);
774	        let panel_layout = attach_panel_layout(terminal_area);
775	        let panel_counts = attach_panel_counts(&state, spend, traces, &events, &live, &tui_state);
776	        tui_state.clamp(panel_counts, panel_layout.rows);
777	        let auto_refresh = event_refresh.or_else(|| {
778	            if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
779	                quiet_tracker.maybe_trigger(
780	                    state.status == RunStatus::Executing,
781	                    narrative::NarrativeCadence::default().quiet_seconds,
782	                    now,
783	                )
784	            } else {
785	                None
786	            }
787	        });
788	        if let Some(kind) = auto_refresh
789	            && tui_state.view.is_narrative()
790	        {
791	            let stage_started = Instant::now();
792	            let input = RunNarrativeRenderInput {
793	                state: &state,
794	                spend,
795	                traces,
796	                events: &events,
797	                live: &live,
798	                tui_state: &tui_state,
799	            };
800	            let notice = start_or_coalesce_run_narrative_refresh_job(
801	                &mut narrative_refresh_job,
802	                run_narrative_refresh_request(paths, &input, &narrative_config, kind),
803	                now,
804	            );
805	            tui_state.record_narrative_refresh(notice);
806	            tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::ProviderNarrativeRefresh, stage_started);
807	        }
808	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
809	        terminal.draw(|frame| {
810	            render_attach(frame, &state, spend, traces, &events, &live, &tui_state)
811	        })?;
812	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::Draw, stage_started);
813	
814	        let stage_started = Instant::now();
815	        let input_ready = event::poll(Duration::from_millis(200))?;
816	        tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::InputPoll, stage_started);
817	        drop(tick.slow_sync_stages());
818	        drop(tick.slow_stage_labels());
819	        let _ = tick.frame_exceeded();
820	        if input_ready {
821	            match event::read()? {
822	                Event::Key(key)
823	                    if tui_state.parent_plan.is_some() && attach_should_return_to_plan(key) =>
824	                {
825	                    break Ok(());
826	                }
827	                Event::Key(key) if attach_should_quit(key) => break Ok(()),
828	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Char('n') && key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
829	                    tui_state.toggle_view();
830	                }
831	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Char('v') && key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
832	                    tui_state.cycle_visual();
833	                }
834	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Char('r') && key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
835	                    let provider_stage_started = Instant::now();
836	                    let input = RunNarrativeRenderInput {
837	                        state: &state,
838	                        spend,
839	                        traces,
840	                        events: &events,
841	                        live: &live,
842	                        tui_state: &tui_state,
843	                    };
844	                    let notice = start_or_coalesce_run_narrative_refresh_job(
845	                        &mut narrative_refresh_job,
846	                        run_narrative_refresh_request(
847	                            paths,
848	                            &input,
849	                            &narrative_config,
850	                            NarrativeRefreshKind::Manual,
851	                        ),
852	                        Utc::now(),
853	                    );
854	                    tui_state.record_narrative_refresh(notice);
855	                    tick.record_since(
856	                        AttachLoopStage::ProviderNarrativeRefresh,
857	                        provider_stage_started,
858	                    );
859	                    let stage_started = Instant::now();
860	                    terminal.draw(|frame| {
861	                        render_attach(frame, &state, spend, traces, &events, &live, &tui_state)
862	                    })?;
863	                    tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::Draw, stage_started);
864	                }
865	                Event::Key(key)
866	                    if key.code == KeyCode::Char('c')
867	                        && key.modifiers.is_empty()
868	                        && read_chain_step_marker(&state.working_dir)?.is_some() =>
869	                {
870	                    if let Some(marker) = read_chain_step_marker(&state.working_dir)? {
871	                        suspend_tui(&mut terminal)?;
872	                        let action =
873	                            commands::chain::chain_attach_command(paths, &marker.chain_id, false);
874	                        if let Err(err) = &action {
875	                            print_error(err);
876	                        }
877	                        resume_tui(&mut terminal)?;
878	                    }
879	                }
880	                Event::Key(key)
881	                    if tui_state.show_completion_actions
882	                        && state.status == RunStatus::Completed =>
883	                {
884	                    if key.code == KeyCode::Char('d') && key.modifiers.is_empty() {
885	                        tui_state.toggle_docs();
886	                    } else if let Some(notice) =
887	                        handle_tui_completion_key(&mut terminal, paths, &state, key).await?
888	                    {
889	                        tui_state.record_post_action(notice);
890	                    } else {
891	                        tui_state.handle_key(key, panel_counts, panel_layout.rows);
892	                    }
893	                }
894	                Event::Key(key) => tui_state.handle_key(key, panel_counts, panel_layout.rows),
895	                Event::Mouse(mouse) => {
896	                    if let Some(panel) = panel_layout.panel_at(mouse.column, mouse.row) {
897	                        tui_state.focused_panel = panel;
898	                    }
899	                    match mouse.kind {
900	                        MouseEventKind::ScrollDown => {
901	                            tui_state.scroll_focused(3, panel_counts, panel_layout.rows)
902	                        }
903	                        MouseEventKind::ScrollUp => {
904	                            tui_state.scroll_focused(-3, panel_counts, panel_layout.rows)
905	                        }
906	                        _ => {}
907	                    }
908	                }
909	                _ => {}
910	            }
911	        }
912	    };
913	
914	    cancel_run_narrative_refresh_job(&mut narrative_refresh_job);
915	    disable_raw_mode()?;
916	    execute!(
917	        terminal.backend_mut(),
918	        DisableMouseCapture,
919	        LeaveAlternateScreen
920	    )?;
921	    terminal.show_cursor()?;
922	    result
923	}
924	
925	async fn handle_tui_completion_key(
926	    terminal: &mut Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>,
927	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
928	    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
929	    key: KeyEvent,
930	) -> Result<Option<AttachActionNotice>> {
931	    let action = match key.code {
932	        KeyCode::Char('m') => CompletionAction::Materialize,
933	        KeyCode::Char('e') => CompletionAction::Extend,
934	        KeyCode::Char('a') => CompletionAction::Apply,
935	        KeyCode::Char('b') => CompletionAction::Abandon,
936	        KeyCode::Char('d') => CompletionAction::Docs,
937	        KeyCode::Char('s') => CompletionAction::Show,
938	        _ => return Ok(None),
939	    };
940	
941	    suspend_tui(terminal)?;
942	    let action_result = match action {
943	        CompletionAction::Materialize => prompt_materialize_action(paths, state),
944	        CompletionAction::Extend => prompt_extend_action(state).await,
945	        CompletionAction::Apply => super::lifecycle::apply_command(
946	            state.run_id.clone(),
947	            "squash".to_string(),
948	            None,
949	            false,
950	            false,
951	            false,
952	            None,
953	            false,
954	        ),
955	        CompletionAction::Abandon => {
956	            super::lifecycle::abandon_command(state.run_id.clone(), false, false)
957	        }
958	        CompletionAction::Docs => {
959	            Box::pin(super::doc::doc_command(super::doc::DocCommandArgs {
960	                run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
961	                kind: CliDocKind::Narrative,
962	                export: None,
963	                polish: false,
964	                no_confirm: true,
965	                force: false,
966	                doc_skill: None,
967	                doc_provider: None,
968	                budget_cap: None,
969	            }))
970	            .await
971	        }
972	        CompletionAction::Show => {
973	            show_command(&state.run_id, None, false, false, false, false, None)
974	        }
975	        CompletionAction::Quit => Ok(()),
976	    };
977	    if let Err(err) = &action_result {
978	        print_error(err);
979	        print_error_hint(err);
980	    }
981	    let _ = prompt::open("press Enter to return to attach...", None);
982	    resume_tui(terminal)?;
983	    Ok(Some(AttachActionNotice {
984	        action,
985	        success: action_result.is_ok(),
986	    }))
987	}
988	
989	pub(crate) fn suspend_tui(terminal: &mut Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>) -> Result<()> {
990	    disable_raw_mode()?;
991	    execute!(
992	        terminal.backend_mut(),
993	        DisableMouseCapture,
994	        LeaveAlternateScreen
995	    )?;
996	    terminal.show_cursor()?;
997	    note_tui_suspended();
998	    Ok(())
999	}
1000	
1001	pub(crate) fn resume_tui(terminal: &mut Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>) -> Result<()> {
1002	    enable_raw_mode()?;
1003	    execute!(
1004	        terminal.backend_mut(),
1005	        EnterAlternateScreen,
1006	        EnableMouseCapture
1007	    )?;
1008	    note_tui_resumed();
1009	    Ok(())
1010	}
1011

1014	    reset_tui_suspend_depth();
1015	    note_tui_suspended();
1016	    note_tui_suspended();
1017	    note_tui_resumed();
1018	    note_tui_resumed();
1019	}

1021	pub(crate) fn attach_should_quit(key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
1022	    matches!(key.code, KeyCode::Char('q') | KeyCode::Esc)
1023	        || (key.code == KeyCode::Char('d') && key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL))
1024	}
