```text
388	async fn collect_doctor_provider_findings(
389	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
390	    root: &toml::Value,
391	) -> Result<Vec<DoctorFinding>> {
392	    let Some(providers) = root.get("providers").and_then(toml::Value::as_table) else {
393	        return Ok(vec![DoctorFinding::failed(
394	            "providers",
395	            "providers table missing",
396	            Some("deadreckon init".to_string()),
397	        )]);
398	    };
399	    let registry = ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())?;
400	    let mut findings = Vec::new();
401	    for (name, entry) in providers {
402	        let kind = entry
403	            .get("kind")
404	            .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
405	            .unwrap_or(name);
406	        let kind_label = registry
407	            .get(name)
408	            .map(|descriptor| descriptor_kind_label(&descriptor.kind).to_string())
409	            .unwrap_or_else(|| config_provider_kind_label(kind).to_string());
410	        let subject = format!("provider {name} kind={kind_label}");
411	        if kind.contains("cli") || name.starts_with("cli:") {
412	            let binary = entry
413	                .get("binary")
414	                .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
415	                .unwrap_or_else(|| {
416	                    if name.contains("claude") {
417	                        "claude"
418	                    } else {
419	                        "codex"
420	                    }
421	                });
422	            if command_exists(binary) || PathBuf::from(binary).exists() {
423	                findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
424	                    subject,
425	                    format!("CLI binary {binary} found"),
426	                    Some(format!(
427	                        "deadreckon run \"goal\" --provider {name} --preview"
428	                    )),
429	                ));
430	            } else {
431	                findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
432	                    subject,
433	                    format!("CLI binary {binary} missing"),
434	                    Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
435	                ));
436	            }
437	        } else if provider_has_key(entry) {
438	            if std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING").is_some() {
439	                findings.push(collect_doctor_provider_ping(paths, name, &kind_label).await?);
440	            } else {
441	                findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
442	                    subject,
443	                    "credential present; ping skipped",
444	                    Some("DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1 deadreckon doctor".to_string()),
445	                ));
446	            }
447	        } else {
448	            findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
449	                subject,
450	                "credential missing",
451	                Some(format!(
452	                    "deadreckon config set providers.{name}.api_key <KEY>"
453	                )),
454	            ));
455	        }
456	    }
457	    Ok(findings)
458	}

460	async fn collect_doctor_provider_ping(
461	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
462	    name: &str,
463	    kind_label: &str,
464	) -> Result<DoctorFinding> {
465	    let router = ProviderRouter::from_config_path(&paths.config_path(), Some(name))?;
466	    let request = ProviderRequest {
467	        prompt: "Reply with OK only.".to_string(),
468	        max_output_tokens: 8,
469	        cwd: None,
470	        output_path: None,
471	        sandbox_backend: None,
472	        pid_file: None,
473	        cancellation_token: None,
474	    };
475	    let subject = format!("provider {name} kind={kind_label}");
476	    match tokio::time::timeout(
477	        std::time::Duration::from_secs(20),
478	        router.complete(&request),
479	    )
480	    .await
481	    {
482	        Ok(Ok(response)) => Ok(DoctorFinding::passed(
483	            subject,
484	            format!("ping ok model {}", response.model),
485	            Some(format!(
486	                "deadreckon run \"goal\" --provider {name} --preview"
487	            )),
488	        )),
489	        Ok(Err(err)) => Ok(DoctorFinding::failed(
490	            subject,
491	            format!("ping failed: {err}"),
492	            Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
493	        )),
494	        Err(_) => Ok(DoctorFinding::failed(
495	            subject,
496	            "ping timed out",
497	            Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
498	        )),
499	    }
500	}

623	fn doctor_seam_resolution(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, no_seams: bool) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
624	    let seams = read_seams_config(&paths.config_path(), no_seams)?;
625	    Ok(SeamKind::all()
626	        .into_iter()
627	        .map(|kind| {
628	            let fail = seam_fail_policy_label(kind);
629	            match seams.command_for(kind) {
630	                Some(command) => format!(
631	                    "{}: external command={} timeout_ms={} fail={fail}",
632	                    kind.config_key(),
633	                    seam_command_basename(&command.command),
634	                    command.timeout_ms
635	                ),
636	                None => format!("{}: builtin fail={fail}", kind.config_key()),
637	            }
638	        })
639	        .collect())
640	}

642	fn seam_command_basename(command: &[String]) -> String {
643	    command
644	        .first()
645	        .and_then(|argv0| Path::new(argv0).file_name())
646	        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
647	        .unwrap_or("-")
648	        .to_string()
649	}

651	fn config_provider_kind_label(kind: &str) -> &'static str {
652	    let kind = kind.to_ascii_lowercase();
653	    if kind.contains("cli") {
654	        "cli"
655	    } else if kind.contains("compatible") || kind.contains("local") {
656	        "local-http"
657	    } else if kind.contains("smoke") || kind.contains("script") {
658	        "scripted"
659	    } else if kind.contains("anthropic") || kind.contains("open-ai") || kind.contains("openai") {
660	        "http"
661	    } else {
662	        "custom"
663	    }
664	}

666	fn provider_has_key(entry: &toml::Value) -> bool {
667	    entry
668	        .get("api_key")
669	        .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
670	        .is_some_and(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
671	        || entry
672	            .get("api_key_env")
673	            .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
674	            .and_then(std::env::var_os)
675	            .is_some()
676	}

678	fn command_version(path: &std::path::Path) -> Option<String> {
679	    std::process::Command::new(path)
680	        .arg("--version")
681	        .output()
682	        .ok()
683	        .filter(|output| output.status.success())
684	        .map(|output| {
685	            let text = if output.stdout.is_empty() {
686	                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string()
687	            } else {
688	                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string()
689	            };
690	            text.lines().next().unwrap_or_default().trim().to_string()
691	        })
692	        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
693	}
```

```text
9989	fn sleep_status_for_working(working_dir: &Path) -> Option<String> {
9990	    let path = sleep::metadata_path(working_dir);
9991	    let raw = fs::read_to_string(path).ok()?;
9992	    let metadata: sleep::SleepMetadata = serde_json::from_str(&raw).ok()?;
9993	    let mode = match metadata.mode {
9994	        sleep::SleepMode::Caffeinate => "caffeinate",
```

```text
62	async fn validate_seam_report(

135	    Ok(classify_validation_outcome(

140	fn classify_validation_outcome(
141	    kind: SeamKind,
142	    command: &SeamCommandConfig,
143	    fixture: &Path,
144	    sandbox: String,
145	    outcome: SeamOutcome,
146	) -> SeamValidationReport {
147	    let command_name = seam_command_basename(&command.command);
148	    let fail_policy = seam_fail_policy_label(kind).to_string();
149	    let base = |outcome: &str,
150	                decision: Option<String>,
151	                detail: Option<String>,
152	                try_lines: Vec<String>,
153	                exit_success| {
154	        SeamValidationReport {
155	            kind: cli_kind_label(kind).to_string(),
156	            command: command_name.clone(),
157	            fixture: display_path(fixture),
158	            sandbox: sandbox.clone(),
159	            outcome: outcome.to_string(),
160	            fail_policy: fail_policy.clone(),
161	            source: "external".to_string(),
162	            decision,
163	            detail,
164	            try_lines,
165	            exit_success,
166	        }
167	    };
168	
169	    match outcome {
170	        SeamOutcome::Ok(_) if kind == SeamKind::Policy => {
171	            base("passed", Some("allow".to_string()), None, Vec::new(), true)
172	        }
173	        SeamOutcome::Ok(value) if kind == SeamKind::Catalog => {
174	            match ModelCatalogOverride::from_value(value) {
175	                Ok(_) => base("passed", None, None, Vec::new(), true),
176	                Err(err) => base(
177	                    "failed",
178	                    None,
179	                    Some(format!("catalog response failed open: {err}")),
180	                    vec![
181	                        r#"return {"models":[{"id":"local-model","context_window":4000}]}"#
182	                            .to_string(),
183	                    ],
184	                    false,
185	                ),
186	            }
187	        }
188	        SeamOutcome::Ok(_) => base("passed", None, None, Vec::new(), true),
189	        SeamOutcome::Deny(reason)
190	            if kind == SeamKind::Policy && !reason.contains("failed closed") =>
191	        {
192	            base(
193	                "passed",
194	                Some("deny".to_string()),
195	                Some(reason),
196	                Vec::new(),
197	                true,
198	            )
199	        }
200	        SeamOutcome::Deny(reason) => base(
201	            "failed",
202	            None,
203	            Some(reason),
204	            vec![
205	                r#"return {"decision":"allow"} or {"decision":"deny","reason":"..."}"#.to_string(),
206	                "rerun the launch with --no-seams to force built-ins".to_string(),
207	            ],
208	            false,
209	        ),
210	        SeamOutcome::Fallback => base(
211	            "failed",
212	            None,
213	            Some("catalog worker failed open; runtime would use the built-in catalog".to_string()),
214	            vec![r#"return {"models":[{"id":"local-model","context_window":4000}]}"#.to_string()],
215	            false,
216	        ),
217	        SeamOutcome::Skipped(reason) => base(
218	            "non_fatal",
219	            None,
220	            Some(format!(
221	                "observer worker failed safe; runtime would continue: {reason}"
222	            )),
223	            vec!["inspect the worker command, timeout, and stderr".to_string()],
224	            true,
225	        ),
226	        SeamOutcome::Unconfigured => base(
227	            "failed",
228	            None,
229	            Some("no external worker configured".to_string()),
230	            vec![format!("add [seams.{}] to config", kind.config_key())],
231	            false,
232	        ),
233	    }
234	}

240	fn seam_validation_surface(report: &SeamValidationReport) -> VerdictSurface {
241	    let kind = if report.exit_success {
242	        VerdictKind::Verified
243	    } else {
244	        VerdictKind::Failed
245	    };
246	    let primary = seam_validation_primary_action(report);
247	    let secondary = report
248	        .try_lines
249	        .iter()
250	        .filter_map(|line| {
251	            let line = line.trim();
252	            (line.starts_with("deadreckon ") && line != primary).then_some(("Secondary", line))
253	        })
254	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
255	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
256	        kind,
257	        "seam",
258	        Some(&report.kind),
259	        seam_validation_explanation(report),
260	        vec![("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
261	        secondary,
262	    )
263	    .expect("seam validation verdict surface must be valid")
264	}
265	
266	fn seam_validation_primary_action(report: &SeamValidationReport) -> String {
267	    if !report.exit_success
268	        && let Some(command) = report
269	            .try_lines
270	            .iter()
271	            .map(|line| line.trim())
272	            .find(|line| line.starts_with("deadreckon "))
273	    {
274	        return command.to_string();
275	    }
276	    if report.exit_success {
277	        "deadreckon run \"goal\"".to_string()
278	    } else {
279	        "deadreckon doctor".to_string()
280	    }
281	}

283	fn seam_validation_explanation(report: &SeamValidationReport) -> ExplanationPanel {
284	    let what = if report.exit_success {
285	        format!(
286	            "Seam validation completed for the {} worker with outcome {}.",
287	            report.kind, report.outcome
288	        )
289	    } else {
290	        format!(
291	            "Seam validation failed for the {} worker with outcome {}.",
292	            report.kind, report.outcome
293	        )
294	    };
295	    let why = report.detail.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {
296	        if report.exit_success {
297	            format!(
298	                "The worker response satisfies the {} fail policy for this seam.",
299	                report.fail_policy
300	            )
301	        } else {
302	            format!(
303	                "The worker response does not satisfy the {} fail policy for this seam.",
304	                report.fail_policy
305	            )
306	        }
307	    });
308	    let mut evidence = vec![
309	        ("kind", report.kind.clone()),
310	        ("outcome", report.outcome.clone()),
311	        ("command", report.command.clone()),
312	        ("fixture", report.fixture.clone()),
313	        ("sandbox", report.sandbox.clone()),
314	        ("fail policy", report.fail_policy.clone()),
315	        ("source", report.source.clone()),
316	    ];
317	    if let Some(decision) = &report.decision {
318	        evidence.push(("decision", decision.clone()));
319	    }
320	    if let Some(detail) = &report.detail {
321	        evidence.push(("detail", detail.clone()));
322	    }
323	    ExplanationPanel::new(what, why, evidence)
324	}
```

```text
6	        path: None,
7	        no_rc: false,
8	    }) {
9	        CompletionCommand::Install { shell, path, no_rc } => {

17	        CompletionCommand::Elvish => write_completion_script(Shell::Elvish, &mut io::stdout()),
18	        CompletionCommand::Fish => write_completion_script(Shell::Fish, &mut io::stdout()),

43	fn install_completion(
44	    shell: Option<Shell>,
45	    path_override: Option<PathBuf>,
46	    update_rc: bool,
47	) -> Result<CompletionInstallOutcome> {
48	    let shell = shell.or_else(detect_completion_shell).ok_or_else(|| {
49	        CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
50	            "could not detect your shell",
51	            "deadreckon completion install --shell zsh",
52	        ))
53	    })?;
54	    let path = path_override.unwrap_or_else(|| default_completion_path(shell));
55	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
56	        fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
57	    }
58	    let mut script = Vec::new();
59	    write_completion_script(shell, &mut script);
60	    fs::write(&path, script)?;
61	    let rc_status = match (shell, update_rc) {
62	        (Shell::Zsh, true) => ensure_zsh_completion_rc(&path)?,
63	        (Shell::Zsh, false) => CompletionRcStatus::Skipped,
64	        _ => CompletionRcStatus::NotApplicable,
65	    };
66	    Ok(CompletionInstallOutcome {
67	        shell,
68	        path,
69	        rc_status,
70	    })
71	}

73	pub(crate) fn try_install_completion_after_init() -> String {
74	    match install_completion(None, None, true) {
75	        Ok(outcome) => format!(
76	            "installed {} completion at {}",

78	            outcome.path.display()
79	        ),

82	}

92	enum CompletionRcStatus {
93	    Updated(PathBuf),
94	    Ready(PathBuf),
95	    Skipped,
96	    NotApplicable,
97	}
98	
99	fn completion_install_surface(outcome: &CompletionInstallOutcome) -> VerdictSurface {
100	    let shell = completion_shell_name(outcome.shell);
101	    let primary = "deadreckon doctor";
102	    let rc_evidence = outcome.rc_status.evidence_value();
103	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
104	        VerdictKind::Completed,
105	        "completion",

107	        ExplanationPanel::new(
108	            format!(
109	                "DeadReckon wrote the {shell} completion script to {}.",
110	                outcome.path.display()
111	            ),

113	            vec![
114	                ("shell", shell.to_string()),
115	                ("script", outcome.path.display().to_string()),
116	                ("shell rc", rc_evidence),
117	            ],
118	        ),
119	        vec![("Recommended", primary)],
120	        Vec::<(&str, &str)>::new(),
121	    )
122	    .expect("completion install verdict surface must be valid")
123	}
124	
125	fn completion_shell_name(shell: Shell) -> &'static str {
126	    match shell {
127	        Shell::Bash => "bash",
128	        Shell::Elvish => "elvish",
129	        Shell::Fish => "fish",
130	        Shell::PowerShell => "powershell",
131	        Shell::Zsh => "zsh",
132	        _ => "shell",
133	    }
134	}
135	
136	impl CompletionRcStatus {
137	    fn evidence_value(&self) -> String {
138	        match self {
139	            Self::Updated(path) => format!("updated {}", path.display()),
140	            Self::Ready(path) => format!("already configured {}", path.display()),
141	            Self::Skipped => "not updated (--no-rc)".to_string(),
142	            Self::NotApplicable => "not required for this shell".to_string(),
143	        }
144	    }
145	}
146	
147	fn detect_completion_shell() -> Option<Shell> {
148	    let shell = std::env::var("SHELL").ok()?;
149	    let name = Path::new(&shell).file_name()?.to_string_lossy();
150	    match name.as_ref() {
151	        "bash" => Some(Shell::Bash),
152	        "elvish" => Some(Shell::Elvish),
153	        "fish" => Some(Shell::Fish),
154	        "pwsh" | "powershell" => Some(Shell::PowerShell),
155	        "zsh" => Some(Shell::Zsh),
156	        _ => None,
157	    }
158	}
159	
160	fn default_completion_path(shell: Shell) -> PathBuf {
161	    let home = std::env::var_os("HOME")
162	        .map(PathBuf::from)
163	        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
164	    match shell {
165	        Shell::Bash => home
166	            .join(".local")
167	            .join("share")
168	            .join("bash-completion")
169	            .join("completions")
170	            .join("deadreckon"),
171	        Shell::Elvish => home
172	            .join(".config")
173	            .join("elvish")
174	            .join("lib")
175	            .join("deadreckon-completers.elv"),
176	        Shell::Fish => home
177	            .join(".config")
178	            .join("fish")
179	            .join("completions")
180	            .join("deadreckon.fish"),
181	        Shell::PowerShell => home
182	            .join(".config")
183	            .join("powershell")
184	            .join("deadreckon-completions.ps1"),
185	        Shell::Zsh => home.join(".zsh").join("completions").join("_deadreckon"),
186	        _ => home.join(".deadreckon").join("completion"),
187	    }
188	}
189	
190	fn ensure_zsh_completion_rc(completion_path: &Path) -> Result<CompletionRcStatus> {
191	    let Some(completion_dir) = completion_path.parent() else {
192	        return Ok(CompletionRcStatus::Skipped);
193	    };
194	    let home = std::env::var_os("HOME")
195	        .map(PathBuf::from)
196	        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
197	    let zshrc = home.join(".zshrc");
198	    let existing = fs::read_to_string(&zshrc).unwrap_or_default();
199	    let completion_dir = completion_dir.display();
200	    let block = format!(
201	        "\n# >>> deadreckon completion >>>\nfpath=({completion_dir} $fpath)\nautoload -Uz compinit\ncompinit\n# <<< deadreckon completion <<<\n"
202	    );
203	    if existing.contains("# >>> deadreckon completion >>>")
204	        || existing.contains(&format!("fpath=({completion_dir} $fpath)"))
205	    {
206	        return Ok(CompletionRcStatus::Ready(zshrc));
207	    }
208	    let mut file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
209	        .create(true)
210	        .append(true)
211	        .open(&zshrc)?;
212	    file.write_all(block.as_bytes())?;
213	    Ok(CompletionRcStatus::Updated(zshrc))
214	}
```

```text
123	            if !quiet {
124	                println!(
125	                    "{}",
126	                    update_shell_completed_surface(&current, &latest, &backup_dir, receipt)
127	                        .render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false))
128	                );
129	            }
130	            Ok(())
131	        }
132	        Err(source) => Err(shell_update_failure(receipt, &backup_dir, &source)),
133	    }
134	}

136	fn create_shell_update_backup(
137	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
138	    receipt: &deadreckon_core::install_receipt::Receipt,
139	    backup_dir: PathBuf,
140	) -> Result<PathBuf> {
141	    let root = shell_backup_root(paths);
142	    fs::create_dir_all(&root)?;
143	    fs::create_dir_all(&backup_dir)?;
144	    fs::copy(&receipt.binary_path, backup_dir.join("deadreckon"))?;
145	    fs::write(
146	        backup_dir.join("receipt.json"),
147	        serde_json::to_vec_pretty(receipt)?,
148	    )?;
149	    Ok(backup_dir)
150	}

205	fn confirm_shell_update(
206	    yes: bool,
207	    current: &str,
208	    latest: &LatestUpdate,
209	    receipt: &deadreckon_core::install_receipt::Receipt,
210	) -> Result<()> {
211	    if yes {
212	        return Ok(());
213	    }
214	    if !io::stdin().is_terminal() {
215	        return Err(CliError::Surface {
216	            code: 1,
217	            surface: update_shell_requires_yes_surface(current, latest, receipt)
218	                .render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false)),
219	        });
220	    }
221	    if prompt::confirm("apply this shell update?", false)? {
222	        Ok(())
223	    } else {
224	        Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
225	            "update cancelled by user".to_string(),
226	        )))
227	    }
228	}

260	fn unique_shell_backup_dir(root: &Path) -> PathBuf {
261	    let stamp = Utc::now().format("%Y%m%d%H%M%S%3f").to_string();
262	    let mut candidate = root.join(&stamp);
263	    let mut suffix = 1_u32;
264	    while candidate.exists() {
265	        candidate = root.join(format!("{stamp}-{suffix}"));
266	        suffix += 1;
267	    }
268	    candidate
269	}

288	async fn run_axoupdater_shell_update(
289	    receipt: &deadreckon_core::install_receipt::Receipt,
290	    force: bool,
291	    allow_prerelease: bool,
292	    quiet: bool,
293	) -> std::result::Result<(), String> {
294	    let mut updater = axoupdater::AxoUpdater::new_for("deadreckon");
295	    updater.set_release_source(axoupdater::ReleaseSource {
296	        release_type: axoupdater::ReleaseSourceType::GitHub,
297	        owner: "gdc".to_string(),
298	        name: "deadreckon".to_string(),
299	        app_name: "deadreckon".to_string(),
300	    });
301	    let version = update_current_version(receipt)
302	        .parse::<axoupdater::Version>()
303	        .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
304	    updater
305	        .set_current_version(version)
306	        .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
307	    if let Some(parent) = receipt.binary_path.parent() {
308	        updater.set_install_dir(parent.to_string_lossy().to_string());
309	    }
310	    if allow_prerelease {
311	        updater.configure_version_specifier(axoupdater::UpdateRequest::LatestMaybePrerelease);
312	    }
313	    if force {
314	        updater.always_update(true);
315	    }
316	    if quiet {
317	        updater.disable_installer_output();
318	    }
319	    updater.run().await.map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
320	    Ok(())
321	}

333	fn prune_shell_backups(paths: &DeadreckonPaths) -> Result<()> {
334	    let root = shell_backup_root(paths);
335	    let mut backups = fs::read_dir(&root)?
336	        .filter_map(|entry| {
337	            let entry = entry.ok()?;
338	            entry.path().is_dir().then_some(entry.path())
339	        })
340	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
341	    backups.sort();
342	    let remove_count = backups.len().saturating_sub(3);
343	    for backup in backups.into_iter().take(remove_count) {
344	        fs::remove_dir_all(backup)?;
345	    }
346	    Ok(())
347	}

416	fn update_check_surface(channel: Channel, current: &str, latest: &LatestUpdate) -> VerdictSurface {
417	    let evidence = vec![
418	        ("channel", channel.as_str().to_string()),
419	        ("current", current.to_string()),

436	        .expect("update-check preview verdict surface must be valid");

439	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
440	        VerdictKind::Noop,
441	        "update",
442	        Some(channel.as_str()),
443	        ExplanationPanel::new(
444	            "DeadReckon did not find a newer release for this install channel.",
445	            "The installed version is already current, or the check fell back to cached/current release metadata.",
446	            evidence,
447	        ),
448	        vec![("Recommended", "deadreckon doctor")],
449	        Vec::<(&str, &str)>::new(),
450	    )
451	    .expect("update-check no-op verdict surface must be valid")
452	}

508	pub(crate) async fn resolve_latest_update(
509	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
510	    current: &str,
511	    allow_prerelease: bool,
512	) -> Result<LatestUpdate> {
513	    let now = Utc::now();
514	    let cache = read_cache(paths)?;
515	    if let Some(cache) = cache.as_ref()
516	        && !cache.is_stale(now)
517	    {
518	        return Ok(LatestUpdate {
519	            version: cache.latest_version.clone(),
520	            release_url: cache.release_url.clone(),
521	            archive_url: None,
522	            sha256: None,
523	            update_available: cache.update_available,
524	        });
525	    }
526	
527	    match fetch_latest_update(allow_prerelease).await {
528	        Ok(mut latest) => {
529	            latest.update_available = version_is_newer(current, &latest.version);
530	            write_cache(
531	                paths,
532	                &deadreckon_core::update_cache::Cache {
533	                    checked_at: now,
534	                    latest_version: latest.version.clone(),
535	                    current_version: current.to_string(),
536	                    release_url: latest.release_url.clone(),
537	                    update_available: latest.update_available,
538	                },
539	            )?;
540	            Ok(latest)
541	        }
542	        Err(_) => Ok(cache.map_or_else(
543	            || LatestUpdate {
544	                version: current.to_string(),
545	                release_url: "https://github.com/gdc/deadreckon/releases".to_string(),
546	                archive_url: None,
547	                sha256: None,
548	                update_available: false,
549	            },
550	            |cache| LatestUpdate {
551	                version: cache.latest_version,
552	                release_url: cache.release_url,
553	                archive_url: None,
554	                sha256: None,
555	                update_available: cache.update_available,
556	            },
557	        )),
558	    }
559	}
560	
561	async fn fetch_latest_update(allow_prerelease: bool) -> std::result::Result<LatestUpdate, String> {
562	    if let Ok(delay_ms) = std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_TEST_FETCH_DELAY_MS")
563	        && let Ok(delay_ms) = delay_ms.parse::<u64>()
564	    {
565	        tokio::time::sleep(Duration::from_millis(delay_ms)).await;
566	    }
567	    if std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_TEST_OFFLINE").is_some() {
568	        return Err("offline test mode".to_string());
569	    }
570	    if let Ok(version) = std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_TEST_LATEST_VERSION") {
571	        let release_url =
572	            std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_TEST_RELEASE_URL").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
573	                format!("https://github.com/gdc/deadreckon/releases/tag/v{version}")
574	            });
575	        return Ok(LatestUpdate {
576	            version,
577	            release_url,
578	            archive_url: std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_TEST_ARCHIVE_URL").ok(),
579	            sha256: std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_TEST_SHA256").ok(),
580	            update_available: false,
581	        });
582	    }
583	
584	    let client = reqwest::Client::builder()
585	        .timeout(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3))
586	        .build()
587	        .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
588	    if allow_prerelease {
589	        let url = std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_RELEASES_URL")
590	            .unwrap_or_else(|_| "https://api.github.com/repos/gdc/deadreckon/releases".to_string());
591	        let releases = client
592	            .get(url)
593	            .header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, "deadreckon-update")
594	            .send()
595	            .await
596	            .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?
597	            .error_for_status()
598	            .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?
599	            .json::<Vec<GithubRelease>>()
600	            .await
601	            .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?;
602	        let Some(release) = releases.into_iter().next() else {
603	            return Err("no releases found".to_string());
604	        };
605	        return Ok(release.into_latest_update());
606	    }
607	
608	    let url = std::env::var("DEADRECKON_UPDATE_RELEASES_URL").unwrap_or_else(|_| {
609	        "https://api.github.com/repos/gdc/deadreckon/releases/latest".to_string()
610	    });
611	    client
612	        .get(url)
613	        .header(reqwest::header::USER_AGENT, "deadreckon-update")
614	        .send()
615	        .await
616	        .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?
617	        .error_for_status()
618	        .map_err(|err| err.to_string())?
619	        .json::<GithubRelease>()
620	        .await
621	        .map(GithubRelease::into_latest_update)
622	        .map_err(|err| err.to_string())
623	}

643	fn version_is_newer(current: &str, latest: &str) -> bool {
644	    let current = current.trim_start_matches('v');
645	    let latest = latest.trim_start_matches('v');
646	    match (
647	        semver::Version::parse(current),
648	        semver::Version::parse(latest),
649	    ) {
650	        (Ok(current), Ok(latest)) => latest > current,
651	        _ => latest != current,
652	    }
653	}

655	async fn providers_list_command(
656	    models: bool,
657	    all: bool,
658	    full: bool,
659	    json_output: bool,
660	) -> Result<()> {
661	    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
662	    let registry = ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())?;
663	    let active = read_config(&paths.config_path())?.default_provider;
664	    let ids = if all {
665	        registry.ids()
666	    } else {
667	        configured_provider_ids(&paths)?
668	    };
669	    let mut results = Vec::new();
670	    let mut missing = Vec::new();
671	    for id in ids {
672	        if let Some(descriptor) = registry.get(&id) {
673	            results.push(descriptor.probe(ProviderProbeOptions { ping: false }).await);
674	        } else {
675	            missing.push(id);
676	        }
677	    }
678	    let surface = providers_list_verdict_surface(&results, &missing, all);
679	    if json_output {
680	        let primary_action = surface.primary_action.command.clone();
681	        println!(
682	            "{}",
683	            serde_json::to_string_pretty(&surface.add_to_json(json!({
684	                "kind": "providers",
685	                "id": if all { "all" } else { "configured" },
686	                "status": "ok",
687	                "next_actions": [primary_action],
688	                "try_lines": Vec::<String>::new(),
689	                "paths": {
690	                    "home": paths.home(),
691	                    "config": paths.config_path(),
692	                },
693	                "providers": results,
694	                "missing_providers": missing,
695	                "active": active,
696	            })))?
697	        );
698	        return Ok(());
699	    }
700	    println!("{}", ui_heading("provider registry"));
701	    if results.is_empty() && missing.is_empty() {
702	        println!("{} no configured providers", ui_muted("-"));
703	        println!("{}", surface.render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false)));
704	        return Ok(());
705	    }
706	    for id in &missing {
707	        let marker = if active.as_deref() == Some(id.as_str()) {
708	            "*"
709	        } else {
710	            " "
711	        };
712	        println!(
713	            "{marker} {} {} not registered | {}",
714	            ui_warn("✗"),
715	            ui_id(id),
716	            ui_command("deadreckon providers list --all")
717	        );
718	    }
719	    for result in &results {
720	        let Some(descriptor) = registry.get(&result.id) else {
721	            continue;
722	        };
723	        print_provider_list_row(&result, descriptor, active.as_deref(), full);
724	        if models {
725	            print_provider_models(descriptor);
726	        }
727	    }
728	    println!("{}", surface.render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false)));
729	    Ok(())
730	}
731	
732	fn providers_list_verdict_surface(
733	    results: &[ProviderProbeResult],
734	    missing: &[String],
735	    all: bool,
736	) -> VerdictSurface {
737	    let failed = results
738	        .iter()
739	        .filter(|result| result.status == ProbeStatus::Failed)
740	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
741	    let ok = results
```

```text
234	fn wrap_campaign_words(value: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
235	    let width = width.max(16);
236	    let mut lines = Vec::new();
237	    let mut current = String::new();
238	    for word in value.split_whitespace() {
239	        push_campaign_word(&mut lines, &mut current, word, width);
240	    }
241	    if !current.is_empty() {
242	        lines.push(current);
243	    }
244	    if lines.is_empty() {
245	        lines.push("-".to_string());
246	    }
247	    lines
248	}

250	fn push_campaign_word(lines: &mut Vec<String>, current: &mut String, word: &str, width: usize) {
251	    let word_len = word.chars().count();
252	    if current.is_empty() {
253	        if word_len <= width {
254	            current.push_str(word);
255	        } else {
256	            push_campaign_word_chunks(lines, current, word, width);
257	        }
258	        return;
259	    }
260	    let current_len = current.chars().count();
261	    if current_len + 1 + word_len <= width {
262	        current.push(' ');
263	        current.push_str(word);
264	        return;
265	    }
266	    lines.push(std::mem::take(current));
267	    if word_len <= width {
268	        current.push_str(word);
269	    } else {
270	        push_campaign_word_chunks(lines, current, word, width);
271	    }
272	}
273	
274	fn push_campaign_word_chunks(
275	    lines: &mut Vec<String>,
276	    current: &mut String,
277	    word: &str,
278	    width: usize,
279	) {
280	    for ch in word.chars() {
281	        current.push(ch);
282	        if current.chars().count() >= width {
283	            lines.push(std::mem::take(current));
284	        }
285	    }
286	}
```

```text
291	fn write_kv_block<K, V>(items: &[(K, V)]) -> io::Result<()>
292	where
293	    K: AsRef<str>,
294	    V: AsRef<str>,
295	{
296	    let width = items
297	        .iter()
298	        .map(|(key, _)| key.as_ref().chars().count())
299	        .max()
300	        .unwrap_or(0);
301	    let prefix_width = width + 2;
302	    let value_width = kv_value_width(prefix_width);
303	    for (key, value) in items {
304	        let mut first = true;
305	        for logical_line in value
306	            .as_ref()
307	            .lines()
308	            .chain(value.as_ref().is_empty().then_some("").into_iter())
309	        {
310	            for line in wrap_kv_value(logical_line, value_width) {
311	                let rendered = if first {
312	                    first = false;
313	                    format!("{:<width$}: {}", key.as_ref(), line)
314	                } else {
315	                    format!("{:prefix_width$}{}", "", line)
316	                };
317	                ui::writeln(ui::Stream::Stdout, ui::Tone::Plain, rendered)?;
318	            }
319	        }
320	    }
321	    Ok(())
322	}

331	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
332	        })
333	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 1)
334	        .unwrap_or(120)
335	        .saturating_sub(1);
336	    terminal_width.saturating_sub(prefix_width).max(20)
337	}
```

```text
## GitHub Stars & Maintenance
```

```text
443	pub(crate) fn estimate_doc_polish_spend(
444	    router: &ProviderRouter,
445	    provider: &str,
446	    token_budget: u32,
447	    subskill_count: usize,
448	) -> Result<SpendEstimate> {
449	    let calls = subskill_count.max(1) as u64;

451	        .estimate_for_route(

456	            },
457	        )
458	        .map_err(CliError::from)

493	    } else {
494	        "The polish record contains an error, so rerunning polish is the primary recovery command while fallback docs remain available."
495	    };
496	    let primary = if successful {

498	    } else {
499	        format!("deadreckon doc {id} --polish --no-confirm --force")
500	    };
501	    let mut evidence = vec![
502	        ("run".to_string(), id.clone()),
503	        ("status".to_string(), record.status.clone()),
504	        ("cost".to_string(), polish_record_cost_label(record)),
505	        ("completed".to_string(), record.completed_at.clone()),
506	    ];

512	    }
513	    if let Some(error) = record.error.as_deref() {

520	                "{} {} in / {} out {}",

525	            ),
526	        ));
527	    }
528	    print!(
529	        "{}",
530	        VerdictSurface::try_new(
531	            kind,
532	            "doc",
533	            Some(&id),
534	            ExplanationPanel::new(what, why, evidence),

539	            ],
540	        )
541	        .expect("doc polish verdict surface must have one primary action")
542	        .render_plain(false)
```

```text
457	pub(crate) fn campaign_replace_sub_goals_before_launch(
458	    campaign: &mut deadreckon_core::campaign::Campaign,
459	    sub_goals: Vec<deadreckon_core::campaign::SubGoal>,
460	) -> Result<()> {

474	    campaign: &mut deadreckon_core::campaign::Campaign,
```

```text
367	    column >= rect.x

369	        && row >= rect.y
370	        && row < rect.y.saturating_add(rect.height)
371	}
```

```text
177	pub(crate) fn materialize_completed_run(
178	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
179	    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
180	    dest: Option<PathBuf>,
181	    force: bool,
182	    include_manifest: bool,
183	) -> Result<MaterializedRun> {
184	    ensure_completed_run(state, "materialize")?;
185	    if let Ok(record) = read_codebase_record(&state.working_dir) {
186	        match record.mode {
187	            CodebaseMode::Worktree => {
188	                return Err(codebase_mode_refusal_error(
189	                    "materialize",
190	                    state,
191	                    record.mode,
192	                    "export is for copy/fresh runs; run was worktree",
193	                    format!("deadreckon apply {}", run_prefix(&state.run_id)),
194	                    "Materialize exports copy/fresh artifacts, while this run already has a worktree branch that should be applied instead.",
195	                ));
196	            }
197	            CodebaseMode::InPlace => {
198	                return Err(codebase_mode_refusal_error(
199	                    "materialize",
200	                    state,
201	                    record.mode,
202	                    "export is not needed; run edited the source in-place",
203	                    format!("deadreckon undo --run {}", run_prefix(&state.run_id)),
204	                    "Materialize would duplicate work already written in place; use undo only if those edits need to be reverted.",
205	                ));
206	            }
207	            CodebaseMode::Copy | CodebaseMode::Fresh => {}
208	        }
209	    }
210	    let library_dir = paths.library_dir(&state.scope, &state.run_id);
211	    if !library_dir.is_dir() {
212	        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::NotFound(format!(
213	            "library missing for run {}; was promotion successful?",
214	            state.run_id
215	        ))));
216	    }
217	
218	    let dest = absolute_dest(dest.unwrap_or_else(|| {
219	        std::env::current_dir()
220	            .unwrap_or_else(|_| PathBuf::from("."))
221	            .join(run_prefix(&state.run_id))
222	    }))?;
223	    refuse_dest_inside_home(paths, &dest, "export")?;
224	    prepare_empty_dest(&dest, force)?;
225	
226	    copy_tree(&library_dir, &dest)?;
227	    if !include_manifest {
228	        remove_if_exists(&dest.join("manifest.json"))?;
229	    }
230	    remove_if_exists(&dest.join(".materialized-to"))?;
231	    write_parent_marker(
232	        &dest.join(".deadreckon").join("parent.json"),
233	        &materialized_parent_marker(state),
234	    )?;
235	    normalize_permissions(&dest)?;
236	    append_materialized_marker(&library_dir, &dest)?;
237	
238	    Ok(MaterializedRun {
239	        run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
240	        source: library_dir,
241	        dest,
242	    })
243	}
```

This confirms a bug: `render_plain` takes `no_hints` (true = suppress hints). Everywhere correct callers pass `!completion_hints_enabled(no_hints)`. But `print_campaign_completion` at line 887 passes `render_plain(no_hints)` directly — which inverts the logic AND skips the env-var check. When `no_hints=false` (default), it passes `false` meaning "show hints" — coincidentally correct for default, but `DEADRECKON_HINTS=0` is ignored, and the double-negation pattern is inconsistent. Let me confirm by checking other campaign render call sites.

```text
105	fn select_one_menu(prompt: &SelectPrompt) -> Result<SelectChoice> {
106	    println!("{}", prompt.title);
107	    if let Some(help) = prompt
108	        .help
109	        .as_deref()
110	        .filter(|help| !help.trim().is_empty())
111	    {
112	        println!("  {help}");
113	    }
114	    let mut selected = prompt
115	        .default_index
116	        .min(prompt.choices.len().saturating_sub(1));
117	    let _raw_mode = RawModeGuard::enable()?;
118	    render_select_menu(prompt, selected, false)?;
119	    loop {
120	        let Event::Key(key) = event::read()? else {
121	            continue;
122	        };
123	        if matches!(key.kind, KeyEventKind::Release) {
124	            continue;
125	        }
126	        match key.code {
127	            KeyCode::Char('c') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => {
128	                finish_select_menu_line()?;
129	                return Err(io::Error::new(io::ErrorKind::Interrupted, "prompt cancelled").into());
130	            }
131	            KeyCode::Enter => {
132	                finish_select_menu_line()?;
133	                return Ok(prompt.choices[selected].clone());
134	            }
135	            KeyCode::Char('j' | 'm') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => {
136	                finish_select_menu_line()?;
137	                return Ok(prompt.choices[selected].clone());
138	            }
139	            KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
140	                selected = selected.saturating_sub(1);
141	                render_select_menu(prompt, selected, true)?;
142	            }
143	            KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
144	                if selected + 1 < prompt.choices.len() {
145	                    selected += 1;
146	                }
147	                render_select_menu(prompt, selected, true)?;
148	            }
149	            KeyCode::Home => {
150	                selected = 0;
151	                render_select_menu(prompt, selected, true)?;
152	            }
153	            KeyCode::End => {
154	                selected = prompt.choices.len().saturating_sub(1);
155	                render_select_menu(prompt, selected, true)?;
156	            }
157	            KeyCode::Char(value) if key.modifiers.is_empty() && value.is_ascii_digit() => {
158	                if let Some(index) = select_index_from_digit(value, prompt.choices.len()) {
159	                    finish_select_menu_line()?;
160	                    return Ok(prompt.choices[index].clone());
161	                }
162	            }
163	            KeyCode::Esc => {
164	                if let Some(index) = prompt
165	                    .choices
166	                    .iter()
167	                    .position(|choice| choice.id == "cancel")
168	                {
169	                    finish_select_menu_line()?;
170	                    return Ok(prompt.choices[index].clone());
171	                }
172	            }
173	            _ => {}
174	        }
175	    }
176	}

178	fn render_select_menu(prompt: &SelectPrompt, selected: usize, redraw: bool) -> Result<()> {
179	    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
180	    if redraw {
181	        execute!(stdout, MoveUp(prompt.choices.len() as u16), MoveToColumn(0))?;
182	    }
183	    let width = selectable_menu_width();
184	    for (index, choice) in prompt.choices.iter().enumerate() {
185	        let ordinal = index + 1;
186	        let marker = if index == selected { ">" } else { " " };
187	        execute!(stdout, Clear(ClearType::CurrentLine))?;
188	        let line = match choice.detail.as_deref() {
189	            Some(detail) if !detail.trim().is_empty() => {
190	                format!("  {marker} [{ordinal}] {} - {detail}", choice.label)
191	            }
192	            _ => format!("  {marker} [{ordinal}] {}", choice.label),
193	        };
194	        write_select_menu_line(&mut stdout, &truncate_menu_line(&line, width))?;
195	    }
196	    execute!(stdout, Clear(ClearType::CurrentLine))?;
197	    let default = prompt
198	        .default_index
199	        .min(prompt.choices.len().saturating_sub(1))
200	        + 1;
201	    write!(stdout, "? choose [{default}]: arrows/Enter or number ")?;
202	    stdout.flush()?;
203	    Ok(())
204	}
205	
206	fn write_select_menu_line(stdout: &mut impl io::Write, line: &str) -> io::Result<()> {
207	    write!(stdout, "{line}\r\n")
208	}
209	
210	fn selectable_menu_width() -> usize {
211	    crossterm::terminal::size()
212	        .ok()
213	        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
214	        .or_else(|| {
215	            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
216	                .ok()
217	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
218	        })
219	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 1)
220	        .map(|columns| columns.saturating_sub(1))
221	        .unwrap_or(119)
222	}
223	
224	fn truncate_menu_line(line: &str, max_visible: usize) -> String {
225	    let normalized = normalize_menu_line(line);
226	    if normalized.chars().count() <= max_visible {
227	        return normalized;
228	    }
229	    if max_visible == 0 {
230	        return String::new();
231	    }
232	    if max_visible <= 3 {
233	        return normalized.chars().take(max_visible).collect();
234	    }
235	    let keep = max_visible.saturating_sub(3);
236	    let mut out = normalized.chars().take(keep).collect::<String>();
237	    out.push_str("...");
238	    out
239	}
240	
241	fn normalize_menu_line(line: &str) -> String {
242	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(line.len());
243	    let mut previous_was_space = false;
244	    for ch in line.chars() {
245	        if ch.is_whitespace() {
246	            if !previous_was_space {
247	                out.push(' ');
248	                previous_was_space = true;
249	            }
250	        } else {
251	            out.push(ch);
252	            previous_was_space = false;
253	        }
254	    }
255	    out.trim_end().to_string()
256	}
257	
258	fn finish_select_menu_line() -> io::Result<()> {
259	    let mut stdout = io::stdout();
260	    write!(stdout, "\r\n")?;
261	    stdout.flush()
262	}

264	fn select_index_from_digit(value: char, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {
265	    let digit = value.to_digit(10)? as usize;
266	    if (1..=len).contains(&digit) {
267	        Some(digit - 1)
268	    } else {
269	        None
270	    }
271	}

288	pub(crate) fn confirm(question: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Result<bool> {
289	    let marker = if default_yes { "[Y/n]" } else { "[y/N]" };
290	    loop {
291	        let answer = open(&format!("{question} {marker}: "), None)?;
292	        if let Some(value) = parse_confirm_answer(&answer, default_yes) {
293	            return Ok(value);
294	        }
295	        println!("Please answer y or n.");
296	    }
297	}
298	
299	fn parse_select_answer(answer: &str, default: usize, len: usize) -> Option<usize> {
300	    if len == 0 {
301	        return None;
302	    }
303	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
304	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
305	        return Some(default.saturating_sub(1).min(len - 1));
306	    }
307	    let value = trimmed.parse::<usize>().ok()?;
308	    if (1..=len).contains(&value) {
309	        Some(value - 1)
310	    } else {
311	        None
312	    }
313	}
314	
315	fn parse_confirm_answer(answer: &str, default_yes: bool) -> Option<bool> {
316	    let trimmed = answer.trim();
317	    if trimmed.is_empty() {
318	        return Some(default_yes);
319	    }
320	    match trimmed.to_ascii_lowercase().as_str() {
321	        "y" | "yes" => Some(true),
322	        "n" | "no" => Some(false),
323	        _ => None,
324	    }
325	}
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about rendering a Ratatui Table widget to string as plain text without a terminal backend:

## Key Findings

Ratatui widgets render to an intermediate buffer before any information is written to the terminal, and content rendered to a Buffer is only stored in the Buffer that is attached to the frame during the draw call.

The core rendering mechanism involves:

1. **The Widget Trait**: A Widget is a type that can be drawn on a Buffer in a given Rect. The `render()` method takes ownership and receives a mutable reference to a `Buffer`.

2. **Buffer-Based Rendering**: A Buffer represents a rectangular area that covers the Terminal's Viewport, and contains a collection of Cells to represent the rows and columns of the terminal's display area.

3. **Buffer Methods**: Buffer implements methods to write text, set styles on particular areas and manipulate individual cells.

## For Extracting Plain Text

To render a Table widget to a string without a terminal backend, you would need to:

1. Create a `Buffer` directly (without Terminal involvement)
2. Call the Table widget's `render()` method with that buffer
3. Extract the text content from the buffer's cells

Unfortunately, the search results don't provide specific code examples for extracting plain text from a Buffer post-render. You may want to examine the `ratatui::buffer::Buffer` documentation or explore the `Buffer` API for methods to convert its contents to plain text strings after rendering.
```

```text
260	        pad_plain(&row.mode, LIST_MODE_WIDTH),
261	        pad_plain(&row.action, LIST_ACTION_WIDTH)
262	    );
263	    let continuation_prefix = " ".repeat(list_prefix_width());
264	    let goal_lines = wrap_list_goal(&row.goal, row.goal_width);
265	    for (index, line) in goal_lines.iter().enumerate() {
266	        if index == 0 {
267	            output.push_str(&first_prefix);
268	            output.push_str(line);
269	        } else {
270	            output.push_str(&continuation_prefix);
271	            output.push_str(line);
272	        }
273	        output.push('\n');
274	    }
275	}

282	        + LIST_KIND_WIDTH

288	fn list_goal_width() -> usize {
289	    if !io::stdout().is_terminal() {
290	        return 72;
291	    }
292	    let terminal_width = crossterm::terminal::size()
293	        .map(|(width, _)| width as usize)

298	fn pad_plain(value: &str, width: usize) -> String {
299	    let plain = truncate_text(value, width);
300	    let padding = width.saturating_sub(plain.chars().count());
301	    format!("{plain}{}", " ".repeat(padding))
302	}
303	
304	fn pad_rendered(value: &str, width: usize, render: Option<fn(String) -> String>) -> String {
305	    let plain = truncate_text(value, width);
306	    let padding = width.saturating_sub(plain.chars().count());
307	    let rendered = render.map_or_else(|| plain.clone(), |render| render(plain.clone()));
308	    format!("{rendered}{}", " ".repeat(padding))
309	}

311	fn wrap_list_goal(value: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
312	    let compact = compact_whitespace(value);
313	    if compact.is_empty() {
314	        return vec![String::new()];
315	    }
316	    let mut lines = wrap_words(&compact, width.max(8));
317	    let truncated = lines.len() > LIST_GOAL_MAX_LINES;
318	    if truncated {
319	        lines.truncate(LIST_GOAL_MAX_LINES);
320	        if let Some(last) = lines.last_mut() {
321	            *last = ellipsize_goal_line(last, width);
322	        }
323	    }
324	    lines
325	}
326	
327	fn ellipsize_goal_line(value: &str, width: usize) -> String {
328	    if width <= 3 {
329	        return ".".repeat(width);
330	    }
331	    let prefix = width - 3;
332	    format!("{}...", value.chars().take(prefix).collect::<String>())
333	}
334	
335	fn wrap_words(value: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
336	    let mut lines = Vec::new();
337	    let mut current = String::new();
338	    for word in value.split(' ') {
339	        let word_len = word.chars().count();
340	        if word_len > width {
341	            if !current.is_empty() {
342	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
343	            }
344	            lines.extend(split_long_word(word, width));
345	            continue;
346	        }
347	        let next_len = if current.is_empty() {
348	            word_len
349	        } else {
350	            current.chars().count() + 1 + word_len
351	        };
352	        if next_len <= width {
353	            if !current.is_empty() {
354	                current.push(' ');
355	            }
356	            current.push_str(word);
357	        } else {
358	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
359	            current.push_str(word);
360	        }
361	    }
362	    if !current.is_empty() {
363	        lines.push(current);
364	    }
365	    lines
366	}
367	
368	fn split_long_word(word: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
369	    let mut chunks = Vec::new();
370	    let mut current = String::new();
371	    for ch in word.chars() {
372	        if current.chars().count() >= width {
373	            chunks.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
374	        }
375	        current.push(ch);
376	    }
377	    if !current.is_empty() {
378	        chunks.push(current);
379	    }
380	    chunks
381	}

389	impl ListEntry {
390	    fn updated_at(&self) -> DateTime<Utc> {

393	            Self::Plan(plan) => plan.updated_at,
394	        }

398	#[derive(Debug)]
399	pub(crate) struct PlanListEntry {
400	    pub(crate) plan_id: String,
401	    pub(crate) merged_run_id: Option<String>,
402	    pub(crate) scope: String,
403	    pub(crate) goal: String,
404	    pub(crate) status: PlanStatus,
405	    pub(crate) mode: PlanMode,
406	    pub(crate) updated_at: DateTime<Utc>,
407	    pub(crate) plan_path: PathBuf,
408	    pub(crate) completed_children: usize,
409	    pub(crate) total_children: usize,
410	}
411	
412	pub(crate) fn list_plan_entries(
413	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
414	    scope_filter: Option<&str>,
415	) -> Result<Vec<PlanListEntry>> {
416	    let root = paths.plans_dir();
417	    if !root.exists() {
418	        return Ok(Vec::new());
419	    }
420	    let mut plans = Vec::new();
421	    for entry in fs::read_dir(&root).map_err(|source| DeadreckonError::Io {
422	        path: root.clone(),
423	        source,
424	    })? {
425	        let entry = entry?;
426	        let plan_path = entry.path().join("plan.json");
427	        if !plan_path.is_file() {
428	            continue;
429	        }
430	        let Some(plan_id) = entry.file_name().to_str().map(str::to_string) else {
431	            continue;
432	        };
433	        let plan = load_plan(paths, &plan_id)?;
434	        if scope_filter.is_some_and(|scope| plan.parent_scope.as_deref() != Some(scope)) {
435	            continue;
436	        }
437	        let updated_at = fs::metadata(&plan_path)
438	            .and_then(|metadata| metadata.modified())
439	            .map(DateTime::<Utc>::from)
440	            .unwrap_or_else(|_| plan.merged_at.or(plan.forked_at).unwrap_or(plan.created_at));
441	        let completed_children = plan
442	            .tasks
443	            .iter()
444	            .filter(|task| task.status == PlanTaskStatus::Completed)
445	            .count();
446	        let total_children = plan.tasks.len();
447	        plans.push(PlanListEntry {
448	            plan_id: plan.plan_id,
449	            merged_run_id: plan.merged_run_id,
450	            scope: plan.parent_scope.unwrap_or_else(|| "global".to_string()),
451	            goal: plan.root_goal,
452	            status: plan.status,
453	            mode: plan.mode,
454	            updated_at,
455	            plan_path,
456	            completed_children,
457	            total_children,
458	        });
459	    }
460	    plans.sort_by_key(|plan| Reverse(plan.updated_at));
461	    Ok(plans)
462	}

464	fn plan_action_label(plan: &PlanListEntry) -> String {
465	    match plan.status {
466	        PlanStatus::Pending => "fork".to_string(),
467	        PlanStatus::Forked if plan.completed_children == plan.total_children => {
468	            format!("merge {}/{}", plan.completed_children, plan.total_children)
469	        }
470	        PlanStatus::Forked => format!("attach {}/{}", plan.completed_children, plan.total_children),
471	        PlanStatus::Merged if plan.merged_run_id.is_some() => "finish".to_string(),
472	        PlanStatus::Merged => "show".to_string(),
473	        PlanStatus::Failed => "show failure".to_string(),
474	    }
475	}
```

```text
## Inquire Crate & Windows Support

Inquire chose to support crossterm by default in order to support many features on Windows out-of-the-box. The library supports UNIX and Windows terminals thanks to crossterm.

## Terminal Backend Options

You can choose your terminal backend between crossterm (default), termion or console. This flexibility allows developers to use whichever terminal library their application already depends on.

## Crossterm's Windows Compatibility

Crossterm supports all UNIX and Windows terminals down to Windows 7. This wide compatibility makes it an excellent choice for CLI projects that need cross-platform support.
```

```text
785	        _ => return Err(invalid_history_since_error(pattern, value)),
786	    };
787	    Ok(Some(Utc::now() - duration))
```

```text
pub(crate) async fn start_command(args: StartCommandArgs) -> Result<()> {
    let stdin_is_tty = io::stdin().is_terminal();
    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
    let cwd = std::env::current_dir()?;
    let latest_extendable_run = start_latest_extendable_run(&paths, &cwd)?;
    let mut decision = start_launch_decision(StartLaunchInput {
        goal: &args.goal,
        requested_mode: args.mode,
        stdin_is_tty,
    });
    add_start_history_actions(&mut decision, latest_extendable_run.as_ref());
    let eligibility = StartPromptEligibility::from_args(&args, stdin_is_tty);
    if start_goal_shape_should_classify(&args, eligibility) {
        let defaults = config_defaults(&paths)?;
        let provider = start_goal_shape_provider_route(&paths, &defaults, &args);
        let recommendation = classify_goal_shape_for_start(
            &paths,
            &cwd,
            &args.goal,
            provider.as_deref(),
            args.plain,
        )
        .await;
        let scope = workspace_scope(&cwd)?;
        write_goal_shape_preview_record(&paths, &scope, &recommendation)?;
        apply_goal_shape_recommendation(&mut decision, recommendation);
    }
    let mut terminal_prompter = TerminalStartPrompter;
    if eligibility.allows_prompts() {
        maybe_prompt_start_mode(
            &mut decision,
            &args,
            latest_extendable_run.as_ref(),
            &mut terminal_prompter,
        )?;
        if decision.recovery.is_none() {
            resolve_start_setup(
                &mut decision,
                &args,
                Some(&mut terminal_prompter),
                stdin_is_tty,
            )?;
        }
    } else if decision.recovery.is_none() {
        resolve_start_setup(&mut decision, &args, None, stdin_is_tty)?;
    }
    if args.json {
        let surface = start_preview_surface(&decision, &args, &paths)?;
        let mut next_actions = vec![surface.primary_action.command.clone()];
```

```text
1026	fn parse_library_date_filter(label: &str, value: Option<String>) -> Result<Option<DateTime<Utc>>> {
1027	    let Some(value) = value else {
1028	        return Ok(None);
1029	    };
1030	    if let Ok(date_time) = DateTime::parse_from_rfc3339(&value) {
1031	        return Ok(Some(date_time.with_timezone(&Utc)));
1032	    }
1033	    if let Ok(date) = chrono::NaiveDate::parse_from_str(&value, "%Y-%m-%d") {
1034	        let date_time = if label == "--until" {
1035	            date.and_hms_nano_opt(23, 59, 59, 999_999_999)
1036	        } else {
1037	            date.and_hms_opt(0, 0, 0)
1038	        };
1039	        let Some(date_time) = date_time else {
1040	            return Err(invalid_library_date_error(label, &value));
1041	        };
1042	        return Ok(Some(date_time.and_utc()));
1043	    }
1044	    Err(invalid_library_date_error(label, &value))
1045	}
```

```text
# Inquire: Interactive CLI Prompt Library

## Prompt Types

Inquire provides **8 different prompt types**:

1. **Text** - Standard text input with built-in autocompletion
2. **Select** - Single option selection from a list
3. **MultiSelect** - Multiple option selection from a list
4. **Confirm** - Yes/no confirmation prompts
5. **Password** - Secretive text input
6. **CustomType** - Parse user input to custom types (numbers, UUIDs, etc.)
7. **DateSelect** - Interactive calendar for date selection
8. **Editor** - Open text editor for longer text inputs

## Feature Support

**Fuzzy Filtering:** Yes. The library uses "SkimV2 from fuzzy_matcher" for default scoring in Select and MultiSelect prompts, enabling fuzzy searching.

**Validation:** Yes. "Almost all prompts provide an API to set custom validators" that return validation results with custom error messages.

**Autocomplete:** Yes. Text prompts support autocompletion through the `Autocomplete` trait with customizable suggestion and completion methods.

**Back/Cancel (ESC):** Yes. Users can "cancel the prompt before submitting a response" by pressing Ctrl-C or ESC, returning `InquireError::OperationCanceled`.

## Notable Projects Using Inquire

The documentation provided does not list specific projects using inquire. The page includes a stargazer chart but doesn't mention any notable adopters by name.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about dialoguer and inquire:

## Dialoguer

Dialoguer is a library for Rust that helps you build useful small interactive user inputs for the command line, providing utilities to render various simple dialogs like confirmation prompts, text inputs and more.

## Inquire

Inquire provides several different prompts in order to interactively ask the user for information via the CLI. With inquire, you can use: Text to get text input from the user with built-in autocompletion support; Editor to get longer text inputs by opening a text editor; DateSelect to get a date input via an interactive calendar; Select to ask the user to select one option from a list; and MultiSelect for selecting multiple options.

## Usage in Notable CLI Tools

The search results show that both libraries are part of the Rust CLI ecosystem. Dialoguer and inquire are among different command line prompt crates used in Rust projects.

## Related Tools

Cargo-edit is a tool that adds missing commands to Cargo, Rust's package manager, and lets you add or remove project dependencies and update them to the latest versions without manually editing configuration files.
```

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 03:29:16Z)**_

Research complete. I inspected DeadReckon's actual styling implementation before evaluating the crates.

Key findings:
- DeadReckon hand-rolls ANSI escapes for line-mode output in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/ui.rs` (a `Stream`/`Tone` model with `ansi_wrap`), with its own `enabled()` gate already honoring `NO_COLOR`, `TERM=dumb`, an explicit plain-output flag, and `is_terminal`. The TUI uses ratatui `Style`/`Color`. So the styled-output category maps onto only that ~40-line line-mode layer, not the TUI.
- All six crates were evaluated for whether they conflict/duplicate/layer cleanly against the existing ratatui 0.29 + crossterm 0.29 stack.

Recommendation delivered: keep the existing hand-rolled layer, or — if replacing it — adopt **anstyle + anstream** (already pulled transitively via clap, maintained by the clap/cargo author, and the only option that meaningfully improves DeadReckon's weak Windows non-TUI output via wincon, with a one-line caveat about avoiding double VT-enable between crossterm and anstream on Windows). **owo-colors** is the lighter ergonomic alternative if Windows console-API support isn't needed. Flagged **console** (duplicates crossterm; the console/dialoguer family is deliberately avoided in this project), **termcolor** (stagnant, ecosystem migrating off it), and **nu-ansi-term** (tiny, nushell-internal, no auto-detection) as poor fits.

Full structured analysis with per-crate health, Windows support, and composition notes was returned via StructuredOutput.

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 03:29:31Z)**_

I've completed the audit of the attach-tui slice. The structured findings cover all six files in scope. Key takeaways:

- **Per-surface divergence is the dominant problem**: run, plan, campaign, and chain attach each re-implement navigation, footers, selection markers, and empty states differently (three glyphs, four footer styles, two border-color sources, two narrative split breakpoints).
- **Navigation inconsistency**: run panels (attach_state.rs) support full paging (Tab/PgUp/PgDn/Home/End/g/G); the plan loop and campaign handler omit paging keys.
- **Silent no-ops and side effects**: `r`/`v` silently flip view to Narrative; Enter on an unloadable child run does nothing despite footers promising "Enter child run"; provider-refresh failures truncate away the actionable hint narrative.rs generated.

```text
## Jujutsu (jj)

Jujutsu is an experimental version control system, available as the `jj-cli` crate on crates.io.

## anstyle and Terminal Styling Crates

anstyle provides core types describing ANSI styling escape codes for interoperability between crates. This allows a crate to provide an API for customizing the colors used without putting the underlying text styling crate in the API.

The anstyle ecosystem is comprehensive for Rust CLI applications. The AnStyle ecosystem is a collection of Rust crates designed to provide a uniform approach to terminal styling across different platforms and handles ANSI terminal styling in a cross-platform manner.

Key components of the ecosystem include:

- The anstyle crate provides the fundamental building blocks for terminal styling by defining data structures and methods for representing ANSI text styles, colors, and effects.
- The anstream crate provides the ability to write styled text to terminals across different platforms, automatically adapting to terminal capabilities.
- anstyle-parse parses ANSI style escapes, colorchoice provides global override of color control, and anstyle-query looks up colored console capabilities.

The anstyle-lossy crate provides mechanisms for converting between different ANSI color representations with a focus on practicality, enabling conversion when exact matches are not possible, with the term "lossy" indicating that conversions may sacrifice some color precision to enable compatibility.
```

```text
Based on the search results, here's what I found about the comparison between unicode-width and unicode-segmentation for Ratatui terminal width handling:

## Current Usage in Ratatui

Ratatui uses the unicode-width crate to calculate the width of characters, and rendering handles Unicode grapheme clusters via the unicode-segmentation crate. Both crates are currently used in Ratatui's text handling system.

## Key Differences and Issues

The crates serve different purposes:

- **unicode-width**: Determines displayed width of char and str types according to Unicode Standard Annex #11 and other portions of the Unicode standard
- **unicode-segmentation**: Provides Grapheme Cluster, Word and Sentence boundaries according to Unicode Standard Annex #29 rules

## Known Challenges

There are ongoing discussions about width calculation accuracy. UnicodeWidthStr::width counts newlines as one unit which is not what we want for terminal rendering, and unicode-width doesn't (or can't?) report the column width for emojis.

## Maintenance Status

The search results don't provide specific 2025 maintenance information for either crate. However, The computed width values may not match the actual rendered column width, which indicates both crates have known limitations for terminal UI purposes.

For the most current maintenance status, you would need to check the GitHub repositories directly (unicode-rs/unicode-width and unicode-rs/unicode-segmentation).
```

Research complete. Summary of findings for the "tables-structured" category:

**Current state:** DeadReckon (`crates/deadreckon/Cargo.toml`, workspace at `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/Cargo.toml`) depends on ratatui 0.29 + crossterm 0.29, no table crate. Plain columnar output is hand-rolled in `crates/deadreckon/src/ui.rs` (manual terminal-width detection + padding), and notably there is **no `unicode-width` dependency anywhere** — so wide-char/CJK alignment is currently best-effort.

**Key data points:**
- **comfy-table** — 1.4k stars, v7.2.2 (2026-01-13). The standout compose finding: it pins `crossterm ^0.29` (optional, only with the `tty` feature) + `unicode-width ^0.2` — the *exact* crossterm version DeadReckon already uses, so no duplicate tree. Added without `tty`, it's a pure deterministic String formatter with correct grapheme/CJK width handling. Caveat: officially "feature freeze / seeking maintainer," but still gets dep bumps.
- **tabled** — 2.3k stars, v0.21.0 (2026-05-31), healthiest maintenance; no crossterm dep; heavier and faster-churning pre-1.0 API. Best if struct-derive tables are wanted.
- **term-table** — 85 stars, dormant since v1.4.0 (2024-07-14), no documented Unicode-width correctness. Avoid.
- **cli-table** — 130 stars, v0.5.0 (2025-03-18), lightly maintained, no documented wrapping/plain/Unicode-width story. Avoid.
- **ratatui Table widget** — already in-tree, native for the attach TUI, but only renders into a frame Buffer; it is NOT a plain-text emitter (you'd have to scrape a `Buffer::empty(Rect)` manually).

**Recommendation:** Per-surface split — keep ratatui Table for TUI frames; for plain/no-TTY columnar output, reach for **comfy-table** (no-`tty`, borderless preset) if/when the hand-rolled width math in `ui.rs` starts producing CJK/wrapping bugs, since it's the only candidate that's both width-correct and crossterm-0.29-compatible. tabled is the fallback only if struct-derive ergonomics are needed. Based on the search results, here's information about gitui's Rust crate dependencies related to ratatui, crossterm, tui-rs, and styling:

```text
## GitUI Dependencies

GitUI uses ratatui as its Terminal UI framework and crossterm for cross-platform terminal manipulation, along with git2 for Git operations.

## Relationship Between Key Dependencies

**Ratatui and tui-rs**: Ratatui was forked from the tui-rs crate in 2023 in order to continue its development. Ratatui is the active continuation of tui-rs.

**Ratatui and Crossterm**: Ratatui uses Crossterm by default as it works on most platforms. The crossterm feature enables the CrosstermBackend backend and adds a dependency on crossterm.

## Styling Support

Ratatui provides UI widgets for building a TUI — things like laying out your UI, tabs, tables, scrollbars, and the like. Ratatui focuses on the UI aspects, and leverages other crates for the low level terminal interaction.

For styling specifically, the underline-color feature enables the backend code that sets the underline color, which is only supported by the Crossterm and Termwiz backends, and is not supported on Windows 7.
```

Research complete. Summary of findings for the ratatui-ecosystem category:

**Codebase reality (verified):** DeadReckon already hand-rolls its CLI prompts in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/prompt.rs` — a raw-mode arrow/number select menu plus confirm, built directly on crossterm 0.29, with a line-mode fallback gated on `is_terminal()` and `DEADRECKON_PROMPT_LINE_MODE`. The persistent ratatui draw loop lives only in the attach TUI (`src/tui/`, `commands/attach*.rs`), not the prompt path.

**The dominant finding — a version cliff:** The ratatui ecosystem moved to **ratatui 0.30** (split into ratatui-core/ratatui-widgets) by early 2026. The *latest* release of essentially every widget crate now requires ratatui ^0.30 and will not compile against DeadReckon's 0.29. The 0.29-compatible pins are: tui-input 0.14.0, tui-prompts 0.5.x, tui-popup 0.6.0, throbber-widgets-tui 0.8.0, tui-textarea 0.7.0. So adopting any current widget crate effectively forces a ratatui 0.30 migration.

**Per-crate verdicts:**
- **inquire** — best version match (crossterm ^0.29, the exact dep already present; crossterm-default; 2.6k stars; active) but renders its own theme, breaking DeadReckon's uniform hand-rolled identity.
- **dialoguer** — drags in the `console` crate as a *second* terminal stack beside crossterm, worsening the known Windows weak spot. Poor fit.
- **tui-prompts / tui-popup** — assume a ratatui Frame loop; wrong rendering model for one-shot prompts; both moved to ratatui 0.30.
- **throbber-widgets-tui** — trivial spinner, trivially hand-rollable; latest needs ratatui 0.30.
- **tui-textarea** — release-stale (0.7.0, Oct 2024), only lists crossterm 0.25/0.28, overkill (no multi-line surface exists).
- **tui-input** — the one keeper-on-shortlist: state-only, lets DeadReckon keep rendering by hand; pin 0.14.0 for ratatui 0.29 if a real editable text field is ever needed.

**Recommendation:** Keep prompts hand-rolled; adopt nothing now. The existing prompt.rs satisfies the need, and every external option violates either the uniform-output principle or the no-duplicate-terminal-stack principle. The real prerequisite decision is a deliberate ratatui 0.29→0.30 upgrade. Full structured detail returned via StructuredOutput.

```text
## Atuin Overview

Atuin replaces your existing shell history with a SQLite database, and records additional context for your commands. Additionally, it provides optional and fully encrypted synchronisation of your history between machines, via an Atuin server.

## Ratatui and Crossterm

Ratatui provides UI widgets for building a TUI — things like laying out your UI, tabs, tables, scrollbars, and the like. Ratatui focuses on the UI aspects, and leverages other crates for the low level terminal interaction.

Crossterm is a backend for the Ratatui Terminal UI library that uses the Crossterm library for all terminal manipulation.

## Integration for Interactive Functionality

Atuin can rebind ctrl-r and up (configurable) to a full screen history search UI, which would likely leverage Ratatui and Crossterm to create the interactive search interface. The combination of these libraries allows Atuin to provide an interactive, full-screen terminal-based history search experience.

The search results confirm that Ratatui and Crossterm are commonly used together for building interactive terminal UIs in Rust, making them ideal dependencies for Atuin's search functionality.
```

```text
## supports-color Crate

The supports-color crate detects whether a terminal supports color and gives details about that support, taking into account the NO_COLOR environment variable. This crate is a Rust port of @sindresorhus' NPM package by the same name.

## anstyle-query Crate

The anstyle-query crate is designed to look up colored console capabilities. It provides detection of terminal capabilities, and the AnStyle ecosystem respects environment variables like NO_COLOR.

## Key Differences

The main difference is their scope and ecosystem integration:

- **supports-color**: A focused, standalone crate specifically for color support detection with NO_COLOR support
- **anstyle-query**: Part of the larger AnStyle ecosystem for comprehensive terminal styling solutions across multiple crates
```

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 03:30:16Z)**_

Research complete. Key findings for the "prompts-menus" category:

**Composability is the deciding axis.** DeadReckon pins crossterm 0.29 + ratatui 0.29 and currently hand-rolls prompts in `/Users/gdc/deadreckon/crates/deadreckon/src/prompt.rs` (`select_one`, `open` over raw crossterm key events).

- **inquire** — crossterm 0.29 is its *default and only-default* backend (exact match, zero duplicate stack), best Windows support, full feature set (select/multiselect/CustomType numeric/validators/fuzzy/autocomplete/ESC-cancel), healthiest maintenance. The clear pick *if* a crate is adopted.
- **dialoguer** & **demand** — both built on the `console` crate, not crossterm. They'd graft a *second* terminal backend onto a codebase that deliberately standardized on crossterm. Flagged against.
- **requestty** — crossterm 0.29-native but near-dormant (24k recent downloads, 1 open issue, no activity since Dec 2025). Maintenance risk.
- **promkit** — crossterm 0.29-native but heavyweight: forces mandatory tokio + rayon + its own widget framework, churny 0.x API. Overkill.

**Overall recommendation:** Given DeadReckon's byte-exact render tests (`navigable_tests.rs`, `effortless_consistency_tests.rs`) and hand-rolled uniform surface (`ui.rs`, `ui_card.rs`, `verdict_surface.rs`, `friendliness_contract.rs`), the most consistent move is to keep the hand-rolled prompts. Any prompt crate brings its own theming engine and owns the terminal in raw mode — it can only replace standalone prompts, not embed in the ratatui attach TUI, and would diverge from the bespoke style. If a real gap appears (fuzzy filter, calendar), reach for inquire pieces behind a thin adapter with a custom RenderConfig. Definitely avoid dialoguer/demand's console backend.
