2212	async fn compose_dependency_source_dir(
2213	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
2214	    plan: &Plan,
2215	    task: &PlanTask,
2216	    dependencies: &[PlanDependencyArtifact],
2217	    repair: DependencyComposeRepair<'_>,
2218	) -> Result<PathBuf> {
2219	    let source_dir = paths
2220	        .plan_dir(&plan.plan_id)
2221	        .join("launch")
2222	        .join(&task.task_id)
2223	        .join("source");
2224	    let sources = dependencies
2225	        .iter()
2226	        .map(|dependency| ComposeFileSource {
2227	            root: dependency.root.clone(),
2228	            data: dependency.clone(),
2229	            prefix_error: "dependency source prefix error",
2230	        })
2231	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
2232	    let conflicts = compose_merge_sources(
2233	        &source_dir,
2234	        &sources,
2235	        |dependency, _relative, file, hash| PlanMergeSeenFile {
2236	            task_id: dependency.task_id.clone(),
2237	            task_index: dependency.index,
2238	            run_id: dependency.run_id.clone(),
2239	            artifact_root: dependency.root.clone(),
2240	            artifact_path: file.to_path_buf(),
2241	            hash,
2242	        },
2243	        |relative, previous, current| {
2244	            if plan_task_depends_on(plan, &current.task_id, &previous.task_id) {
2245	                ComposeMergeDecision::UseCurrent
2246	            } else if plan_task_depends_on(plan, &previous.task_id, &current.task_id) {
2247	                ComposeMergeDecision::KeepExisting
2248	            } else {
2249	                ComposeMergeDecision::RecordConflict {
2250	                    conflict: plan_merge_conflict(plan, relative, previous, current, None),
2251	                    use_current: false,
2252	                }
2253	            }
2254	        },
2255	    )?;
2256	    if !conflicts.is_empty() {
2257	        repair_dependency_source_conflicts(
2258	            paths,
2259	            plan,
2260	            task,
2261	            repair,
2262	            source_dir.clone(),
2263	            conflicts,
2264	        )
2265	        .await?;
2266	    }
2267	    Ok(source_dir)
2268	}
2269	
2270	async fn repair_dependency_source_conflicts(
2271	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
2272	    plan: &Plan,
2273	    task: &PlanTask,
2274	    repair: DependencyComposeRepair<'_>,
2275	    source_dir: PathBuf,
2276	    conflicts: Vec<PlanMergeConflict>,
2277	) -> Result<()> {
2278	    let mut merge = PlanMergeOutcome {
2279	        working_dir: source_dir,
2280	        conflicts,
2281	    };
2282	    let unresolved_conflicts = merge.unresolved_conflicts();
2283	    let context = MergeRepairContext::dependency(paths, plan, task);
2284	    write_plan_merge_conflicts_to(
2285	        &context.proof_dir,
2286	        plan,
2287	        "dependency-compose",
2288	        &unresolved_conflicts,
2289	    )?;
2290	    let worker_spec = render_launch_worker_spec(paths, plan, task);
2291	    write_worker_spec(paths, &plan.plan_id, &task.task_id, &worker_spec)?;
2292	    let provider = if repair.disabled {
2293	        None
2294	    } else {
2295	        resolve_merge_repair_provider(paths, plan, repair.provider)?
2296	    };
2297	    write_merge_repair_request(
2298	        paths,
2299	        plan,
2300	        &context,
2301	        provider.as_deref(),
2302	        &unresolved_conflicts,
2303	    )?;
2304	    if repair.disabled {
2305	        return Err(dependency_source_conflict_error(
2306	            task,
2307	            &unresolved_conflicts,
2308	            &format!(
2309	                "automatic repair disabled; inspect {}",
2310	                context.proof_dir.join("conflicts.json").display()
2311	            ),
2312	        ));
2313	    }
2314	    append_plan_event(
2315	        paths,
2316	        &plan.plan_id,
2317	        PlanEventKind::MergeConflict {
2318	            conflict_count: unresolved_conflicts.len(),
2319	        },
2320	    )?;
2321	    append_plan_event(
2322	        paths,
2323	        &plan.plan_id,
2324	        PlanEventKind::MergeRepairPlanned {
2325	            conflict_count: unresolved_conflicts.len(),
2326	            provider: provider.clone(),
2327	        },
2328	    )?;
2329	    let Some(provider) = provider else {
2330	        let reason = format!(
2331	            "dependency merge repair for {} needs a configured provider",
2332	            task.task_id
2333	        );
2334	        append_plan_event(
2335	            paths,
2336	            &plan.plan_id,
2337	            PlanEventKind::MergeRepairFailed {
2338	                reason: reason.clone(),
2339	            },
2340	        )?;
2341	        return Err(CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
2342	            &format!("{reason}; conflicts remain"),
2343	            "deadreckon providers list --all",
2344	        )));
2345	    };
2346	    append_plan_event(
2347	        paths,
2348	        &plan.plan_id,
2349	        PlanEventKind::MergeRepairStarted {
2350	            mode: MergeRepairMode::Auto.as_str().to_string(),
2351	        },
2352	    )?;
2353	    match run_merge_repair(
2354	        paths,
2355	        plan,
2356	        &context,
2357	        &MergeRepairOptions {
2358	            provider: &provider,
2359	            mode: MergeRepairMode::Auto,
2360	            attempts: 1,
2361	            quiet: repair.quiet,
2362	        },
2363	        &mut merge,
2364	    )
2365	    .await
2366	    {
2367	        Ok(repaired) => {
2368	            append_plan_event(
2369	                paths,
2370	                &plan.plan_id,
2371	                PlanEventKind::MergeRepaired {
2372	                    strategy: format!("dependency-{}", repaired.strategy),
2373	                    repair_run_id: repaired.repair_run_id,
2374	                },
2375	            )?;
2376	            write_plan_merge_conflicts_to(
2377	                &context.proof_dir,
2378	                plan,
2379	                "dependency-compose",
2380	                &merge.conflicts,
2381	            )?;
2382	            Ok(())
2383	        }
2384	        Err(error) => {
2385	            let reason = error.to_string();
2386	            append_plan_event(
2387	                paths,
2388	                &plan.plan_id,
2389	                PlanEventKind::MergeRepairFailed { reason },
2390	            )?;
2391	            Err(error)
2392	        }
2393	    }
2394	}

2396	fn dependency_source_conflict_error(
2397	    task: &PlanTask,
2398	    conflicts: &[PlanMergeConflict],
2399	    hint: &str,
2400	) -> CliError {
2401	    let paths = conflicts
2402	        .iter()

2404	        .collect::<Vec<_>>()
2405	        .join(", ");
2406	    CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(

2415	pub(crate) fn plan_task_depends_on(plan: &Plan, task_id: &str, dependency_id: &str) -> bool {
2416	    let mut stack = vec![task_id.to_string()];
2417	    let mut seen = BTreeSet::new();
2418	    while let Some(next) = stack.pop() {
2419	        if !seen.insert(next.clone()) {
2420	            continue;
2421	        }
2422	        let Some(task) = plan.task_by_id(&next) else {
2423	            continue;
2424	        };
2425	        if task
2426	            .depends_on
2427	            .iter()
2428	            .any(|dependency| dependency == dependency_id)
2429	        {
2430	            return true;
2431	        }
2432	        stack.extend(task.depends_on.iter().cloned());
2433	    }
2434	    false
2435	}

2437	struct PlanChildLaunch<'a> {
2438	    paths: &'a DeadreckonPaths,
2439	    plan: &'a Plan,
2440	    task_index: usize,
2441	    source_dir: &'a Path,
2442	    sandbox: &'a str,
2443	    max_spend: Option<f64>,
2444	    max_wall_seconds: Option<f64>,
2445	    quiet: bool,
2446	    plain: bool,
2447	    forward_output: bool,
2448	    signal_sender: Option<std::sync::mpsc::Sender<PlanChildSignal>>,
2449	}
2450	
2451	fn run_plan_child(launch: PlanChildLaunch<'_>) -> Result<String> {
2452	    let PlanChildLaunch {
2453	        paths,
2454	        plan,
2455	        task_index,
2456	        source_dir,
2457	        sandbox,
2458	        max_spend,
2459	        max_wall_seconds,
2460	        quiet,
2461	        plain,
2462	        forward_output,
2463	        signal_sender,
2464	    } = launch;
2465	    let task = &plan.tasks[task_index];
2466	    let worker_spec_path = paths.worker_spec(&plan.plan_id, &task.task_id);
2467	    let worker_spec = render_launch_worker_spec(paths, plan, task);
2468	    write_worker_spec(paths, &plan.plan_id, &task.task_id, &worker_spec)?;
2469	    let prompt = plan_child_prompt(plan, task, &worker_spec, &worker_spec_path);
2470	    let launch_dir = paths
2471	        .plan_dir(&plan.plan_id)
2472	        .join("launch")
2473	        .join(&task.task_id);
2474	    fs::create_dir_all(&launch_dir)?;
2475	
2476	    let mut command = std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe()?);
2477	    command
2478	        .current_dir(source_dir)
2479	        .env("DEADRECKON_HOME", paths.home())
2480	        .env("DEADRECKON_HINTS", "0")
2481	        .env("DEADRECKON_SCOPE_ROOT", &launch_dir);
2482	    let review_parent_run_id = review_parent_run_id(plan, task);
2483	    if let Some(parent_run_id) = review_parent_run_id.as_deref() {
2484	        command
2485	            .arg("extend")
2486	            .arg(parent_run_id)
2487	            .arg(prompt)
2488	            .arg("--no-docs");
2489	    } else {
2490	        command
2491	            .arg("run")
2492	            .arg(prompt)
2493	            .arg("--from")
2494	            .arg(source_dir)
2495	            .arg("--yes")
2496	            .arg("--no-confirm")
2497	            .arg("--no-hints")
2498	            .arg("--no-docs");
2499	        if plain {
2500	            command.arg("--plain");
2501	        }
2502	        if let Some(acceptance_path) = plan.acceptance_path.as_deref() {
2503	            command.arg("--acceptance").arg(acceptance_path);
2504	        }
2505	    }
2506	    command.arg("--sandbox").arg(sandbox);
2507	    if let Some(max_spend) = max_spend {
2508	        command.arg("--max-spend").arg(format!("{max_spend:.6}"));
2509	    }
2510	    if let Some(max_wall_seconds) = max_wall_seconds {
2511	        command
2512	            .arg("--max-wall-seconds")
2513	            .arg(max_wall_seconds.to_string());
2514	    }
2515	    if task
2516	        .provider
2517	        .as_deref()
2518	        .is_some_and(|provider| provider == "smoke" || provider.starts_with("smoke:"))
2519	    {
2520	        if review_parent_run_id.is_some() {
2521	            command.arg("--provider").arg("smoke");
2522	        } else {
2523	            command.arg("--smoke");
2524	        }
2525	    } else if let Some(provider) = task.provider.as_deref() {
2526	        command.arg("--provider").arg(provider);
2527	    }
2528	    command
2529	        .stdout(std::process::Stdio::piped())
2530	        .stderr(std::process::Stdio::piped());
2531	    let mut child = command.spawn()?;
2532	    if let Some(sender) = signal_sender.as_ref() {
2533	        let _ = sender.send(PlanChildSignal::Pid {
2534	            task_index,
2535	            pid: child.id(),
2536	        });
2537	    } else {
2538	        write_coordinator_snapshot(paths, plan, Some((task_index, child.id())))?;
2539	    }
2540	    let stdout = child.stdout.take().ok_or_else(|| {
2541	        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
2542	            "failed to capture child stdout".to_string(),
2543	        ))
2544	    })?;
2545	    let stderr = child.stderr.take().ok_or_else(|| {
2546	        CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(
2547	            "failed to capture child stderr".to_string(),
2548	        ))
2549	    })?;
2550	    let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel::<(bool, String)>();
2551	    let stdout_thread = commands::chain::spawn_chain_step_reader(stdout, true, tx.clone());
2552	    let stderr_thread = commands::chain::spawn_chain_step_reader(stderr, false, tx);
2553	    let mut stdout_text = String::new();
2554	    let mut stderr_text = String::new();
2555	    let mut live_run_id = None;
2556	    let suppress_child_output = quiet || !forward_output;
2557	    let status = loop {
2558	        while let Ok((is_stdout, line)) = rx.try_recv() {
2559	            if let Some(run_id) = commands::chain::capture_chain_step_output(
2560	                is_stdout,
2561	                &line,
2562	                &mut stdout_text,
2563	                &mut stderr_text,
2564	                suppress_child_output,
2565	            )? {
2566	                note_plan_child_run_id(
2567	                    &launch_dir,
2568	                    signal_sender.as_ref(),
2569	                    task_index,
2570	                    &mut live_run_id,
2571	                    run_id,
2572	                );
2573	            }
2574	        }
2575	        if let Some(status) = child.try_wait()? {
2576	            break status;
2577	        }
2578	        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
2579	    };
2580	    let _ = stdout_thread.join();
2581	    let _ = stderr_thread.join();
2582	    while let Ok((is_stdout, line)) = rx.try_recv() {
2583	        if let Some(run_id) = commands::chain::capture_chain_step_output(
2584	            is_stdout,
2585	            &line,
2586	            &mut stdout_text,
2587	            &mut stderr_text,
2588	            suppress_child_output,
2589	        )? {
2590	            note_plan_child_run_id(
2591	                &launch_dir,
2592	                signal_sender.as_ref(),
2593	                task_index,
2594	                &mut live_run_id,
2595	                run_id,
2596	            );
2597	        }
2598	    }
2599	    let run_id = live_run_id.or_else(|| commands::chain::parse_started_run_id(&stdout_text));
2600	    if let Some(run_id) = run_id.as_ref() {
2601	        let _ = fs::write(launch_dir.join("run-id"), run_id);
2602	        if let Some(sender) = signal_sender.as_ref() {
2603	            let _ = sender.send(PlanChildSignal::RunId {
2604	                task_index,
2605	                run_id: run_id.clone(),
2606	            });
2607	        }
2608	    }
2609	    if !status.success() {
2610	        return Err(CliError::Core(DeadreckonError::InvalidInput(format!(
2611	            "child {} failed: {}{}",
2612	            task.task_id, stdout_text, stderr_text
2613	        ))));
2614	    }
2615	    run_id.ok_or_else(|| {
2616	        CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
2617	            &format!("could not find run id for child {}", task.task_id),
2618	            "deadreckon list",
2619	        ))
2620	    })
2621	}
2622	
2623	fn note_plan_child_run_id(
2624	    launch_dir: &Path,
2625	    sender: Option<&std::sync::mpsc::Sender<PlanChildSignal>>,
2626	    task_index: usize,
2627	    live_run_id: &mut Option<String>,
2628	    run_id: String,
2629	) {
2630	    if live_run_id.as_deref() == Some(run_id.as_str()) {
2631	        return;
2632	    }
2633	    let _ = fs::write(launch_dir.join("run-id"), &run_id);
2634	    if let Some(sender) = sender {
2635	        let _ = sender.send(PlanChildSignal::RunId {
2636	            task_index,
2637	            run_id: run_id.clone(),
2638	        });
2639	    }
2640	    *live_run_id = Some(run_id);
2641	}

2650	        .and_then(|parent_task| parent_task.child_run_id.clone())

2740	fn mark_blocked_pending_tasks(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, plan: &mut Plan) -> Result<()> {
2741	    let completed = plan
2742	        .tasks
2743	        .iter()
2744	        .filter(|task| task.status == PlanTaskStatus::Completed)
2745	        .map(|task| task.task_id.clone())
2746	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
2747	    let blockers = plan
2748	        .tasks
2749	        .iter()
2750	        .filter(|task| task.status != PlanTaskStatus::Completed)
2751	        .map(|task| task.task_id.clone())
2752	        .collect::<BTreeSet<_>>();
2753	    let pending = plan
2754	        .tasks
2755	        .iter()
2756	        .enumerate()
2757	        .filter(|(_, task)| task.status == PlanTaskStatus::Pending)
2758	        .map(|(index, _)| index)
2759	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
2760	    for index in pending {
2761	        let missing = plan.tasks[index]
2762	            .depends_on
2763	            .iter()
2764	            .filter(|dependency| !completed.contains(*dependency))
2765	            .cloned()
2766	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
2767	        let blocked_by = missing
2768	            .iter()
2769	            .filter(|dependency| blockers.contains(*dependency))
2770	            .cloned()
2771	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
2772	        let task_id = plan.tasks[index].task_id.clone();
2773	        plan.tasks[index].status = PlanTaskStatus::Failed;
2774	        append_plan_event(
2775	            paths,
2776	            &plan.plan_id,
2777	            PlanEventKind::TaskBlocked {
2778	                task_id: task_id.clone(),
2779	                task_index: index,
2780	                reason: format!(
2781	                    "missing dependencies: {}",
2782	                    if missing.is_empty() {
2783	                        "unknown".to_string()
2784	                    } else {
2785	                        missing.join(", ")
2786	                    }
2787	                ),
2788	            },
2789	        )?;
2790	        append_plan_message(
2791	            paths,
2792	            &plan.plan_id,
2793	            &PlanMessage::new(
2794	                "coordinator",
2795	                &task_id,
2796	                PlanMessageKind::Blocker,
2797	                format!("{task_id} blocked"),
2798	                json!({ "missing_dependencies": missing, "blocked_by": blocked_by }),
2799	            )?,
2800	        )?;
2801	    }
2802	    Ok(())
2803	}
2804	
2805	fn mark_failed_fork_plan_terminal(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, plan: &mut Plan) -> Result<()> {
2806	    let all_terminal = plan.tasks.iter().all(|task| {
2807	        !matches!(
2808	            task.status,
2809	            PlanTaskStatus::Pending | PlanTaskStatus::Running
2810	        )
2811	    });
2812	    let has_failure = plan
2813	        .tasks
2814	        .iter()
2815	        .any(|task| matches!(task.status, PlanTaskStatus::Failed | PlanTaskStatus::Killed));
2816	    if all_terminal && has_failure && plan.status != PlanStatus::Failed {
2817	        plan.status = PlanStatus::Failed;
2818	        append_plan_event(
2819	            paths,
2820	            &plan.plan_id,
2821	            PlanEventKind::PlanFailed {
2822	                reason: "one or more child tasks failed or were blocked".to_string(),
2823	            },
2824	        )?;
2825	    }
2826	    Ok(())
2827	}

2829	fn print_fork_finished(plan: &Plan, no_hints: bool) {
2830	    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
2831	    println!(
2832	        "{}",

3432	fn chain_step_glyph(status: ChainStepStatus, plain: bool) -> &'static str {

3440	        (ChainStepStatus::Failed, false) => "✗",
3441	        (ChainStepStatus::Failed, true) => "x",
3442	        (ChainStepStatus::Skipped, false) => "↷",
3443	        (ChainStepStatus::Skipped, true) => "~",
3444	        (ChainStepStatus::Applied, false) => "◉",
3445	        (ChainStepStatus::Applied, true) => "*",
3446	        (ChainStepStatus::Undone, false) => "↶",
3447	        (ChainStepStatus::Undone, true) => "<",
3448	    }
3449	}

86	impl Status {
87	    pub(crate) fn classify(status: &str) -> Status {
88	        let status = status.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
89	        if status.contains("failed")
90	            || status.contains("killed")
91	            || status.contains("error")
92	            || status.contains("missing")
93	            || status.contains("refused")
94	        {
95	            return Status::Negative;
96	        }
97	        if status.contains("paused") {
98	            return Status::Paused;
99	        }
100	        if status.contains("warning") || status.contains("warn") {
101	            return Status::Warn;
102	        }
103	        match status.as_str() {
104	            "ok" | "ready" | "set" | "wrote" | "updated" | "installed" | "completed" | "passed"
105	            | "polished" | "applied" | "cleaned" | "exported" => Status::Ok,
106	            "running" => Status::Running,
107	            "pending" | "planned" | "skipped" | "undone" | "recorded" | "note" => Status::Note,
108	            _ => Status::Unknown,
109	        }
110	    }

116	            Status::Paused => Tone::Paused,
117	            Status::Warn => Tone::Warn,
118	            Status::Negative => Tone::Negative,
119	            Status::Note => Tone::Note,
120	            // Unknown stays a visible default rather than a dim that hides it.
121	            Status::Unknown => Tone::Plain,
122	        }
123	    }

179	pub(crate) fn render(stream: Stream, tone: Tone, text: impl AsRef<str>) -> String {
180	    let text = text.as_ref();
181	    let Some(code) = tone.to_ansi() else {
182	        return text.to_string();
183	    };
184	    if enabled(stream) {
185	        ansi_wrap(code, text)
186	    } else {
187	        text.to_string()
188	    }
189	}

191	pub(crate) fn ansi_wrap(code: &str, text: &str) -> String {
192	    format!("\x1b[{code}m{text}{ANSI_RESET}")
193	}

196	pub(crate) fn ansi_reset() -> &'static str {
197	    ANSI_RESET

200	#[allow(dead_code)]
201	pub(crate) fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
202	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
203	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
204	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
205	        if read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars).is_some() {
206	            continue;
207	        }
208	        out.push(ch);
209	    }
210	    out
211	}

213	#[allow(dead_code)]
214	pub(crate) fn read_ansi_sequence<I>(first: char, chars: &mut Peekable<I>) -> Option<(String, bool)>
215	where
216	    I: Iterator<Item = char>,
217	{
218	    if first != ANSI_ESC || chars.peek() != Some(&'[') {
219	        return None;
220	    }
221	    let mut sequence = String::from(first);
222	    if let Some(bracket) = chars.next() {
223	        sequence.push(bracket);
224	    }
225	    for code in chars.by_ref() {
226	        sequence.push(code);
227	        if code.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
228	            let active = sequence != ANSI_RESET;
229	            return Some((sequence, active));
230	        }
231	    }
232	    Some((sequence, false))
233	}

235	/// Display width of `text` in terminal columns: ANSI escape sequences are
236	/// stripped first, then each glyph is measured by its Unicode display width so
237	/// wide (CJK / full-width) glyphs count as two columns and zero-width / combining
238	/// marks count as zero. This is the single width function behind every pad,
239	/// truncate, and column-alignment site.
240	#[allow(dead_code)] // used by ui_card today; kv_block/columns/prompt sites adopt it in later phases.
241	pub(crate) fn display_width(text: &str) -> usize {
242	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr;
243	    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(text).as_str())
244	}
245	
246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

314	/// Color the leading status token of `value` (e.g. `PASSED` in `PASSED 1/1`,
315	/// `completed` in `completed -> done`) by its status tone, leaving the rest
316	/// plain. A value whose leading token is not a recognized status is returned
317	/// unchanged. Safe for an unpadded (last-column / kv) value.
318	#[allow(dead_code)]
319	pub(crate) fn color_status_word(value: &str) -> String {
320	    let mut parts = value.splitn(2, ' ');
321	    let Some(first) = parts.next() else {
322	        return value.to_string();
323	    };
324	    let tone = status_tone(first);
325	    if tone == Tone::Plain {
326	        return value.to_string();
327	    }
328	    match parts.next() {
329	        Some(rest) => format!("{} {}", render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first), rest),
330	        None => render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first),
331	    }
332	}

426	fn stream_is_terminal(stream: Stream) -> bool {
427	    match stream {
428	        Stream::Stdout => io::stdout().is_terminal(),
429	        Stream::Stderr => io::stderr().is_terminal(),
430	    }

433	fn current_terminal_width() -> usize {
434	    crossterm::terminal::size()
435	        .ok()
436	        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
437	        .or_else(|| {
438	            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
439	                .ok()
440	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
441	        })
442	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 0)
443	        .unwrap_or(120)
444	}

446	fn replacement_line_text(text: &str, terminal_width: usize) -> String {
447	    let visible_limit = terminal_width.saturating_sub(1);
448	    truncate_visible_single_line(text, visible_limit)
449	}
450	
451	fn truncate_visible_single_line(text: &str, max_visible: usize) -> String {
452	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
453	    if max_visible == 0 {
454	        return String::new();
455	    }
456	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len().min(max_visible));
457	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
458	    let mut visible = 0usize;
459	    let mut style_active = false;
460	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
461	        if let Some((sequence, active)) = read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars) {
462	            style_active = active;
463	            out.push_str(&sequence);
464	            continue;
465	        }
466	        let glyph = match ch {
467	            '\n' | '\r' => ' ',
468	            _ => ch,
469	        };
470	        let glyph_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(glyph).unwrap_or(0);
471	        if visible + glyph_width > max_visible {
472	            break;
473	        }
474	        out.push(glyph);
475	        visible += glyph_width;
476	    }
477	    if style_active {
478	        out.push_str(ANSI_RESET);
479	    }
480	    out
481	}

179	
180	impl VerdictSurface {
181	    pub fn try_new<L, C, SL, SC>(
182	        kind: VerdictKind,
183	        subject_kind: impl Into<String>,
184	        subject: Option<&str>,
185	        explanation: ExplanationPanel,
186	        primary_actions: impl IntoIterator<Item = (L, C)>,
187	        secondary_actions: impl IntoIterator<Item = (SL, SC)>,
188	    ) -> Result<Self, VerdictSurfaceError>
189	    where
190	        L: Into<String>,
191	        C: Into<String>,
192	        SL: Into<String>,
193	        SC: Into<String>,
194	    {
195	        let subject_kind = subject_kind.into();
196	        if subject_kind.trim().is_empty() {
197	            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::MissingSubjectKind);
198	        }
199	        explanation.validate()?;
200	
201	        let primary = primary_actions
202	            .into_iter()
203	            .map(|(label, command)| HintLine {
204	                label: label.into(),
205	                command: command.into(),
206	            })
207	            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
208	        if primary.len() != 1 {
209	            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::ExpectedOnePrimaryAction {
210	                actual: primary.len(),
211	            });
212	        }
213	        let mut primary = primary;
214	        let primary_action = primary.remove(0);
215	        if primary_action.command.trim().is_empty() {
216	            return Err(VerdictSurfaceError::MissingPrimaryCommand);
217	        }
218	
219	        let primary_command = primary_action.command.clone();
220	        let secondary_actions = secondary_actions
221	            .into_iter()
222	            .map(|(label, command)| HintLine {
223	                label: label.into(),
224	                command: command.into(),
225	            })
226	            .filter(|action| action.command != primary_command)
227	            .collect();
228	
229	        Ok(Self {
230	            kind,
231	            subject_kind,
232	            subject: subject.map(str::to_string),
233	            explanation,
234	            primary_action,
235	            secondary_actions,
236	        })
237	    }
238	
239	    pub fn label(&self) -> String {
240	        match self.subject.as_deref() {
241	            Some(subject) if !subject.trim().is_empty() => {
242	                format!("{} {} {}", self.kind.as_str(), self.subject_kind, subject)
243	            }
244	            _ => format!("{} {}", self.kind.as_str(), self.subject_kind),
245	        }
246	    }
247	
248	    pub fn render_card(&self, options: &CardOptions) -> String {
249	        let mut sections = self.explanation.sections();
250	        if !self.secondary_actions.is_empty() {
251	            sections.push(Section::Blank);
252	            sections.push(Section::Lines {
253	                lines: vec!["Secondary".to_string()],
254	            });
255	        }
256	        render_card(
257	            &Card {
258	                title: TitleLine {
259	                    glyph: self.kind.glyph(),
260	                    label: self.label(),
261	                },
262	                subtitle: None,
263	                sections,
264	                primary_action: Some(self.primary_action.clone()),
265	                hints: self.secondary_actions.clone(),
266	            },
267	            options,
268	        )
269	    }
270	
271	    pub fn render_plain(&self, no_hints: bool) -> String {
272	        use crate::ui::{self, Stream, Tone};
273	        // Color is gated on ui::enabled (TTY, not --plain/NO_COLOR), so this stays
274	        // byte-identical plain text on non-terminals and in the golden tests while
275	        // a real terminal gets a readable, tone-coded surface.
276	        let heading = |text: &str| ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Heading, text);
277	        let command = |text: &str| ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Command, text);
278	        let mut out = String::new();
279	        out.push_str(&ui::render(Stream::Stdout, self.kind.tone(), self.label()));
280	        out.push_str("\n\n");
281	        out.push_str(&heading("Explanation"));
282	        out.push('\n');
283	        out.push_str(self.explanation.what_happened.trim());
284	        out.push('\n');
285	        out.push_str(self.explanation.why_this_verdict.trim());
286	        out.push_str("\n\n");
287	        out.push_str(&heading("Evidence"));
288	        out.push('\n');
289	        for (key, value) in &self.explanation.evidence {
290	            out.push_str(&ui::render(Stream::Stdout, Tone::Muted, key));
291	            out.push_str(": ");
292	            out.push_str(&color_evidence_value(value));
293	            out.push('\n');
294	        }
295	        out.push('\n');
296	        out.push_str(&heading("Recommended"));
297	        out.push('\n');
298	        out.push_str(&command(&self.primary_action.command));
299	        out.push('\n');
300	        if !no_hints && !self.secondary_actions.is_empty() {
301	            out.push('\n');
302	            out.push_str(&heading("Secondary"));
303	            out.push('\n');
304	            for action in &self.secondary_actions {
305	                out.push_str(&command(&action.command));
306	                out.push('\n');
307	            }
308	        }
309	        out
310	    }
311	
312	    pub fn verdict_json(&self) -> Value {
313	        json!({
314	            "kind": self.kind.as_str(),
315	            "label": self.label(),
316	            "subject": self.subject.as_deref().unwrap_or(self.subject_kind.as_str()),
317	            "recommended_command": self.primary_action.command,
318	            "explanation": self.explanation.one_line(),
319	            "evidence": self.explanation.evidence.iter().map(|(key, value)| {
320	                json!([key, value])
321	            }).collect::<Vec<_>>(),
322	        })
323	    }
324	
325	    pub fn add_to_json(&self, mut value: Value) -> Value {
326	        if !value.is_object() {
327	            value = Value::Object(Map::new());
328	        }
329	        if let Value::Object(object) = &mut value {
330	            object.insert(
331	                "primary_action".to_string(),
332	                Value::String(self.primary_action.command.clone()),
333	            );
334	            object.insert("verdict".to_string(), self.verdict_json());
335	        }
336	        value
337	    }
338	}

71	/// The closed set of lifecycle status classes. `status_tone` resolves a free-form
72	/// status string into exactly one of these — including an explicit `Unknown` —
73	/// so an unrecognized status renders in a visible default tone rather than being
74	/// silently folded into a dim catch-all, and so adding a class is a compile error.
75	#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
76	pub(crate) enum Status {
77	    Ok,
78	    Running,
79	    Paused,
80	    Warn,
81	    Negative,
82	    Note,
83	    Unknown,
84	}
85	
86	impl Status {
87	    pub(crate) fn classify(status: &str) -> Status {
88	        let status = status.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
89	        if status.contains("failed")
90	            || status.contains("killed")
91	            || status.contains("error")
92	            || status.contains("missing")
93	            || status.contains("refused")
94	        {
95	            return Status::Negative;
96	        }
97	        if status.contains("paused") {
98	            return Status::Paused;
99	        }
100	        if status.contains("warning") || status.contains("warn") {
101	            return Status::Warn;
102	        }
103	        match status.as_str() {
104	            "ok" | "ready" | "set" | "wrote" | "updated" | "installed" | "completed" | "passed"
105	            | "polished" | "applied" | "cleaned" | "exported" => Status::Ok,
106	            "running" => Status::Running,
107	            "pending" | "planned" | "skipped" | "undone" | "recorded" | "note" => Status::Note,
108	            _ => Status::Unknown,
109	        }
110	    }
111	
112	    pub(crate) const fn tone(self) -> Tone {
113	        match self {
114	            Status::Ok => Tone::Ok,
115	            Status::Running => Tone::Heading,
116	            Status::Paused => Tone::Paused,
117	            Status::Warn => Tone::Warn,
118	            Status::Negative => Tone::Negative,
119	            Status::Note => Tone::Note,
120	            // Unknown stays a visible default rather than a dim that hides it.
121	            Status::Unknown => Tone::Plain,
122	        }
123	    }
124	}

166	pub(crate) fn enabled(stream: Stream) -> bool {
167	    if PLAIN_OUTPUT.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
168	        return false;
169	    }
170	    if std::env::var_os("NO_COLOR").is_some() {
171	        return false;
172	    }
173	    if std::env::var("TERM").is_ok_and(|term| term == "dumb") {
174	        return false;
175	    }
176	    stream_is_terminal(stream)
177	}

179	pub(crate) fn render(stream: Stream, tone: Tone, text: impl AsRef<str>) -> String {
180	    let text = text.as_ref();
181	    let Some(code) = tone.to_ansi() else {
182	        return text.to_string();
183	    };
184	    if enabled(stream) {
185	        ansi_wrap(code, text)
186	    } else {
187	        text.to_string()
188	    }
189	}

191	pub(crate) fn ansi_wrap(code: &str, text: &str) -> String {
192	    format!("\x1b[{code}m{text}{ANSI_RESET}")
193	}

196	pub(crate) fn ansi_reset() -> &'static str {
197	    ANSI_RESET
198	}

200	#[allow(dead_code)]
201	pub(crate) fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
202	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
203	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
204	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
205	        if read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars).is_some() {
206	            continue;
207	        }
208	        out.push(ch);
209	    }
210	    out
211	}
212	
213	#[allow(dead_code)]
214	pub(crate) fn read_ansi_sequence<I>(first: char, chars: &mut Peekable<I>) -> Option<(String, bool)>
215	where
216	    I: Iterator<Item = char>,
217	{
218	    if first != ANSI_ESC || chars.peek() != Some(&'[') {
219	        return None;
220	    }
221	    let mut sequence = String::from(first);
222	    if let Some(bracket) = chars.next() {
223	        sequence.push(bracket);
224	    }
225	    for code in chars.by_ref() {
226	        sequence.push(code);
227	        if code.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
228	            let active = sequence != ANSI_RESET;
229	            return Some((sequence, active));
230	        }
231	    }
232	    Some((sequence, false))
233	}

235	/// Display width of `text` in terminal columns: ANSI escape sequences are
236	/// stripped first, then each glyph is measured by its Unicode display width so
237	/// wide (CJK / full-width) glyphs count as two columns and zero-width / combining
238	/// marks count as zero. This is the single width function behind every pad,
239	/// truncate, and column-alignment site.
240	#[allow(dead_code)] // used by ui_card today; kv_block/columns/prompt sites adopt it in later phases.
241	pub(crate) fn display_width(text: &str) -> usize {
242	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr;
243	    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(text).as_str())
244	}
245	
246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

310	pub(crate) fn status_tone(status: impl AsRef<str>) -> Tone {
311	    Status::classify(status.as_ref()).tone()
312	}

314	/// Color the leading status token of `value` (e.g. `PASSED` in `PASSED 1/1`,
315	/// `completed` in `completed -> done`) by its status tone, leaving the rest
316	/// plain. A value whose leading token is not a recognized status is returned
317	/// unchanged. Safe for an unpadded (last-column / kv) value.
318	#[allow(dead_code)]
319	pub(crate) fn color_status_word(value: &str) -> String {
320	    let mut parts = value.splitn(2, ' ');
321	    let Some(first) = parts.next() else {
322	        return value.to_string();
323	    };
324	    let tone = status_tone(first);
325	    if tone == Tone::Plain {
326	        return value.to_string();
327	    }
328	    match parts.next() {
329	        Some(rest) => format!("{} {}", render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first), rest),
330	        None => render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first),
331	    }
332	}

409	pub(crate) fn replace_current_line(stream: Stream, text: impl AsRef<str>) -> io::Result<()> {
410	    if !stream_is_terminal(stream) {

412	    }

414	    match stream {
415	        Stream::Stdout => {
416	            print!("\r{text}\x1b[K");
417	            io::stdout().flush()

426	fn stream_is_terminal(stream: Stream) -> bool {
427	    match stream {
428	        Stream::Stdout => io::stdout().is_terminal(),
429	        Stream::Stderr => io::stderr().is_terminal(),
430	    }
431	}
432	
433	fn current_terminal_width() -> usize {
434	    crossterm::terminal::size()
435	        .ok()
436	        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
437	        .or_else(|| {
438	            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
439	                .ok()
440	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
441	        })
442	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 0)
443	        .unwrap_or(120)
444	}
445	
446	fn replacement_line_text(text: &str, terminal_width: usize) -> String {
447	    let visible_limit = terminal_width.saturating_sub(1);
448	    truncate_visible_single_line(text, visible_limit)
449	}
450	
451	fn truncate_visible_single_line(text: &str, max_visible: usize) -> String {
452	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
453	    if max_visible == 0 {
454	        return String::new();
455	    }
456	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len().min(max_visible));
457	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
458	    let mut visible = 0usize;
459	    let mut style_active = false;
460	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
461	        if let Some((sequence, active)) = read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars) {
462	            style_active = active;
463	            out.push_str(&sequence);
464	            continue;
465	        }
466	        let glyph = match ch {
467	            '\n' | '\r' => ' ',
468	            _ => ch,
469	        };
470	        let glyph_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(glyph).unwrap_or(0);
471	        if visible + glyph_width > max_visible {
472	            break;
473	        }
474	        out.push(glyph);
475	        visible += glyph_width;
476	    }
477	    if style_active {
478	        out.push_str(ANSI_RESET);
479	    }
480	    out
481	}

87	    pub(crate) fn classify(status: &str) -> Status {
88	        let status = status.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
89	        if status.contains("failed")
90	            || status.contains("killed")
91	            || status.contains("error")
92	            || status.contains("missing")
93	            || status.contains("refused")
94	        {
95	            return Status::Negative;
96	        }
97	        if status.contains("paused") {

99	        }
100	        if status.contains("warning") || status.contains("warn") {
101	            return Status::Warn;
102	        }
103	        match status.as_str() {
104	            "ok" | "ready" | "set" | "wrote" | "updated" | "installed" | "completed" | "passed"
105	            | "polished" | "applied" | "cleaned" | "exported" => Status::Ok,
106	            "running" => Status::Running,
107	            "pending" | "planned" | "skipped" | "undone" | "recorded" | "note" => Status::Note,
108	            _ => Status::Unknown,
109	        }
110	    }

201	pub(crate) fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
202	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
203	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
204	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
205	        if read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars).is_some() {
206	            continue;
207	        }
208	        out.push(ch);
209	    }
210	    out
211	}

213	#[allow(dead_code)]
214	pub(crate) fn read_ansi_sequence<I>(first: char, chars: &mut Peekable<I>) -> Option<(String, bool)>
215	where
216	    I: Iterator<Item = char>,
217	{
218	    if first != ANSI_ESC || chars.peek() != Some(&'[') {
219	        return None;
220	    }
221	    let mut sequence = String::from(first);
222	    if let Some(bracket) = chars.next() {
223	        sequence.push(bracket);
224	    }
225	    for code in chars.by_ref() {
226	        sequence.push(code);
227	        if code.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
228	            let active = sequence != ANSI_RESET;
229	            return Some((sequence, active));
230	        }
231	    }
232	    Some((sequence, false))
233	}

235	/// Display width of `text` in terminal columns: ANSI escape sequences are
236	/// stripped first, then each glyph is measured by its Unicode display width so
237	/// wide (CJK / full-width) glyphs count as two columns and zero-width / combining
238	/// marks count as zero. This is the single width function behind every pad,
239	/// truncate, and column-alignment site.
240	#[allow(dead_code)] // used by ui_card today; kv_block/columns/prompt sites adopt it in later phases.
241	pub(crate) fn display_width(text: &str) -> usize {
242	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr;
243	    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(text).as_str())
244	}
245	
246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

314	/// Color the leading status token of `value` (e.g. `PASSED` in `PASSED 1/1`,
315	/// `completed` in `completed -> done`) by its status tone, leaving the rest
316	/// plain. A value whose leading token is not a recognized status is returned
317	/// unchanged. Safe for an unpadded (last-column / kv) value.
318	#[allow(dead_code)]
319	pub(crate) fn color_status_word(value: &str) -> String {
320	    let mut parts = value.splitn(2, ' ');
321	    let Some(first) = parts.next() else {
322	        return value.to_string();
323	    };
324	    let tone = status_tone(first);
325	    if tone == Tone::Plain {
326	        return value.to_string();
327	    }
328	    match parts.next() {
329	        Some(rest) => format!("{} {}", render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first), rest),
330	        None => render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first),
331	    }
332	}

433	fn current_terminal_width() -> usize {
434	    crossterm::terminal::size()
435	        .ok()
436	        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
437	        .or_else(|| {
438	            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
439	                .ok()
440	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
441	        })
442	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 0)
443	        .unwrap_or(120)
444	}

446	fn replacement_line_text(text: &str, terminal_width: usize) -> String {
447	    let visible_limit = terminal_width.saturating_sub(1);
448	    truncate_visible_single_line(text, visible_limit)
449	}
450	
451	fn truncate_visible_single_line(text: &str, max_visible: usize) -> String {
452	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
453	    if max_visible == 0 {
454	        return String::new();
455	    }
456	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len().min(max_visible));
457	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
458	    let mut visible = 0usize;
459	    let mut style_active = false;
460	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
461	        if let Some((sequence, active)) = read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars) {
462	            style_active = active;
463	            out.push_str(&sequence);
464	            continue;
465	        }
466	        let glyph = match ch {
467	            '\n' | '\r' => ' ',
468	            _ => ch,
469	        };
470	        let glyph_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(glyph).unwrap_or(0);
471	        if visible + glyph_width > max_visible {
472	            break;
473	        }
474	        out.push(glyph);
475	        visible += glyph_width;
476	    }
477	    if style_active {
478	        out.push_str(ANSI_RESET);
479	    }
480	    out
481	}

240	#[allow(dead_code)] // used by ui_card today; kv_block/columns/prompt sites adopt it in later phases.
241	pub(crate) fn display_width(text: &str) -> usize {
242	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr;
243	    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(text).as_str())
244	}
245	
246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

314	/// Color the leading status token of `value` (e.g. `PASSED` in `PASSED 1/1`,
315	/// `completed` in `completed -> done`) by its status tone, leaving the rest
316	/// plain. A value whose leading token is not a recognized status is returned

318	#[allow(dead_code)]
319	pub(crate) fn color_status_word(value: &str) -> String {
320	    let mut parts = value.splitn(2, ' ');

323	    };

329	        Some(rest) => format!("{} {}", render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first), rest),
330	        None => render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first),
331	    }
332	}

283	fn print_kv_block<K, V>(items: &[(K, V)])

291	fn write_kv_block<K, V>(items: &[(K, V)]) -> io::Result<()>
292	where
293	    K: AsRef<str>,
294	    V: AsRef<str>,
295	{
296	    print!("{}", kv_block_string("", items));

299	
300	/// The shared `key: value` block primitive. The key column is sized to the widest
301	/// key by display width (ANSI-aware), `indent` prefixes every line, and values
302	/// wrap to the terminal. Use this instead of hand-aligned `println!("  k:  v")`
303	/// blocks so every kv surface aligns the same way.
304	fn kv_block_string<K, V>(indent: &str, items: &[(K, V)]) -> String
305	where
306	    K: AsRef<str>,
307	    V: AsRef<str>,
308	{
309	    let key_width = items
310	        .iter()
311	        .map(|(key, _)| ui::display_width(key.as_ref()))
312	        .max()
313	        .unwrap_or(0);
314	    let prefix_width = ui::display_width(indent) + key_width + 2;
315	    let value_width = kv_value_width(prefix_width);
316	    let mut out = String::new();
317	    for (key, value) in items {
318	        let mut first = true;
319	        for logical_line in value
320	            .as_ref()
321	            .lines()
322	            .chain(value.as_ref().is_empty().then_some(""))
323	        {
324	            for line in wrap_kv_value(logical_line, value_width) {
325	                if first {
326	                    first = false;
327	                    out.push_str(indent);
328	                    // Dim the key (label) so it reads as subordinate to its value;
329	                    // ui::render is gated on a TTY, so plain output is unchanged.
330	                    out.push_str(&ui::render(
331	                        ui::Stream::Stdout,
332	                        ui::Tone::Muted,
333	                        ui::pad_visible(key.as_ref(), key_width),
334	                    ));
335	                    out.push_str(": ");
336	                    out.push_str(&line);
337	                } else {
338	                    out.push_str(&" ".repeat(prefix_width));
339	                    out.push_str(&line);
340	                }
341	                out.push('\n');
342	            }

240	#[allow(dead_code)] // used by ui_card today; kv_block/columns/prompt sites adopt it in later phases.
241	pub(crate) fn display_width(text: &str) -> usize {
242	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr;
243	    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(text).as_str())
244	}
245	
246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

310	pub(crate) fn status_tone(status: impl AsRef<str>) -> Tone {

312	}
313	
314	/// Color the leading status token of `value` (e.g. `PASSED` in `PASSED 1/1`,
315	/// `completed` in `completed -> done`) by its status tone, leaving the rest
316	/// plain. A value whose leading token is not a recognized status is returned
317	/// unchanged. Safe for an unpadded (last-column / kv) value.
318	#[allow(dead_code)]
319	pub(crate) fn color_status_word(value: &str) -> String {
320	    let mut parts = value.splitn(2, ' ');
321	    let Some(first) = parts.next() else {
322	        return value.to_string();
323	    };
324	    let tone = status_tone(first);
325	    if tone == Tone::Plain {
326	        return value.to_string();
327	    }
328	    match parts.next() {
329	        Some(rest) => format!("{} {}", render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first), rest),
330	        None => render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first),
331	    }
332	}

300	/// The shared `key: value` block primitive. The key column is sized to the widest
301	/// key by display width (ANSI-aware), `indent` prefixes every line, and values
302	/// wrap to the terminal. Use this instead of hand-aligned `println!("  k:  v")`
303	/// blocks so every kv surface aligns the same way.
304	fn kv_block_string<K, V>(indent: &str, items: &[(K, V)]) -> String
305	where
306	    K: AsRef<str>,
307	    V: AsRef<str>,
308	{
309	    let key_width = items

312	        .max()

359	        .saturating_sub(1);
360	    terminal_width.saturating_sub(prefix_width).max(20)
361	}

310	pub(crate) fn status_tone(status: impl AsRef<str>) -> Tone {
311	    Status::classify(status.as_ref()).tone()
312	}
313	
314	/// Color the leading status token of `value` (e.g. `PASSED` in `PASSED 1/1`,
315	/// `completed` in `completed -> done`) by its status tone, leaving the rest
316	/// plain. A value whose leading token is not a recognized status is returned
317	/// unchanged. Safe for an unpadded (last-column / kv) value.
318	#[allow(dead_code)]
319	pub(crate) fn color_status_word(value: &str) -> String {
320	    let mut parts = value.splitn(2, ' ');
321	    let Some(first) = parts.next() else {
322	        return value.to_string();
323	    };
324	    let tone = status_tone(first);
325	    if tone == Tone::Plain {
326	        return value.to_string();
327	    }
328	    match parts.next() {
329	        Some(rest) => format!("{} {}", render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first), rest),
330	        None => render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first),
331	    }
332	}
333	
334	pub(crate) fn render_status(stream: Stream, status: impl AsRef<str>) -> String {
335	    let status = status.as_ref();
336	    render(stream, status_tone(status), status)
337	}

150	                        .map(|version| format!(" ({version})"))
151	                        .unwrap_or_default()
152	                ),
153	                Some(format!(
154	                    "deadreckon run \"goal\" --sandbox {} --preview",
155	                    backend.backend
156	                )),
157	            ));
158	        } else {
159	            findings.push(DoctorFinding::warning(
160	                format!("sandbox {}", backend.backend),
161	                format!("missing: {}", backend.note),
162	                None,
163	            ));
164	        }
165	        sandboxes.push(json!({
166	            "backend": backend.backend,
167	            "available": backend.available,
168	            "path": backend.path,
169	            "note": backend.note,
170	        }));
171	    }
172	
173	    let mut config_root = None;
174	    let config_present = paths.config_path().exists();
175	    if config_present {
176	        match load_config_value(paths) {
177	            Ok(root) => {
178	                findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
179	                    "config",
180	                    format!("{} present and parseable", paths.config_path().display()),
181	                    Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
182	                ));
183	                config_root = Some(root);
184	            }
185	            Err(err) => findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
186	                "config",
187	                format!("{} is not parseable: {err}", paths.config_path().display()),
188	                Some("deadreckon init".to_string()),
189	            )),
190	        }
191	    } else {
192	        findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
193	            "config",
194	            format!("{} missing", paths.config_path().display()),
195	            Some("deadreckon init".to_string()),
196	        ));
197	    }
198	
199	    if let Some(root) = &config_root {
200	        findings.extend(collect_doctor_provider_findings(paths, root).await?);
201	    }
202	
203	    let defaults = config_defaults(paths).unwrap_or_default();
204	    if defaults.provider.is_some() || config_present {
205	        findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
206	            "provider defaults",
207	            "provider defaults configured",
208	            Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
209	        ));
210	    } else if command_exists("claude") || command_exists("codex") {
211	        findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
212	            "provider defaults",
213	            "CLI subscription provider available",
214	            Some("deadreckon init --no-confirm".to_string()),
215	        ));
216	    } else {
217	        findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
218	            "provider defaults",
219	            "no provider configured",
220	            Some("deadreckon init".to_string()),
221	        ));
222	    }
223	
224	    let seams = match doctor_seam_resolution(paths, false) {
225	        Ok(lines) => {
226	            findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
227	                "seams",
228	                format!("resolved: {}", lines.join("; ")),
229	                Some("deadreckon run \"goal\" --no-seams".to_string()),
230	            ));
231	            json!({
232	                "status": "ok",
233	                "resolution": lines,
234	            })
235	        }
236	        Err(err) => {
237	            findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
238	                "seams",
239	                format!("config invalid: {err}"),
240	                Some("deadreckon doctor".to_string()),
241	            ));
242	            json!({
243	                "status": "invalid",
244	                "error": err.to_string(),
245	            })
246	        }
247	    };
248	
249	    collect_doctor_disk_and_permission_findings(paths, &mut findings);
250	    collect_doctor_os_finding(&mut findings);
251	    collect_doctor_sleep_finding(&mut findings);
252	    collect_doctor_subscription_binary_finding("claude", &mut findings);
253	    collect_doctor_subscription_binary_finding("codex", &mut findings);
254	
255	    Ok(DoctorReport {
256	        source,
257	        config_present,
258	        sandboxes,
259	        seams,
260	        findings,
261	    })
262	}
263	
264	fn doctor_verdict_surface(report: &DoctorReport) -> VerdictSurface {
265	    let failed_count = report
266	        .findings
267	        .iter()
268	        .filter(|finding| finding.is_failed())
269	        .count();
270	    let warning_count = report
271	        .findings
272	        .iter()
273	        .filter(|finding| finding.status == "warning")
274	        .count();
275	    let kind = if failed_count == 0 {
276	        VerdictKind::Verified
277	    } else {
278	        VerdictKind::Blocked
279	    };
280	    let primary = doctor_primary_action(report);
281	    let secondary = doctor_secondary_actions(report, &primary)
282	        .into_iter()
283	        .map(|action| ("Secondary", action))
284	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
285	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
286	        kind,
287	        "doctor",
288	        None,
289	        doctor_explanation(report, failed_count, warning_count),
290	        vec![("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
291	        secondary,
292	    )
293	    .expect("doctor verdict surface must be valid")
294	}
295	
296	fn doctor_explanation(
297	    report: &DoctorReport,
298	    failed_count: usize,
299	    warning_count: usize,
300	) -> ExplanationPanel {
301	    let what = if failed_count == 0 {
302	        format!(
303	            "Doctor checked {} setup areas and found no blocking setup failures.",
304	            report.findings.len()
305	        )
306	    } else {
307	        format!(
308	            "Doctor checked {} setup areas and found {failed_count} blocking setup issue(s).",
309	            report.findings.len()
310	        )
311	    };
312	    let why = if failed_count == 0 {
313	        "All required checks passed; warnings, if any, are optional capabilities or local environment notes."
314	            .to_string()
315	    } else {
316	        format!(
317	            "The verdict is blocked because required setup checks failed; {warning_count} optional warning(s) were also recorded."
318	        )
319	    };
320	    let evidence = report
321	        .findings
322	        .iter()
323	        .map(|finding| {
324	            (
325	                finding.subject.clone(),
326	                format!("{} - {}", finding.status, finding.detail),
327	            )
328	        })
329	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
330	    ExplanationPanel::new(what, why, evidence)
331	}
332	
333	fn doctor_primary_action(report: &DoctorReport) -> String {
334	    report
335	        .findings
336	        .iter()
337	        .filter(|finding| finding.is_failed())
338	        .filter_map(|finding| finding.action.as_deref())
339	        .find(|action| action.starts_with("deadreckon "))
340	        .map(str::to_string)
341	        .unwrap_or_else(|| "deadreckon run \"goal\" --preview".to_string())
342	}
343	
344	fn doctor_secondary_actions(report: &DoctorReport, primary: &str) -> Vec<String> {
345	    let mut actions = Vec::new();
346	    for action in report
347	        .findings
348	        .iter()
349	        .filter_map(|finding| finding.action.as_deref())
350	    {
351	        if action != primary && !actions.iter().any(|existing| existing == action) {
352	            actions.push(action.to_string());
353	        }
354	    }
355	    actions
356	}

358	fn doctor_json_payload(
359	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
360	    report: &DoctorReport,
361	    surface: &VerdictSurface,
362	) -> Value {
363	    let mut next_actions = vec![surface.primary_action.command.clone()];
364	    next_actions.extend(doctor_secondary_actions(
365	        report,
366	        &surface.primary_action.command,
367	    ));
368	    json!({
369	        "kind": "doctor",
370	        "id": &report.source,
371	        "status": surface.kind.as_str(),
372	        "next_actions": next_actions,
373	        "try_lines": Vec::<String>::new(),
374	        "paths": {
375	            "home": paths.home(),
376	            "config": paths.config_path(),
377	        },
378	        "source": &report.source,
379	        "home": paths.home(),
380	        "config_path": paths.config_path(),
381	        "config_present": report.config_present,
382	        "sandboxes": report.sandboxes,
383	        "seams": report.seams,
384	        "findings": report.findings,
385	    })
386	}

388	async fn collect_doctor_provider_findings(
389	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
390	    root: &toml::Value,
391	) -> Result<Vec<DoctorFinding>> {
392	    let Some(providers) = root.get("providers").and_then(toml::Value::as_table) else {
393	        return Ok(vec![DoctorFinding::failed(
394	            "providers",
395	            "providers table missing",
396	            Some("deadreckon init".to_string()),
397	        )]);
398	    };
399	    let registry = ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())?;
400	    let mut findings = Vec::new();
401	    for (name, entry) in providers {
402	        let kind = entry
403	            .get("kind")
404	            .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
405	            .unwrap_or(name);
406	        let kind_label = registry
407	            .get(name)
408	            .map(|descriptor| descriptor_kind_label(&descriptor.kind).to_string())
409	            .unwrap_or_else(|| config_provider_kind_label(kind).to_string());
410	        let subject = format!("provider {name} kind={kind_label}");
411	        if kind.contains("cli") || name.starts_with("cli:") {
412	            let binary = entry
413	                .get("binary")
414	                .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
415	                .unwrap_or_else(|| {
416	                    if name.contains("claude") {
417	                        "claude"
418	                    } else {
419	                        "codex"
420	                    }
421	                });
422	            if command_exists(binary) || PathBuf::from(binary).exists() {
423	                findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
424	                    subject,
425	                    format!("CLI binary {binary} found"),
426	                    Some(format!(
427	                        "deadreckon run \"goal\" --provider {name} --preview"
428	                    )),
429	                ));
430	            } else {
431	                findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
432	                    subject,
433	                    format!("CLI binary {binary} missing"),
434	                    Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
435	                ));
436	            }
437	        } else if provider_has_key(entry) {
438	            if std::env::var_os("DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING").is_some() {
439	                findings.push(collect_doctor_provider_ping(paths, name, &kind_label).await?);
440	            } else {
441	                findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(
442	                    subject,
443	                    "credential present; ping skipped",
444	                    Some("DEADRECKON_DOCTOR_PING=1 deadreckon doctor".to_string()),
445	                ));
446	            }
447	        } else {
448	            findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
449	                subject,
450	                "credential missing",
451	                Some(format!(
452	                    "deadreckon config set providers.{name}.api_key <KEY>"
453	                )),
454	            ));
455	        }
456	    }
457	    Ok(findings)
458	}

460	async fn collect_doctor_provider_ping(
461	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
462	    name: &str,
463	    kind_label: &str,
464	) -> Result<DoctorFinding> {
465	    let router = ProviderRouter::from_config_path(&paths.config_path(), Some(name))?;
466	    let request = ProviderRequest {
467	        prompt: "Reply with OK only.".to_string(),
468	        max_output_tokens: 8,
469	        cwd: None,
470	        output_path: None,
471	        sandbox_backend: None,
472	        pid_file: None,
473	        cancellation_token: None,
474	    };
475	    let subject = format!("provider {name} kind={kind_label}");
476	    match tokio::time::timeout(
477	        std::time::Duration::from_secs(20),
478	        router.complete(&request),
479	    )
480	    .await
481	    {
482	        Ok(Ok(response)) => Ok(DoctorFinding::passed(
483	            subject,
484	            format!("ping ok model {}", response.model),
485	            Some(format!(
486	                "deadreckon run \"goal\" --provider {name} --preview"
487	            )),
488	        )),
489	        Ok(Err(err)) => Ok(DoctorFinding::failed(
490	            subject,
491	            format!("ping failed: {err}"),
492	            Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
493	        )),
494	        Err(_) => Ok(DoctorFinding::failed(
495	            subject,
496	            "ping timed out",
497	            Some("deadreckon config provider".to_string()),
498	        )),
499	    }
500	}

515	            Ok(()) => findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(

520	            Err(err) => findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(

524	            )),
525	        }

527	
528	    match free_kb(paths.home()) {
529	        Some(kb) if kb < 1_048_576 => findings.push(DoctorFinding::failed(
530	            "disk space",

532	            None,
533	        )),
534	        Some(kb) => findings.push(DoctorFinding::passed(

539	        None => findings.push(DoctorFinding::warning(
540	            "disk space",
541	            format!("check unavailable for {}", paths.home().display()),

543	        )),
