623	fn doctor_seam_resolution(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, no_seams: bool) -> Result<Vec<String>> {
624	    let seams = read_seams_config(&paths.config_path(), no_seams)?;
625	    Ok(SeamKind::all()
626	        .into_iter()
627	        .map(|kind| {
628	            let fail = seam_fail_policy_label(kind);
629	            match seams.command_for(kind) {
630	                Some(command) => format!(
631	                    "{}: external command={} timeout_ms={} fail={fail}",
632	                    kind.config_key(),
633	                    seam_command_basename(&command.command),
634	                    command.timeout_ms
635	                ),
636	                None => format!("{}: builtin fail={fail}", kind.config_key()),
637	            }
638	        })
639	        .collect())
640	}
641	
642	fn seam_command_basename(command: &[String]) -> String {
643	    command
644	        .first()
645	        .and_then(|argv0| Path::new(argv0).file_name())
646	        .and_then(|name| name.to_str())
647	        .unwrap_or("-")
648	        .to_string()
649	}
650	
651	fn config_provider_kind_label(kind: &str) -> &'static str {
652	    let kind = kind.to_ascii_lowercase();
653	    if kind.contains("cli") {
654	        "cli"
655	    } else if kind.contains("compatible") || kind.contains("local") {
656	        "local-http"
657	    } else if kind.contains("smoke") || kind.contains("script") {
658	        "scripted"
659	    } else if kind.contains("anthropic") || kind.contains("open-ai") || kind.contains("openai") {
660	        "http"
661	    } else {
662	        "custom"
663	    }
664	}
665	
666	fn provider_has_key(entry: &toml::Value) -> bool {
667	    entry
668	        .get("api_key")
669	        .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
670	        .is_some_and(|value| !value.trim().is_empty())
671	        || entry
672	            .get("api_key_env")
673	            .and_then(toml::Value::as_str)
674	            .and_then(std::env::var_os)
675	            .is_some()
676	}
677	
678	fn command_version(path: &std::path::Path) -> Option<String> {
679	    std::process::Command::new(path)
680	        .arg("--version")
681	        .output()
682	        .ok()
683	        .filter(|output| output.status.success())
684	        .map(|output| {
685	            let text = if output.stdout.is_empty() {
686	                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr).to_string()
687	            } else {
688	                String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout).to_string()
689	            };
690	            text.lines().next().unwrap_or_default().trim().to_string()
691	        })
692	        .filter(|line| !line.is_empty())
693	}

7	    max_spend: f64,
8	    sandbox: String,
9	    no_confirm: bool,
10	    no_completion: bool,
11	) -> Result<()> {
12	    let paths = DeadreckonPaths::discover();
13	    fs::create_dir_all(paths.home())?;
14	    let registry = ProviderRegistry::with_overrides(paths.home())?;
15	    let provider = match provider {
16	        Some(provider) => provider,
17	        None if no_confirm => preferred_init_subscription_cli_provider(&registry)
18	            .unwrap_or_else(|| "anthropic".to_string()),
19	        None => prompt_provider()?,
20	    };
21	    provider_setup_selection(
22	        &paths,
23	        setup::ProviderSetupRequest {
24	            role: setup::SetupProviderRoleRef::ConfigDefault,
25	            explicit_provider: Some(&provider),
26	            explicit_model: None,
27	            config_default_provider: None,
28	            config_doc_provider: None,
29	            run_provider: None,
30	            auto_subscription_provider: None,
31	            built_in_default_provider: Some("anthropic"),
32	            use_router_default: false,
33	            allow_auto_subscription: true,
34	            require_usable_route: false,
35	        },
36	    )?;
37	    let api_key = api_key.or_else(|| {
38	        if provider.starts_with("cli:") {
39	            None
40	        } else {
41	            prompt::open("provider API key (leave blank to use env var): ", None).ok()
42	        }
43	    });
44	    let config = init_config_text(
45	        &provider,
46	        api_key.as_deref(),
47	        base_url.as_deref(),
48	        max_spend,
49	        &sandbox,
50	    );
51	    fs::write(paths.config_path(), config)?;
52	    let provider_setup = provider_setup_selection(
53	        &paths,
54	        setup::ProviderSetupRequest {
55	            role: setup::SetupProviderRoleRef::ConfigDefault,
56	            explicit_provider: Some(&provider),
57	            explicit_model: None,
58	            config_default_provider: None,
59	            config_doc_provider: None,
60	            run_provider: None,
61	            auto_subscription_provider: None,
62	            built_in_default_provider: Some("anthropic"),
63	            use_router_default: false,
64	            allow_auto_subscription: true,
65	            require_usable_route: false,
66	        },
67	    )?;
68	    println!("{} {}", ui_ok("wrote"), paths.config_path().display());
69	    print_provider_setup_rows(&[provider_setup]);
70	    let doctor_summary = super::doctor::doctor_setup_summary().await?;
71	    let completion_status = if no_completion {
72	        "skipped by --no-completion".to_string()
73	    } else {
74	        super::completion::try_install_completion_after_init()
75	    };
76	    print!(
77	        "{}",
78	        init_completion_surface(
79	            &paths,
80	            &provider,
81	            &sandbox,
82	            &completion_status,
83	            &doctor_summary,
84	        )
85	        .render_plain(!completion_hints_enabled(false))
86	    );
87	    Ok(())
88	}
89	
90	fn init_completion_surface(
91	    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
92	    provider: &str,
93	    sandbox: &str,
94	    completion_status: &str,
95	    doctor_summary: &super::doctor::DoctorSetupSummary,
96	) -> VerdictSurface {
97	    let (kind, why, primary, secondary) = if doctor_summary.has_blocking_issues() {
98	        (
99	            VerdictKind::Blocked,
100	            "Initialization wrote the config, but setup verification found blocking issues; run doctor before starting managed work.",
101	            "deadreckon doctor",
102	            vec![("Secondary", "deadreckon run \"describe the coding goal\"")],
103	        )
104	    } else {
105	        (
106	            VerdictKind::Completed,
107	            "Initialization completed; the next step is to start a managed run from this workspace.",
108	            "deadreckon run \"describe the coding goal\"",
109	            vec![("Secondary", "deadreckon doctor")],
110	        )
111	    };
112	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
113	        kind,
114	        "init",
115	        None,
116	        ExplanationPanel::new(
117	            "DeadReckon wrote the local configuration and checked the provider setup.",
118	            why,
119	            vec![
120	                ("config", paths.config_path().display().to_string()),
121	                ("provider", provider.to_string()),
122	                ("sandbox", sandbox.to_string()),
123	                ("doctor", doctor_summary.evidence_detail()),
124	                ("completion", completion_status.to_string()),
125	            ],
126	        ),
127	        vec![("Recommended", primary)],
128	        secondary,
129	    )
130	    .expect("init verdict surface must be valid")
131	}
132	
133	fn preferred_init_subscription_cli_provider(registry: &ProviderRegistry) -> Option<String> {
134	    registry
135	        .iter()
136	        .filter(|descriptor| {
137	            descriptor.kind == DescriptorKind::Cli
138	                && descriptor.subscription
139	                && descriptor
140	                    .default_binary
141	                    .as_deref()
142	                    .is_some_and(command_exists)
143	        })
144	        .map(|descriptor| descriptor.id.clone())
145	        .next()
146	}

140	fn classify_validation_outcome(
141	    kind: SeamKind,
142	    command: &SeamCommandConfig,
143	    fixture: &Path,
144	    sandbox: String,
145	    outcome: SeamOutcome,
146	) -> SeamValidationReport {
147	    let command_name = seam_command_basename(&command.command);
148	    let fail_policy = seam_fail_policy_label(kind).to_string();
149	    let base = |outcome: &str,
150	                decision: Option<String>,
151	                detail: Option<String>,
152	                try_lines: Vec<String>,
153	                exit_success| {
154	        SeamValidationReport {
155	            kind: cli_kind_label(kind).to_string(),
156	            command: command_name.clone(),
157	            fixture: display_path(fixture),
158	            sandbox: sandbox.clone(),
159	            outcome: outcome.to_string(),
160	            fail_policy: fail_policy.clone(),
161	            source: "external".to_string(),
162	            decision,
163	            detail,
164	            try_lines,
165	            exit_success,
166	        }
167	    };
168	
169	    match outcome {
170	        SeamOutcome::Ok(_) if kind == SeamKind::Policy => {
171	            base("passed", Some("allow".to_string()), None, Vec::new(), true)
172	        }
173	        SeamOutcome::Ok(value) if kind == SeamKind::Catalog => {
174	            match ModelCatalogOverride::from_value(value) {
175	                Ok(_) => base("passed", None, None, Vec::new(), true),
176	                Err(err) => base(
177	                    "failed",
178	                    None,
179	                    Some(format!("catalog response failed open: {err}")),
180	                    vec![
181	                        r#"return {"models":[{"id":"local-model","context_window":4000}]}"#
182	                            .to_string(),
183	                    ],
184	                    false,
185	                ),
186	            }
187	        }
188	        SeamOutcome::Ok(_) => base("passed", None, None, Vec::new(), true),
189	        SeamOutcome::Deny(reason)
190	            if kind == SeamKind::Policy && !reason.contains("failed closed") =>
191	        {
192	            base(
193	                "passed",
194	                Some("deny".to_string()),
195	                Some(reason),
196	                Vec::new(),
197	                true,
198	            )
199	        }
200	        SeamOutcome::Deny(reason) => base(
201	            "failed",
202	            None,
203	            Some(reason),
204	            vec![
205	                r#"return {"decision":"allow"} or {"decision":"deny","reason":"..."}"#.to_string(),
206	                "rerun the launch with --no-seams to force built-ins".to_string(),
207	            ],
208	            false,
209	        ),
210	        SeamOutcome::Fallback => base(
211	            "failed",
212	            None,
213	            Some("catalog worker failed open; runtime would use the built-in catalog".to_string()),
214	            vec![r#"return {"models":[{"id":"local-model","context_window":4000}]}"#.to_string()],
215	            false,
216	        ),
217	        SeamOutcome::Skipped(reason) => base(
218	            "non_fatal",
219	            None,
220	            Some(format!(
221	                "observer worker failed safe; runtime would continue: {reason}"
222	            )),
223	            vec!["inspect the worker command, timeout, and stderr".to_string()],
224	            true,
225	        ),
226	        SeamOutcome::Unconfigured => base(
227	            "failed",
228	            None,
229	            Some("no external worker configured".to_string()),
230	            vec![format!("add [seams.{}] to config", kind.config_key())],
231	            false,
232	        ),
233	    }
234	}

240	fn seam_validation_surface(report: &SeamValidationReport) -> VerdictSurface {
241	    let kind = if report.exit_success {
242	        VerdictKind::Verified
243	    } else {
244	        VerdictKind::Failed
245	    };
246	    let primary = seam_validation_primary_action(report);
247	    let secondary = report
248	        .try_lines
249	        .iter()
250	        .filter_map(|line| {
251	            let line = line.trim();
252	            (line.starts_with("deadreckon ") && line != primary).then_some(("Secondary", line))
253	        })
254	        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
255	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
256	        kind,
257	        "seam",
258	        Some(&report.kind),
259	        seam_validation_explanation(report),
260	        vec![("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
261	        secondary,
262	    )
263	    .expect("seam validation verdict surface must be valid")
264	}
265	
266	fn seam_validation_primary_action(report: &SeamValidationReport) -> String {
267	    if !report.exit_success
268	        && let Some(command) = report
269	            .try_lines
270	            .iter()
271	            .map(|line| line.trim())
272	            .find(|line| line.starts_with("deadreckon "))
273	    {
274	        return command.to_string();
275	    }
276	    if report.exit_success {
277	        "deadreckon run \"goal\"".to_string()
278	    } else {
279	        "deadreckon doctor".to_string()
280	    }
281	}

283	fn seam_validation_explanation(report: &SeamValidationReport) -> ExplanationPanel {
284	    let what = if report.exit_success {
285	        format!(
286	            "Seam validation completed for the {} worker with outcome {}.",
287	            report.kind, report.outcome
288	        )
289	    } else {
290	        format!(
291	            "Seam validation failed for the {} worker with outcome {}.",
292	            report.kind, report.outcome
293	        )
294	    };
295	    let why = report.detail.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| {
296	        if report.exit_success {
297	            format!(
298	                "The worker response satisfies the {} fail policy for this seam.",
299	                report.fail_policy
300	            )
301	        } else {
302	            format!(
303	                "The worker response does not satisfy the {} fail policy for this seam.",
304	                report.fail_policy
305	            )
306	        }
307	    });
308	    let mut evidence = vec![
309	        ("kind", report.kind.clone()),
310	        ("outcome", report.outcome.clone()),
311	        ("command", report.command.clone()),
312	        ("fixture", report.fixture.clone()),
313	        ("sandbox", report.sandbox.clone()),
314	        ("fail policy", report.fail_policy.clone()),
315	        ("source", report.source.clone()),
316	    ];
317	    if let Some(decision) = &report.decision {
318	        evidence.push(("decision", decision.clone()));
319	    }
320	    if let Some(detail) = &report.detail {
321	        evidence.push(("detail", detail.clone()));
322	    }
323	    ExplanationPanel::new(what, why, evidence)
324	}

18	        CompletionCommand::Fish => write_completion_script(Shell::Fish, &mut io::stdout()),
19	        CompletionCommand::PowerShell => {

43	fn install_completion(
44	    shell: Option<Shell>,
45	    path_override: Option<PathBuf>,
46	    update_rc: bool,
47	) -> Result<CompletionInstallOutcome> {
48	    let shell = shell.or_else(detect_completion_shell).ok_or_else(|| {
49	        CliError::Core(deadreckon_core::user_error(
50	            "could not detect your shell",
51	            "deadreckon completion install --shell zsh",
52	        ))
53	    })?;
54	    let path = path_override.unwrap_or_else(|| default_completion_path(shell));
55	    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
56	        fs::create_dir_all(parent)?;
57	    }
58	    let mut script = Vec::new();
59	    write_completion_script(shell, &mut script);
60	    fs::write(&path, script)?;
61	    let rc_status = match (shell, update_rc) {
62	        (Shell::Zsh, true) => ensure_zsh_completion_rc(&path)?,
63	        (Shell::Zsh, false) => CompletionRcStatus::Skipped,
64	        _ => CompletionRcStatus::NotApplicable,
65	    };
66	    Ok(CompletionInstallOutcome {
67	        shell,
68	        path,
69	        rc_status,
70	    })
71	}

125	fn completion_shell_name(shell: Shell) -> &'static str {
126	    match shell {
127	        Shell::Bash => "bash",
128	        Shell::Elvish => "elvish",
129	        Shell::Fish => "fish",
130	        Shell::PowerShell => "powershell",
131	        Shell::Zsh => "zsh",

133	    }

136	impl CompletionRcStatus {
137	    fn evidence_value(&self) -> String {
138	        match self {
139	            Self::Updated(path) => format!("updated {}", path.display()),
140	            Self::Ready(path) => format!("already configured {}", path.display()),
141	            Self::Skipped => "not updated (--no-rc)".to_string(),
142	            Self::NotApplicable => "not required for this shell".to_string(),
143	        }
144	    }
145	}
146	
147	fn detect_completion_shell() -> Option<Shell> {
148	    let shell = std::env::var("SHELL").ok()?;
149	    let name = Path::new(&shell).file_name()?.to_string_lossy();
150	    match name.as_ref() {
151	        "bash" => Some(Shell::Bash),
152	        "elvish" => Some(Shell::Elvish),
153	        "fish" => Some(Shell::Fish),
154	        "pwsh" | "powershell" => Some(Shell::PowerShell),
155	        "zsh" => Some(Shell::Zsh),
156	        _ => None,
157	    }
158	}
159	
160	fn default_completion_path(shell: Shell) -> PathBuf {
161	    let home = std::env::var_os("HOME")
162	        .map(PathBuf::from)
163	        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
164	    match shell {
165	        Shell::Bash => home
166	            .join(".local")
167	            .join("share")
168	            .join("bash-completion")
169	            .join("completions")
170	            .join("deadreckon"),
171	        Shell::Elvish => home
172	            .join(".config")
173	            .join("elvish")
174	            .join("lib")
175	            .join("deadreckon-completers.elv"),
176	        Shell::Fish => home
177	            .join(".config")
178	            .join("fish")
179	            .join("completions")
180	            .join("deadreckon.fish"),
181	        Shell::PowerShell => home
182	            .join(".config")
183	            .join("powershell")
184	            .join("deadreckon-completions.ps1"),
185	        Shell::Zsh => home.join(".zsh").join("completions").join("_deadreckon"),
186	        _ => home.join(".deadreckon").join("completion"),
187	    }
188	}
189	
190	fn ensure_zsh_completion_rc(completion_path: &Path) -> Result<CompletionRcStatus> {
191	    let Some(completion_dir) = completion_path.parent() else {
192	        return Ok(CompletionRcStatus::Skipped);
193	    };
194	    let home = std::env::var_os("HOME")
195	        .map(PathBuf::from)
196	        .unwrap_or_else(|| PathBuf::from("."));
197	    let zshrc = home.join(".zshrc");
198	    let existing = fs::read_to_string(&zshrc).unwrap_or_default();
199	    let completion_dir = completion_dir.display();
200	    let block = format!(
201	        "\n# >>> deadreckon completion >>>\nfpath=({completion_dir} $fpath)\nautoload -Uz compinit\ncompinit\n# <<< deadreckon completion <<<\n"
202	    );
203	    if existing.contains("# >>> deadreckon completion >>>")
204	        || existing.contains(&format!("fpath=({completion_dir} $fpath)"))
205	    {
206	        return Ok(CompletionRcStatus::Ready(zshrc));
207	    }
208	    let mut file = fs::OpenOptions::new()
209	        .create(true)
210	        .append(true)
211	        .open(&zshrc)?;
212	    file.write_all(block.as_bytes())?;
213	    Ok(CompletionRcStatus::Updated(zshrc))
214	}

185	                return Err(error);
186	            }
187	        }
188	    }
189	    let merged_run = create_merged_plan_run(&paths, &plan, no_gate)?;
190	    plan.status = PlanStatus::Merged;
191	    plan.merged_at = Some(Utc::now());
192	    plan.merged_run_id = Some(merged_run.run_id.clone());
193	    save_plan(&paths, &plan)?;
194	    append_plan_event(
195	        &paths,
196	        &plan.plan_id,
197	        PlanEventKind::MergeCompleted {
198	            merged_run_id: merged_run.run_id.clone(),
199	        },
200	    )?;
201	    append_plan_event(&paths, &plan.plan_id, PlanEventKind::PlanCompleted)?;
202	    let library_dir = paths.library_dir(&merged_run.scope, &merged_run.run_id);
203	    write_plan_merge_manifest(&paths, &library_dir, &plan, &merge.conflicts)?;
204	    let doc_provider = select_plan_doc_provider(&paths, &plan, None)?;
205	    let defaults = config_defaults(&paths)?;
206	    let _manifest = maybe_with_cli_wait_status(
207	        !quiet,
208	        "consolidating plan docs",
209	        refresh_plan_docs(
210	            &paths,
211	            &plan,
212	            PlanDocRefreshOptions {
213	                provider: doc_provider.provider.clone(),
214	                provider_source: doc_provider.source.as_str().to_string(),
215	                budget_cap_usd: defaults.doc_polish_budget_cap_usd,
216	                force: true,
217	            },
218	        ),
219	    )
220	    .await?;
221	    materialize_plan_docs_to_working(&paths, &plan, &library_dir, None)?;
222	    if !quiet && completion_surface {
223	        print_merge_finished(&paths, &plan, &merged_run, &library_dir, no_hints);
224	    }
225	    Ok(())
226	}

228	fn merge_unavailable_plan_surface(paths: &DeadreckonPaths, plan: &Plan) -> VerdictSurface {
229	    let id = run_prefix(&plan.plan_id);
230	    let status = merge_plan_status_word(plan.status);
231	    let kind = match plan.status {
232	        PlanStatus::Merged => VerdictKind::Noop,
233	        _ => VerdictKind::Blocked,
234	    };
235	    let primary = super::plan::plan_next_actions_with_context(paths, plan)
236	        .into_iter()
237	        .next()
238	        .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("deadreckon show {id}"));
239	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
240	        kind,
241	        "plan",
242	        Some(&id),
243	        ExplanationPanel::new(
244	            format!("DeadReckon did not merge the plan because it is {status}."),
245	            "Merge only composes forked or failed plans; the recommended command follows the current plan state instead.",
246	            [
247	                ("plan".to_string(), id.clone()),
248	                ("status".to_string(), status.to_string()),
249	                ("tasks".to_string(), plan.tasks.len().to_string()),
250	            ],
251	        ),
252	        [("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
253	        Vec::<(&str, &str)>::new(),
254	    )
255	    .expect("merge unavailable plan surface must have one primary action")
256	}

380	fn parse_merge_strategy(
381	    plan: &Plan,
382	    strategy: &str,
383	    prefer_child: Option<u32>,
384	    no_hints: bool,
385	) -> Result<PlanMergeStrategy> {
386	    match strategy {
387	        "fail-on-conflict" => Ok(PlanMergeStrategy::FailOnConflict),
388	        "dag-aware" => Ok(PlanMergeStrategy::DagAware),
389	        "prefer-child" => prefer_child
390	            .map(PlanMergeStrategy::PreferChild)
391	            .ok_or_else(|| {
392	                let id = run_prefix(&plan.plan_id);
393	                merge_argument_surface_error(
394	                    plan,
395	                    no_hints,
396	                    "DeadReckon did not merge because prefer-child needs --prefer-child <idx>.",
397	                    "The prefer-child strategy requires a concrete child index so DeadReckon knows which completed child result to keep for conflicting files.",
398	                    vec![
399	                        ("flag".to_string(), "--prefer-child".to_string()),
400	                        ("strategy".to_string(), "prefer-child".to_string()),
401	                    ],
402	                    format!("deadreckon merge {id} --strategy prefer-child --prefer-child 1"),
403	                )
404	            }),
405	        other => Err({
406	            let id = run_prefix(&plan.plan_id);
407	            merge_argument_surface_error(
408	                plan,
409	                no_hints,
410	                format!("DeadReckon did not merge because unknown plan merge strategy {other}."),
411	                "Merge only supports dag-aware, fail-on-conflict, or prefer-child strategies.",
412	                vec![
413	                    ("flag".to_string(), "--strategy".to_string()),
414	                    ("value".to_string(), other.to_string()),
415	                ],
416	                format!("deadreckon merge {id} --strategy dag-aware"),
417	            )
418	        }),
419	    }
420	}

445	fn merge_argument_surface_error(
446	    plan: &Plan,
447	    no_hints: bool,
448	    what_happened: impl Into<String>,
449	    why_this_verdict: impl Into<String>,
450	    mut evidence: Vec<(String, String)>,
451	    primary: String,
452	) -> CliError {

235	fn selection_for_route(

245	        .map_err(|err| setup_refusal_for_provider_error(provider, err))?;
246	    let descriptor = provider

248	        .or_else(|| {

251	                .and_then(|route| registry.get(route.name.as_str()))
252	        });

269	            .or_else(|| route.as_ref().map(|route| provider_kind_label(&route.kind))),
270	        credential: Some(provider_credential_label(descriptor, route.as_ref())),
271	        install_hint: descriptor.and_then(first_install_hint),
272	        warnings: Vec::new(),

275	    if route.as_ref().is_some_and(|route| !route.has_credential) {
276	        if let Some(provider) = selection.provider.as_deref() {

279	            ));
280	        }
281	        if let Some(hint) = selection.install_hint.clone() {
282	            selection.try_lines.push(hint);
283	        } else if let Some(provider) = selection.provider.as_deref() {
284	            selection.try_lines.push(format!(
285	                "deadreckon config set providers.{provider}.api_key <KEY>"
286	            ));
287	        }
288	        if require_usable_route {
289	            let provider_label = selection
290	                .provider
291	                .as_deref()
292	                .or(provider)
293	                .unwrap_or("provider");
294	            return Err(SetupRefusal {
295	                message: selection
296	                    .warnings
297	                    .first()
298	                    .cloned()
299	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| format!("provider {provider_label} is not usable")),
300	                try_line: selection
301	                    .try_lines
302	                    .first()
303	                    .cloned()
304	                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "deadreckon providers list --all".to_string()),
305	            });
306	        }
307	    }
308	    Ok(selection)
309	}
310	
311	fn provider_candidate<'a>(
312	    request: &ProviderSetupRequest<'a>,
313	) -> (Option<&'a str>, SetupProviderSource) {
314	    if let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.explicit_provider) {
315	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::Flag);
316	    }
317	    if matches!(request.role, SetupProviderRoleRef::DocPolish)
318	        && let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.config_doc_provider)
319	    {
320	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::Config);
321	    }
322	    if !matches!(request.role, SetupProviderRoleRef::DocPolish)
323	        && let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.config_default_provider)
324	    {
325	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::Config);
326	    }
327	    if request.allow_auto_subscription
328	        && let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.auto_subscription_provider)
329	    {
330	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::AutoSubscription);
331	    }
332	    if let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.run_provider) {
333	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::RunProvider);
334	    }
335	    if let Some(provider) = non_empty(request.built_in_default_provider) {
336	        return (Some(provider), SetupProviderSource::BuiltInDefault);
337	    }
338	    (None, SetupProviderSource::None)
339	}

343	}

361	fn setup_refusal_for_provider_error(provider: Option<&str>, error: ProviderError) -> SetupRefusal {
362	    match error {
363	        ProviderError::InvalidConfig(message) if message.contains("unknown provider route") => {
364	            match provider {
365	                Some(provider) => SetupRefusal::unknown_provider(provider),
366	                None => SetupRefusal {

370	            }
371	        }

374	            try_line: "deadreckon providers list --all".to_string(),
375	        },
376	    }

380	    descriptor: Option<&ProviderDescriptor>,
381	    route: Option<&ProviderRouteInfo>,
382	) -> String {

384	    match descriptor {
385	        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.subscription && has_credential => "subscription",
386	        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.subscription => "missing",
387	        Some(descriptor) if descriptor.auth.kind == AuthKind::None && has_credential => "none",
388	        Some(_) if has_credential => "ready",
389	        Some(_) => "missing",
390	        None if has_credential => "ready",
391	        None => "missing",
392	    }
393	    .to_string()

296	    print!("{}", kv_block_string("", items));
297	    io::stdout().flush()
298	}
299	
300	/// The shared `key: value` block primitive. The key column is sized to the widest
301	/// key by display width (ANSI-aware), `indent` prefixes every line, and values
302	/// wrap to the terminal. Use this instead of hand-aligned `println!("  k:  v")`
303	/// blocks so every kv surface aligns the same way.
304	fn kv_block_string<K, V>(indent: &str, items: &[(K, V)]) -> String
305	where
306	    K: AsRef<str>,
307	    V: AsRef<str>,
308	{
309	    let key_width = items
310	        .iter()
311	        .map(|(key, _)| ui::display_width(key.as_ref()))
312	        .max()
313	        .unwrap_or(0);
314	    let prefix_width = ui::display_width(indent) + key_width + 2;
315	    let value_width = kv_value_width(prefix_width);
316	    let mut out = String::new();
317	    for (key, value) in items {
318	        let mut first = true;
319	        for logical_line in value
320	            .as_ref()
321	            .lines()
322	            .chain(value.as_ref().is_empty().then_some(""))
323	        {
324	            for line in wrap_kv_value(logical_line, value_width) {
325	                if first {
326	                    first = false;
327	                    out.push_str(indent);
328	                    // Dim the key (label) so it reads as subordinate to its value;
329	                    // ui::render is gated on a TTY, so plain output is unchanged.
330	                    out.push_str(&ui::render(
331	                        ui::Stream::Stdout,
332	                        ui::Tone::Muted,
333	                        ui::pad_visible(key.as_ref(), key_width),
334	                    ));
335	                    out.push_str(": ");
336	                    out.push_str(&line);
337	                } else {
338	                    out.push_str(&" ".repeat(prefix_width));
339	                    out.push_str(&line);
340	                }
341	                out.push('\n');
342	            }
```
</details></tool-use>

201	pub(crate) fn strip_ansi(text: &str) -> String {
202	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len());
203	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
204	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
205	        if read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars).is_some() {

208	        out.push(ch);

213	#[allow(dead_code)]
214	pub(crate) fn read_ansi_sequence<I>(first: char, chars: &mut Peekable<I>) -> Option<(String, bool)>
215	where
216	    I: Iterator<Item = char>,
217	{
218	    if first != ANSI_ESC || chars.peek() != Some(&'[') {
219	        return None;
220	    }
221	    let mut sequence = String::from(first);
222	    if let Some(bracket) = chars.next() {
223	        sequence.push(bracket);
224	    }
225	    for code in chars.by_ref() {
226	        sequence.push(code);
227	        if code.is_ascii_alphabetic() {
228	            let active = sequence != ANSI_RESET;
229	            return Some((sequence, active));
230	        }
231	    }
232	    Some((sequence, false))
233	}

235	/// Display width of `text` in terminal columns: ANSI escape sequences are
236	/// stripped first, then each glyph is measured by its Unicode display width so
237	/// wide (CJK / full-width) glyphs count as two columns and zero-width / combining
238	/// marks count as zero. This is the single width function behind every pad,
239	/// truncate, and column-alignment site.
240	#[allow(dead_code)] // used by ui_card today; kv_block/columns/prompt sites adopt it in later phases.
241	pub(crate) fn display_width(text: &str) -> usize {
242	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthStr;
243	    UnicodeWidthStr::width(strip_ansi(text).as_str())
244	}
245	
246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}
259	
260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

314	/// Color the leading status token of `value` (e.g. `PASSED` in `PASSED 1/1`,
315	/// `completed` in `completed -> done`) by its status tone, leaving the rest
316	/// plain. A value whose leading token is not a recognized status is returned
317	/// unchanged. Safe for an unpadded (last-column / kv) value.
318	#[allow(dead_code)]
319	pub(crate) fn color_status_word(value: &str) -> String {
320	    let mut parts = value.splitn(2, ' ');
321	    let Some(first) = parts.next() else {
322	        return value.to_string();
323	    };
324	    let tone = status_tone(first);
325	    if tone == Tone::Plain {
326	        return value.to_string();
327	    }

329	        Some(rest) => format!("{} {}", render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first), rest),
330	        None => render(Stream::Stdout, tone, first),
331	    }
332	}

433	fn current_terminal_width() -> usize {
434	    crossterm::terminal::size()
435	        .ok()
436	        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
437	        .or_else(|| {
438	            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
439	                .ok()
440	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
441	        })
442	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 0)
443	        .unwrap_or(120)
444	}

446	fn replacement_line_text(text: &str, terminal_width: usize) -> String {
447	    let visible_limit = terminal_width.saturating_sub(1);
448	    truncate_visible_single_line(text, visible_limit)
449	}
450	
451	fn truncate_visible_single_line(text: &str, max_visible: usize) -> String {
452	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
453	    if max_visible == 0 {
454	        return String::new();
455	    }
456	    let mut out = String::with_capacity(text.len().min(max_visible));
457	    let mut chars = text.chars().peekable();
458	    let mut visible = 0usize;
459	    let mut style_active = false;
460	    while let Some(ch) = chars.next() {
461	        if let Some((sequence, active)) = read_ansi_sequence(ch, &mut chars) {
462	            style_active = active;
463	            out.push_str(&sequence);
464	            continue;
465	        }
466	        let glyph = match ch {
467	            '\n' | '\r' => ' ',
468	            _ => ch,
469	        };
470	        let glyph_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(glyph).unwrap_or(0);
471	        if visible + glyph_width > max_visible {
472	            break;
473	        }
474	        out.push(glyph);
475	        visible += glyph_width;
476	    }
477	    if style_active {
478	        out.push_str(ANSI_RESET);
479	    }
480	    out
481	}

`ui_status` colors a whole status label. "cancelled" classifies via `Status::classify` — it contains no negative/paused/warn keyword and isn't in the Ok/Running/Note match arms, so it resolves to `Status::Unknown` → `Tone::Plain`. That means `ui_status("cancelled")` returns "cancelled" unchanged even on a TTY. 264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;

267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();

277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }

284	                chunk_width += ch_width;

286	            current = chunk;

289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {

292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)

```
Then line 198: `print_campaign_wrapped("    ", &primary, CAMPAIGN_WRAP_WIDTH);`

`print_campaign_wrapped` (line 228-232) wraps the raw text into lines and prints each with indent. If I wrap `primary` in `ui_command` before passing, the ANSI codes would be fed into `wrap_words` which is ANSI-naive (it uses `display_width` which strips ANSI for width, but it splits on whitespace and would break the ANSI codes across lines — corrupting them). So I should NOT color a multi-line-wrapped command. 

This is a command suggestion that gets word-wrapped. Per the invariants, wrapping colored text through an ANSI-naive wrapper is dangerous. The command could wrap across lines (the goal can be long). Coloring it safely would require coloring each wrapped line after wrapping, which `print_campaign_wrapped` doesn't support generically (it's used for prose too). 

Given the hazard and that `print_campaign_wrapped` is shared with prose/goal text, I'll leave the wrapped command at line 198 plain and record it in left_plain. This is the conservative, golden-safe choice. (Coloring it would risk splitting ANSI across wrap boundaries.)

Let me double check whether the goal here could realistically wrap. `CAMPAIGN_WRAP_WIDTH = 88`, indent 4 → 84 cols. A `deadreckon campaign "<goal>" --n N --yes` with a long goal absolutely can exceed 84 cols → multi-line → ANSI corruption risk. Confirmed: leave plain.

283	fn print_kv_block<K, V>(items: &[(K, V)])
284	where
285	    K: AsRef<str>,
286	    V: AsRef<str>,
287	{
288	    let _ = write_kv_block(items);
289	}
290	
291	fn write_kv_block<K, V>(items: &[(K, V)]) -> io::Result<()>
292	where
293	    K: AsRef<str>,
294	    V: AsRef<str>,
295	{
296	    print!("{}", kv_block_string("", items));
297	    io::stdout().flush()
298	}
299	
300	/// The shared `key: value` block primitive. The key column is sized to the widest
301	/// key by display width (ANSI-aware), `indent` prefixes every line, and values
302	/// wrap to the terminal. Use this instead of hand-aligned `println!("  k:  v")`
303	/// blocks so every kv surface aligns the same way.
304	fn kv_block_string<K, V>(indent: &str, items: &[(K, V)]) -> String
305	where
306	    K: AsRef<str>,
307	    V: AsRef<str>,
308	{
309	    let key_width = items
310	        .iter()
311	        .map(|(key, _)| ui::display_width(key.as_ref()))
312	        .max()
313	        .unwrap_or(0);
314	    let prefix_width = ui::display_width(indent) + key_width + 2;
315	    let value_width = kv_value_width(prefix_width);
316	    let mut out = String::new();
317	    for (key, value) in items {
318	        let mut first = true;
319	        for logical_line in value
320	            .as_ref()
321	            .lines()
322	            .chain(value.as_ref().is_empty().then_some(""))
323	        {
324	            for line in wrap_kv_value(logical_line, value_width) {
325	                if first {
326	                    first = false;
327	                    out.push_str(indent);
328	                    // Dim the key (label) so it reads as subordinate to its value;
329	                    // ui::render is gated on a TTY, so plain output is unchanged.
330	                    out.push_str(&ui::render(
331	                        ui::Stream::Stdout,
332	                        ui::Tone::Muted,
333	                        ui::pad_visible(key.as_ref(), key_width),
334	                    ));
335	                    out.push_str(": ");
336	                    out.push_str(&line);
337	                } else {
338	                    out.push_str(&" ".repeat(prefix_width));
339	                    out.push_str(&line);
340	                }
341	                out.push('\n');
342	            }
343	        }
344	    }
345	    out
346	}
347	
348	fn kv_value_width(prefix_width: usize) -> usize {
349	    let terminal_width = crossterm::terminal::size()
350	        .ok()
351	        .map(|(columns, _)| usize::from(columns))
352	        .or_else(|| {
353	            std::env::var("COLUMNS")
354	                .ok()
355	                .and_then(|columns| columns.parse::<usize>().ok())
356	        })
357	        .filter(|columns| *columns > 1)
358	        .unwrap_or(120)
359	        .saturating_sub(1);
360	    terminal_width.saturating_sub(prefix_width).max(20)
361	}
362	
363	fn wrap_kv_value(value: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
364	    ui::wrap_words(value, width)
365	}

I analyzed all six files and determined that **no code changes are warranted** — every user-facing output site is already golden-safe and colored at the correct layer.

Key findings:

- **`merge.rs` and `setup.rs`** contain zero output macros (no `println!`/`print!`/`eprintln!`/`write!`). They only build `VerdictSurface`/`ExplanationPanel` objects and plain data strings (e.g. `ProviderSetupSelection::row_value`) that are colored downstream.

- **`doctor.rs`, `init.rs`, `seams.rs`, `completion.rs`** route all human-readable output through `surface.render_plain(...)`, which lives in `verdict_surface.rs` (outside the task's edit list) and already applies color: `kind.tone()` to the status label, `Tone::Heading` to the Explanation/Evidence/Recommended/Secondary headings, and `Tone::Muted` to kv keys. The remaining direct prints are JSON (`serde_json::to_string_pretty`), raw shell-completion scripts (`write_completion_script`), and `init.rs:68`, which already wraps the success word in `ui_ok` with a deliberately-plain path.

Coloring anything here would either nest ANSI inside an already-colored `{line}`, tint a path/JSON/script (forbidden), or duplicate the renderer's work and risk breaking the `{:<N}` alignment that `main.rs::print_provider_setup_rows` performs. Per the conservative invariant, leaving every site plain is the correct golden-safe outcome. Full per-site classification is in the structured `left_plain` output.

If the goal was to push color *deeper* (e.g. status-word tinting of seam `outcome`/`decision` evidence values or run/plan ids in evidence rows), that belongs in `verdict_surface.rs::render_plain`, not these caller files.

Color is applied ONLY through existing helpers, every one of which is gated on a TTY
(crate::ui::enabled). In non-TTY/piped output they return PLAIN text, so byte-for-byte
output is unchanged — that is what keeps the golden tests green. NEVER hand-write ANSI.

Helpers (all in crate::ui::, already imported in command files as bare names):

  LEADING status token of a string; render_status(ui::Stream::Stdout, label) or
  ui_status(label) color a whole status label.
- section headings: ui_heading("text")
- kv keys / labels (the "key:" part): ui_muted("label:")
- run/plan/chain ids, run-prefixes, SHAs, hashes: ui_id(text)
- command suggestions ("deadreckon ..."): ui_command(text)
- success word/glyph: ui_ok(text); warning: ui_warn(text)
- errors to stderr: ui::render(ui::Stream::Stderr, ui::Tone::Negative, text)

FIXED-WIDTH COLUMNS — the one true hazard:
- NEVER place colored text inside a {:<N} / {:>N} format pad. ANSI bytes count toward
  the pad width and shatter column alignment on a TTY.
- Instead drop the pad to {} and wrap with ui::pad_visible(colored_text, N), which pads
  by DISPLAY width (ANSI stripped). Right-aligned numeric {:>N} stays as-is (numbers
  are not colored).
- Reference implementations to mirror: commands/chain/mod.rs print_chain_table uses

  commands/inspection.rs append_list_row uses pad_rendered(value, WIDTH, Some(ui_status)).

DO NOT color (leave exactly plain):
- file paths and directories
- raw git output (diff --stat, git log passthrough)
- machine/JSON/tab-separated/porcelain/export/--plain formats
- a value that is a pre-built string already colored upstream, e.g. println!("{line}")
  where line was built with ui:: — verify the source before touching
- descriptive prose VALUES that follow a colored label (color the label only)

- Use the helper style already present in the file (match local idiom). pad_rendered /

use std::io::{self, IsTerminal, Write as _};
use std::iter::Peekable;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};

use ratatui::style::Color;

static PLAIN_OUTPUT: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
#[allow(dead_code)]
const ANSI_ESC: char = '\u{1b}';
const ANSI_RESET: &str = "\x1b[0m";

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Stream {
    Stdout,
    Stderr,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Tone {
    #[allow(dead_code)]
    Plain,
    Heading,
    Muted,
    Id,
    Command,
    Ok,
    Warn,
    Paused,
    Note,
    Negative,
    Prompt,
    Hint,
}

impl Tone {
    /// The single tone->ANSI SGR-parameter table for line output. `None` means
    /// the tone carries no color (plain text).
    pub(crate) const fn to_ansi(self) -> Option<&'static str> {
        match self {
            Tone::Plain => None,
            Tone::Heading => Some("1;36"),
            Tone::Muted => Some("2"),
            Tone::Id => Some("1;35"),
            Tone::Command => Some("1;34"),
            Tone::Ok => Some("1;32"),
            Tone::Warn => Some("1;33"),
            Tone::Paused => Some("1;33"),
            Tone::Note => Some("2"),
            Tone::Negative => Some("1;31"),
            Tone::Prompt => Some("1;36"),
            Tone::Hint => Some("1;34"),
        }
    }

    /// The single tone->ratatui::Color table for the TUI, derived from the same
    /// Tone enum so a status renders the same color on a line and in a frame.
    pub(crate) const fn to_tui_color(self) -> Color {
        match self {
            Tone::Plain => Color::Reset,
            Tone::Heading | Tone::Prompt => Color::Cyan,
            Tone::Muted | Tone::Note => Color::DarkGray,
            Tone::Id => Color::Magenta,
            Tone::Command | Tone::Hint => Color::Blue,
            Tone::Ok => Color::Green,
            Tone::Warn | Tone::Paused => Color::Yellow,
            Tone::Negative => Color::Red,
        }
    }
}

/// The closed set of lifecycle status classes. `status_tone` resolves a free-form
/// status string into exactly one of these — including an explicit `Unknown` —
/// so an unrecognized status renders in a visible default tone rather than being
/// silently folded into a dim catch-all, and so adding a class is a compile error.
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Status {
    Ok,
    Running,
    Paused,
    Warn,
    Negative,
    Note,
    Unknown,
}

impl Status {
    pub(crate) fn classify(status: &str) -> Status {
        let status = status.trim().to_ascii_lowercase();
        if status.contains("failed")
            || status.contains("killed")
            || status.contains("error")
            || status.contains("missing")
            || status.contains("refused")
        {
            return Status::Negative;
        }
        if status.contains("paused") {
            return Status::Paused;
        }
        if status.contains("warning") || status.contains("warn") {
            return Status::Warn;
        }
        match status.as_str() {
            "ok" | "ready" | "set" | "wrote" | "updated" | "installed" | "completed" | "passed"
            | "polished" | "applied" | "cleaned" | "exported" => Status::Ok,
            "running" => Status::Running,
            "pending" | "planned" | "skipped" | "undone" | "recorded" | "note" => Status::Note,
            _ => Status::Unknown,
        }
    }

    pub(crate) const fn tone(self) -> Tone {
        match self {
            Status::Ok => Tone::Ok,
            Status::Running => Tone::Heading,
            Status::Paused => Tone::Paused,
            Status::Warn => Tone::Warn,
            Status::Negative => Tone::Negative,
            Status::Note => Tone::Note,
            // Unknown stays a visible default rather than a dim that hides it.
            Status::Unknown => Tone::Plain,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) struct TuiPalette {
    pub(crate) border_focused: Color,
    pub(crate) border_idle: Color,
    pub(crate) status_running: Color,
    pub(crate) status_completed: Color,
    pub(crate) status_failed: Color,
    pub(crate) acceptance_default: Color,
    pub(crate) acceptance_configured: Color,
    pub(crate) acceptance_running: Color,
    pub(crate) acceptance_passed: Color,
    pub(crate) acceptance_failed: Color,
    pub(crate) spend_low: Color,
    pub(crate) spend_mid: Color,
    pub(crate) spend_high: Color,
    pub(crate) spend_pause_cap: Color,
}

pub(crate) const TUI_PALETTE: TuiPalette = TuiPalette {
    border_focused: Color::Cyan,
    border_idle: Color::Reset,
    // Derived from the shared Tone so line and TUI status colors cannot drift.
    status_running: Status::Running.tone().to_tui_color(),
    status_completed: Status::Ok.tone().to_tui_color(),
    status_failed: Status::Negative.tone().to_tui_color(),
    acceptance_default: Color::DarkGray,
    acceptance_configured: Color::Yellow,
    acceptance_running: Color::Cyan,
    acceptance_passed: Color::Green,
    acceptance_failed: Color::Red,
    spend_low: Color::Green,
    spend_mid: Color::Yellow,
    spend_high: Color::Red,
    spend_pause_cap: Color::Magenta,
};

pub(crate) fn set_plain_output(plain: bool) {
    PLAIN_OUTPUT.store(plain, Ordering::Relaxed);
}

pub(crate) fn enabled(stream: Stream) -> bool {
    if PLAIN_OUTPUT.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
        return false;
    }
    if std::env::var_os("NO_COLOR").is_some() {
        return false;
    }
    if std::env::var("TERM").is_ok_and(|term| term == "dumb") {
        return false;
    }
    stream_is_terminal(stream)
}

pub(crate) fn render(stream: Stream, tone: Tone, text: impl AsRef<str>) -> String {
    let text = text.as_ref();
    let Some(code) = tone.to_ansi() else {
        return text.to_string();
    };
    if enabled(stream) {
        ansi_wrap(code, text)
    } else {
        text.to_string()
    }
}

pub(crate) fn ansi_wrap(code: &str, text: &str) -> String {
    format!("\x1b[{code}m{text}{ANSI_RESET}")
}

#[allow(dead_code)]
pub(crate) fn ansi_reset() -> &'static str {
    ANSI_RESET
}

246	/// Right-pad `text` with spaces to `width` DISPLAY columns (ANSI-aware). Use this
247	/// for column alignment instead of `{:<N}`: a `{:<N}` format-pad counts the ANSI
248	/// escape bytes of a styled cell, so a colored column ends up short and misaligns
249	/// against its plain header.
250	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P3/P5/P6.
251	pub(crate) fn pad_visible(text: &str, width: usize) -> String {
252	    let used = display_width(text);
253	    if used >= width {
254	        text.to_string()
255	    } else {
256	        format!("{text}{}", " ".repeat(width - used))
257	    }
258	}

260	/// Word-wrap `text` to `width` display columns, breaking words longer than the
261	/// width. This is the single wrap engine behind the kv block, run list, and
262	/// campaign facts. Wrap RAW (unstyled) text — it is ANSI-naive.
263	#[allow(dead_code)] // call sites adopt it across P10.
264	pub(crate) fn wrap_words(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String> {
265	    use unicode_width::UnicodeWidthChar;
266	    let width = width.max(1);
267	    let mut lines: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
268	    let mut current = String::new();
269	    for word in text.split_whitespace() {
270	        if display_width(word) > width {
271	            if !current.is_empty() {
272	                lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
273	            }
274	            // Break a too-long word into width-sized chunks.
275	            let mut chunk = String::new();
276	            let mut chunk_width = 0usize;
277	            for ch in word.chars() {
278	                let ch_width = UnicodeWidthChar::width(ch).unwrap_or(0);
279	                if chunk_width + ch_width > width {
280	                    lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut chunk));
281	                    chunk_width = 0;
282	                }
283	                chunk.push(ch);
284	                chunk_width += ch_width;
285	            }
286	            current = chunk;
287	            continue;
288	        }
289	        let next = if current.is_empty() {
290	            display_width(word)
291	        } else {
292	            display_width(&current) + 1 + display_width(word)
293	        };
294	        if next <= width {
295	            if !current.is_empty() {
296	                current.push(' ');
297	            }
298	            current.push_str(word);
299	        } else {
300	            lines.push(std::mem::take(&mut current));
301	            current.push_str(word);
302	        }
303	    }
304	    if !current.is_empty() || lines.is_empty() {
305	        lines.push(current);
306	    }
307	    lines
308	}

- kv keys / labels (the "key:" part): ui_muted("label:")
- run/plan/chain ids, run-prefixes, SHAs, hashes: ui_id(text)
- command suggestions ("deadreckon ..."): ui_command(text)
- success word/glyph: ui_ok(text); warning: ui_warn(text)
- errors to stderr: ui::render(ui::Stream::Stderr, ui::Tone::Negative, text)

FIXED-WIDTH COLUMNS — the one true hazard:
- NEVER place colored text inside a {:<N} / {:>N} format pad. ANSI bytes count toward
  the pad width and shatter column alignment on a TTY.
- Instead drop the pad to {} and wrap with ui::pad_visible(colored_text, N), which pads
  by DISPLAY width (ANSI stripped). Right-aligned numeric {:>N} stays as-is (numbers
  are not colored).
- Reference implementations to mirror: commands/chain/mod.rs print_chain_table uses
  ui::pad_visible(&ui_id(&id), 9) and ui::pad_visible(&ui_status(label), 10);
  commands/inspection.rs append_list_row uses pad_rendered(value, WIDTH, Some(ui_status)).
  For table HEADER rows, color each header cell with ui_muted(...) wrapped in pad_visible.

DO NOT color (leave exactly plain):
- file paths and directories
- raw git output (diff --stat, git log passthrough)
- machine/JSON/tab-separated/porcelain/export/--plain formats
- a value that is a pre-built string already colored upstream, e.g. println!("{line}")
  where line was built with ui:: — verify the source before touching
- descriptive prose VALUES that follow a colored label (color the label only)

ABSOLUTE RULES:
- Do NOT change literal text content. Only wrap existing text in a color helper. Non-TTY
  output MUST stay byte-identical.
- Use the helper style already present in the file (match local idiom). pad_rendered /
  pad_plain are LOCAL to inspection.rs; everywhere else use ui::pad_visible.
- The file must still compile (helpers take impl AsRef<str>; pad_visible takes &str).
- Read each file fully (or grep print sites) before editing; Edit requires a prior Read.

pub(crate) fn print_acceptance_results(results: &[deadreckon_core::AcceptanceCheckResult]) {
    for result in results {
        let mark = if result.passed {
            ui_ok("✓")
        } else if result.must_pass {
            ui::render(ui::Stream::Stdout, ui::Tone::Negative, "✗")
        } else {
            ui_warn("!")

        let requirement = if result.must_pass {
            "required"
        } else {
            "optional"
        };
        let elapsed = result
            .duration_ms
            .map(|ms| format!(" ({:.1}s)", ms as f64 / 1000.0))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        println!(
            "  {mark} {:<13} {:<8} {}{}",
            result.kind, requirement, result.detail, elapsed
        );

            }
            if let Some(stderr) = result.stderr.as_deref() {

const CAMPAIGN_WRAP_WIDTH: usize = 88;

fn print_campaign_fact(label: &str, value: &str) {
    println!("  {} {value}", crate::ui::pad_visible(&ui_muted(label), 9));
}

fn print_campaign_sub_goal(sub: &deadreckon_core::campaign::SubGoal) {
    println!("  {}", ui_id(&sub.sub_id));
    if let Some((body, acceptance)) = split_acceptance_clause(&sub.goal) {
        print_campaign_wrapped("    ", body, CAMPAIGN_WRAP_WIDTH);
        println!("    {}", ui_heading("Acceptance"));
        print_campaign_wrapped("      ", acceptance, CAMPAIGN_WRAP_WIDTH);
    } else {
        print_campaign_wrapped("    ", &sub.goal, CAMPAIGN_WRAP_WIDTH);
    }
}

fn split_acceptance_clause(goal: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)> {
    let (body, acceptance) = goal.split_once("Acceptance:")?;
    Some((body.trim(), acceptance.trim()))
}

fn print_campaign_wrapped(indent: &str, value: &str, width: usize) {
    for line in wrap_campaign_words(value, width.saturating_sub(indent.chars().count())) {
        println!("{indent}{line}");
    }
}

pub(crate) fn columns(headers: &[&str], rows: &[Vec<String>]) -> String {
    let col_count = headers.len();
    let mut widths: Vec<usize> = headers.iter().map(|h| ui::display_width(h)).collect();
    for row in rows {
        for (index, cell) in row.iter().enumerate().take(col_count) {
            widths[index] = widths[index].max(ui::display_width(cell));
        }
    }
    let mut out = String::new();
    let mut push_row = |cells: &[&str]| {
        for (index, cell) in cells.iter().enumerate().take(col_count) {
            if index > 0 {
                out.push_str("  ");
            }
            if index + 1 == col_count {
                out.push_str(cell);
            } else {
                out.push_str(&ui::pad_visible(cell, widths[index]));
            }
        }
        out.push('\n');
    };
    push_row(headers);
    for row in rows {
        let cells = row.iter().map(String::as_str).collect::<Vec<_>>();
        push_row(&cells);
    }
    out
}

This is the **TUI refactor goal you carved off earlier** in the session (the one you wanted kept separate from "everything else"). It's a pure presentation/chrome refactor of the interactive attach TUI. Here's what executing it produces.

## The outcome in one line

Today the attach TUI's controls **change depending on what you attached to** (run vs plan vs campaign vs chain), because each surface re-implements its own key handling, glyph, footer, and confirm logic. After this slice, **all attach surfaces share one set of chrome** while each keeps its own content body.

## Concrete behavior changes (what you'd notice)

| Area | Today | After |
|---|---|---|
| **Paging keys** (PgUp/PgDn/Home/End/g/G) | only in run-attach | work in **run, plan, campaign, chain** alike |
| **Selection highlight** | `*` in some places, `>` in others | one `selection_glyph()` everywhere |
| **Footer** | 4 different styles + a brittle `parent_plan_footer.replace()` hack | one `footer(items)` builder, always lists active keys incl. `Esc`/`q` |
| **Scroll readout** | only on run panels | `first-last/total` indicator on **every** list panel |
| **Apply / Abandon** | fire instantly — one mistyped key is destructive | require a **two-step confirm** (key, then `y`); ambiguous `b` (back vs abandon) and `d` (docs vs detach) split into distinct keys |
| **Exit/return** | `press Enter to return` (Enter only); Enter on a dead child = silent no-op | prompts also accept `q`/`Esc`; `Esc`=graceful back, `Ctrl-D`=detach; unloadable child shows an "unavailable" notice |
| **Empty panels** | leak internal filenames (`campaign-events.jsonl`, `plan-events.jsonl`) | one-line next step, **never** a filename |
| **Chain step glyphs** (`○●◐✗↷◉↶`) | Unicode only | ASCII fallback set + legend under `--plain`/non-VT (Windows) |

## How it lands

11 TDD phases (P1–P11), each: write the named depth test → watch it fail → narrow change → `fmt`/`clippy`/`cargo test` green → conventional commit → CHANGELOG line.
- **P1–P4**: extract a shared key dispatcher (run-panel semantics are the reference) and route plan/campaign/chain onto it, each supplying only a `mode_key()` hook.
- **P5–P7**: one glyph, one footer, one scroll indicator.
- **P8–P9**: confirm-before-destructive + uniform exit/return.
- **P10**: empty states, single narrative-split breakpoint, Windows glyph fallback.
- **P11**: docs only (AS-BUILT section, CHANGELOG, V1-CANDIDATES for deferred items).

## What it explicitly does *not* change

- **No new capability** — no new attach target kinds.
- **No runtime schema changes** — `PipelineState`/plans/campaigns/chains/projections stay byte-identical on disk.
- **Content panels untouched** — run turn stream, plan child-ref tree, campaign feed, chain step graph, narrative projection all render the same data; only the surrounding chrome is unified.
- **Run behavior must not regress** (it's the reference), and byte-exact ratatui golden frames are the contract — updated deliberately per phase.
- No `git push`; local phased commits inside the repo.

## Worth noting given this session

- Its stated **dependency — the Uniform Surface primitives (`ui::Tone`/`display_width`/`kv_block`) — now exist** (that's the sibling slice already on `main`), so it can land cleanly rather than stubbing.
- Part of **P10 is already partially in place**: the colorization work this session added a `chain_step_glyph(status, ascii)` ASCII fallback and a TTY-gated `chain_step_dot_for_output`. So the glyph-fallback phase would be largely confirm-and-test rather than net-new.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 20:45:47Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 20:45:55Z)**_

No — not in the speed sense. This is explicitly a presentation refactor ("uniform chrome, mode-specific content… chrome only"), so nothing on the performance-critical path changes:

- **Render cost is unchanged.** The expensive part of a TUI frame is the content panels — run turn stream, plan child tree, campaign feed, chain step graph, narrative projection — and the rider forbids touching those. Unifying the footer/glyph/scroll-indicator draws the same widgets; it doesn't draw fewer.
- **Keypress latency is unchanged.** Going from four `handle_key`s to one shared dispatcher + per-mode hook is a code-organization change. Key handling already runs once per human keystroke, not in a hot loop — one extra layer of indirection is microseconds, imperceptible.
- **No data-path changes.** No schema changes, no change to how events are read or projected, which is what actually gates "feels sluggish."

Where it *does* feel faster is **to operate**, not to compute:

- **Paging keys gained.** Plan/campaign/chain get `PgUp/PgDn/Home/End/g/G`, so you jump pages or leap to the ends instead of holding the arrow key down a long list. That's a real navigation-speed win on big plans/chains.
- **Transferable muscle memory.** One control scheme across run/plan/campaign/chain means you stop re-learning (and mis-pressing) controls when you switch what you attached to — fewer wasted keystrokes.

And one place it's deliberately a keystroke *slower*: Apply/Abandon now require a confirm key (`y`) — intentional safety, since today a single mistyped key fires them.

So: same performance, meaningfully better *to drive* on large lists, and safer on destructive actions. If actual TUI latency on big runs is what you're worried about, that'd be a separate profiling task — say the word and I'll look at the render/event-read path instead.

75	                        && (!io::stdout().is_terminal() || args.plain)
76	                    {
77	                        print_plan_narrative_plain(&paths, &plan, args.visual)?;
78	                    } else if io::stdout().is_terminal() && !args.plain && !args.json {
79	                        print_attach_banner("plan", &plan.plan_id);
80	                        attach_plan_tui(
81	                            &paths,
82	                            &plan.plan_id,
83	                            show_hints,
84	                            args.view,
85	                            args.visual,
86	                            narrative_config.clone(),
87	                            None,
88	                        )
89	                        .await?;
90	                    } else {
91	                        print_plan_summary(&paths, &plan, show_hints);
92	                    }
93	                    return Ok(());
94	                }
95	                if commands::chain::resolve_chain_id(&paths, &run_ref, false).is_ok() {
96	                    if args.view.is_narrative() || args.json {
97	                        return print_chain_narrative_refusal(&run_ref, args.json);
98	                    }
99	                    return commands::chain::chain_attach_command(&paths, &run_ref, args.plain);
100	                }
101	                return Err(run_error);
102	            }
103	        }
104	    };
105	    let run_id = state.run_id.clone();
106	    let show_hints = completion_hints_enabled(args.no_hints);
107	    if args.view.is_narrative() && args.json {
108	        print_run_narrative_json(&state, parent_plan.as_ref(), args.visual)?;
109	        return Ok(());
110	    }
111	    if args.view.is_narrative() && (!io::stdout().is_terminal() || args.plain) {
112	        print_run_narrative_plain(&state, parent_plan.as_ref(), args.visual)?;
113	        return Ok(());
114	    }
115	    if io::stdout().is_terminal() && !args.plain && !args.json {
116	        print_attach_banner("run", &run_id);
117	        if parent_plan.is_some() {
118	            attach_tui_with_parent(
119	                &paths,
120	                &run_id,
121	                show_hints,
122	                parent_plan,
123	                args.view,
124	                args.visual,
125	                narrative_config.clone(),
126	            )
127	            .await?;
128	        } else {
129	            attach_tui(
130	                &paths,
131	                &run_id,
132	                show_hints,
133	                args.view,
134	                args.visual,
135	                narrative_config.clone(),
136	            )
137	            .await?;
138	        }
139	        let state = load_run(&paths, &run_id)?;
140	        if state.status == RunStatus::Completed && show_hints {
141	            print_exit_summary_card(&state, &RunLoopOutcome::Done, args.plain, true);
142	            print_chain_context_for_working(&state.working_dir);
143	        }
144	        return Ok(());
145	    }
146	    if let Some(parent_plan) = parent_plan.as_ref() {
147	        println!(
148	            "plan {} / {} -> run {}",
149	            ui_id(run_prefix(&parent_plan.plan_id)),
150	            ui_id(&parent_plan.task_id),
151	            ui_id(run_prefix(&state.run_id))
152	        );
153	    }
154	    if state.status == RunStatus::Completed && show_hints {
155	        print_exit_summary_card(&state, &RunLoopOutcome::Done, args.plain, true);
156	        print_chain_context_for_working(&state.working_dir);
157	    } else {
158	        print_run_summary(&state);
159	    }
160	    Ok(())
161	}

235	fn run_projection_for_plain(
236	    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,

238	    visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
239	) -> Result<narrative::NarrativeProjection> {

274	pub(crate) fn chain_narrative_refusal_text(run_ref: &str, json_output: bool) -> Result<String> {
275	    let surface = chain_narrative_refusal_surface(run_ref);
276	    if json_output {
277	        return Ok(format!(
278	            "{}\n",
279	            serde_json::to_string_pretty(&surface.add_to_json(json!({
280	                "status": "unsupported",
281	                "kind": "chain",
282	                "id": run_ref,
283	                "message": "Narrative attach is currently supported for runs, plans, and plan child refs.",
284	                "try": [
285	                    "deadreckon chain status",
286	                    "deadreckon attach <run-id> --view narrative",
287	                    "deadreckon attach <plan-id> --view narrative"
288	                ]
289	            })))?
290	        ));
291	    }
292	    Ok(surface.render_plain(false))
293	}
294	
295	fn chain_narrative_refusal_surface(run_ref: &str) -> VerdictSurface {
296	    let primary = format!("deadreckon chain status {run_ref}");
297	    VerdictSurface::try_new(
298	        VerdictKind::Blocked,
299	        "chain narrative",
300	        Some(run_ref),
301	        ExplanationPanel::new(
302	            "Chain narrative attach is not supported yet.",
303	            "Narrative attach currently supports runs, plans, and plan child refs; chain status is the supported chain inspection path.",
304	            vec![
305	                ("chain", run_ref),
306	                ("view", "narrative"),
307	                ("supported narrative targets", "run, plan, plan child"),
308	            ],
309	        ),
310	        vec![("Recommended", primary.as_str())],
311	        vec![
312	            ("Secondary", "deadreckon attach <run-id> --view narrative"),
313	            ("Secondary", "deadreckon attach <plan-id> --view narrative"),
314	        ],
315	    )
316	    .expect("chain narrative refusal surface must be valid")
317	}
