This confirms several things and surfaces another per-frame cost:

1. The narrative projection **signature** (render.rs:828) is O(1) — it hashes `.len()` and `.last()`, not iterating all events/spend/traces. Good: the narrative cache is correctly gated so the expensive narrative build only runs when the signature changes. But the signature only covers narrative view.

2. `attach_panel_counts` (attach_state.rs:353/355) calls `run_narrative_lines(...)` or `attach_activity_lines_for_tui(...)` and takes `.len()` — these BUILD the full line vectors from ALL `events`/`spend`/`traces` **every frame** just to count rows for clamping. This is O(events + spend + traces) per frame, on the UI thread, every tick AND every keypress (clamp runs in the loop body before draw). Since `events` is uncapped (grows with run length), this is genuinely O(run length) per frame. And `render_attach` itself then rebuilds the same lines a second time to actually render. 

3. `live_file` (line 11585) does a `fs::metadata` syscall per file — combined with the recursive walk, that's O(source files) stat syscalls per frame.

4. `live_pid` (line 11599) spawns a `ps` subprocess per supervised PID every frame.

I have a complete, well-evidenced picture. I've completed the projection-io analysis. Here is the summary of findings.

## Where displayed data comes from in the attach TUI

I mapped all three event loops in `attach.rs` (run: lines 700-900, plan: 414-690, campaign: 319-411) down through the projection/load functions in `deadreckon-core` and the render path in `tui/render.rs`.

### What is done RIGHT (incremental, not re-read per frame)
- **Append-only event/JSONL tails are correctly incremental.** `AttachJsonlTail` (main.rs:11135), `TuiEventFeed` (tui_events.rs:46), and `PlanEventBus`'s `JsonlTail` all use a `(len + mtime)` signature early-return plus a saved byte offset + `SeekFrom::Start`, so spend.jsonl / traces.jsonl / flight / events.jsonl read only newly-appended bytes. No O(history) re-parse there.
- **Narrative projection is gated by an O(1) signature** (render.rs:828 hashes `.len()`/`.last()`, not contents) so the expensive narrative build only runs on change.
- **Provider-log scan is throttled** to a 5s/30s freshness window (main.rs:11663).

### What is NOT — per-frame work on the UI/draw thread (every idle tick AND every keypress redraw)
The answer to "does each draw/tick re-read files / does cost scale with run length" is **yes, in three places**:

1. **O(run length) line rebuild — the dominant keypress cost** (render.rs:2398). The default (non-narrative) view formats a string for *every* event + trace in the whole run, the run-loop `events` Vec is **uncapped** (attach.rs:743, unlike the plan loop which drains at 1000), and the full vector is built **twice per frame** — once in `attach_panel_counts` just for `.len()` (attach_state.rs:355), once in `render_attach` to render. This is what a user feels on keypress for a long run.

2. **Per-frame whole-file reads, ungated.** Run loop: `load_run` every tick → `find_run_state_path` does an *unbounded-depth* `WalkDir` of the entire runstate dir (state.rs:367). Plan loop is worse — `PlanEventBus::refresh` re-reads plan.json + an `fs::read_to_string` of a per-task `run-id` sidecar **for every task** (plan_event_bus.rs:130/199) every tick, and the plan loop body re-reads ALL plan messages via `read_plan_messages` (attach.rs:471, O(messages)).

3. **Full working-tree filesystem walk per run tick** (main.rs:11356) — recursive `read_dir` + `metadata` stat per file + sort, bounded only by directory pruning.

The code self-instruments (`AttachTickTiming`) with its own thresholds — `max_sync_io_ms=80`, `target_frame_ms=500` — which I used to calibrate severity. Full per-site detail (file:line, frequency, cost, severity) is in the structured output.

Everything below is in-crate (no new test crate) because the test files are declared as plain modules: `mod tui_tests;` at crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs:13615 (also `mod navigable_tests;` :5848, `mod acceptance_render_tests;` :3203). An in-crate module sees every pub(crate) symbol.

(a) RENDER ENTRY-POINT SIGNATURES (all in crates/deadreckon/src/tui/render.rs, all pub(crate), re-exported via tui/mod.rs):
  - render_attach(frame: &mut ratatui::Frame, state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState, spend: &[SpendRecord], traces: &[TraceRecord], events: &[RunEvent], live: &AttachLive, tui_state: &AttachTuiState)   <- render.rs:1734, THE main attach frame.
  - render_plan_attach(frame, paths: &DeadreckonPaths, plan: &Plan, state: &PlanAttachRenderState)   <- render.rs:931.
  - render_chain_attach(frame, chain: &Chain, events: &[ChainEvent], tui_state: &ChainAttachTuiState)   <- render.rs:105.
  - render_campaign_attach(frame, state: &CampaignAttachState)   <- render.rs:318 (no TestBackend wrapper exists; render_campaign_attach_text at render.rs:392 returns plain text but does NOT exercise TestBackend).

(b) EXISTING TESTBACKEND WRAPPERS + FIXTURE BUILDERS (all in crates/deadreckon/src/tui_tests.rs unless noted). The canonical draw-one-frame helper is render_attach_text_with_size (tui_tests.rs:1901):

      #[test]
      fn render_attach_frame_cost_scales_with_history() {
          let (_temp, mut state) = doc_preview_state();
          state.status = deadreckon_core::RunStatus::Executing;
          let n = 10_000usize;
          let spend: Vec<_> = (0..n).map(|t| spend_record(t as u32)).collect();
          let traces: Vec<_> = (0..n).map(|t| trace_record(&state.run_id, t as u32)).collect();
          let events: Vec<_> = (0..n).map(|t| RunEvent{ timestamp: Utc::now(), run_id: state.run_id.clone(), event: RunEventKind::TurnStarted{ turn: t as u32 } }).collect();
          let live = AttachLive { working_dir_exists: true, ..AttachLive::default() };
          let tui = AttachTuiState::default();
          let backend = TestBackend::new(140, 34);
          let mut terminal = Terminal::new(backend).expect("terminal");
          let start = std::time::Instant::now();
          terminal.draw(|f| render_attach(f, &state, &spend, &traces, &events, &live, &tui)).expect("draw");
          let elapsed = start.elapsed();
          eprintln!("render_attach frame n={n}: {elapsed:?}");
      }

Summary of what I measured (all in RELEASE mode, single-threaded, on the throwaway worktree at `/tmp/dr-tuiperf`, branch `perf/tui-profile`):

**Key findings:**
- **`render_attach` Activity view is O(history)** and dominates keypress latency: 106 µs floor (n=0) → 9.0 ms at n=50k. Crosses the ~16 ms (60fps) budget around n≈80k and is already a felt ~1.7 ms at n=10k.
- **`render_attach` Narrative view is flat** (~205–250 µs regardless of in-memory history) because narrative lines don't iterate the events/traces/spend slices the same way — its cost is on-disk flight rows + projection, not in-memory history.
- **`attach_panel_counts` duplicates the activity-line cost**: 7.8 ms at n=50k, essentially equal to the render's own activity-line generation — confirming the "done twice per frame" finding. Combined, the Activity path pays ~2× the line-gen cost per loop iteration.
- **Projection build is O(flight rows on disk)**: 0.39 ms floor → 18–20 ms at 20k rows (linear, ~0.9–1.0 µs/row).
- **Projection cache**: miss = ~26 ms (full build+persist at 5k rows), hit = ~3.4 µs/call (a deep clone of NarrativeProjection paid every narrative draw).

| **render_attach Narrative view** | 237 µs | 236 µs | (flat) |

| Projection (on-disk flight rows) | 0 | 5k | 20k |
|---|---|---|---|
| **build_run_narrative_projection** | 0.39 ms | 4.68 ms | 18.3 ms |
| Cache: miss=25.8 ms @5k, hit(clone)=3.4 µs |

## Interpretation
- **Activity render is the keypress-felt cost.** Linear in events+traces+spend (~180 ns/item over floor) — exactly the `attach_activity_lines` reverse+format path (render.rs:2381). Already a felt ~1.7 ms at 10k history; crosses the 16 ms/60fps budget around n≈80-90k.
- **`attach_panel_counts` pays ~the same O(history) cost as the render itself** (7.8 ms vs 9.0 ms at 50k) — confirms the "line vectors generated twice per frame" finding (attach.rs:775). The Activity path effectively does this work ~2×; caching once would roughly halve per-frame cost.
- **Narrative render is flat in in-memory history** (~205-250 µs) — its real cost is on-disk flight rows via the projection, which is linear (~1 µs/row). The per-draw `NarrativeProjection` clone (render.rs:773) is the 3.4 µs unconditional hit.

## Caveats
TestBackend isolates render+projection CPU only — it does NOT exercise the real terminal flush, idle poll, or the medium-severity per-tick disk walks (`load_run` WalkDir, `collect_attach_live` read_dir) flagged in the mapping; those are independent of run size and weren't timed here. macOS foreground machine, run-to-run variance ~10-25% (directionally identical across both runs). Nothing committed.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 21:20:53Z)**_

Worktree cleaned up, your tree is untouched. Here's what the profiling found — **empirical release-mode numbers**, not guesses.

## Verdict

**The attach TUI is not slow for normal use.** No busy-spin (idle ~4–5 fps, low CPU). Real latency shows up only on **very-long-history runs in the Activity view**, where per-frame cost grows with total events *and is built twice per frame*. A few idle-tick I/O taxes (unbounded dir walks, a `ps` fork) are invisible on small projects but bite on big disks / long histories.

## The numbers (release, 120×40, ns→ms per frame)

| Activity history | Render/frame | | Narrative view |
|---|---|---|---|
| empty | 0.11 ms | | 0.24 ms |
| 100 events | 0.13 ms | | 0.21 ms |
| 1,000 | 0.27 ms | | 0.23 ms |
| 10,000 | **1.75 ms** | | 0.24 ms |
| 50,000 | **9.0 ms** | | **0.24 ms ← flat** |

The narrative view stays **flat ~0.24 ms regardless of history** because it's already windowed — that's the proof the fix works. The Activity view is linear O(events) because it rebuilds the whole history every frame. (Projection itself is cached: cache hit = 3.4 µs.)

So: under ~1k events every frame is sub-millisecond — imperceptible. Even the 50k worst case (9 ms) is technically under the 16 ms smooth-frame bar, but it's **unbounded** (grows forever in a long session) and **wastefully doubled**.

## Hotspots (ranked, all fixes golden-safe)

| # | Sev | Where | Problem | Fix | Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1** | high | `attach_state.rs:355` / `render.rs:2398` | Activity line vector built **twice/frame** (once just for a `.len()` scroll-clamp), one `String` per event over **all** history, events `Vec` **unbounded** (plan caps at 1000, run doesn't) | build once + reuse; window to the visible tail; cap the Vec | 9 ms → **~0.13 ms** @50k |
| **2** | high | `core/state.rs:367` | `load_run` → `find_run_state_path` does an **unbounded `WalkDir`** over the whole runstate dir every tick — O(total runs ever). `list_runs` already caps `max_depth(4)`; this doesn't | add `max_depth(4)` or cache the resolved path | O(all runs) → O(1); kills deep-history first-frame lag |
| 3 | med | `render.rs:1016` | Plan attach reads the **entire** child `spend.jsonl` + `traces.jsonl` per task per frame just for the last line | seek-from-end / incremental tail | removes O(tasks)×O(child-history) I/O |
| 4 | med | `main.rs:11356` | `attach_live_inventory` walks+stats+sorts the **whole working dir** every idle tick | 1–2 s freshness window | idle dir-walk 5×/s → 1×/s |
| 5 | low | `main.rs:11602` | forks `ps -p <pid>` per live PID per idle tick | throttle / libproc | removes the only fork on the draw path |
| 6 | low | `attach.rs:585` | `r` refresh fires a redundant second `draw()` | drop it | saves one frame per `r` |

## Recommendation

For your day-to-day runs the TUI is already sub-millisecond per frame — **no action needed**. The two worth doing are the high-ROI pair:

- **#2** is the cleanest win — low effort, low risk, and arguably a latent bug (it's inconsistent with `list_runs`, which already bounds the walk). It helps first-frame/idle latency on a machine with lots of run history, regardless of run length.
- **#1** is the scaling fix that makes the Activity view O(visible rows) like the narrative view, and caps the unbounded growth.

Both are golden-safe (output unchanged — only the build path changes), and the rider's byte-exact TUI render tests would guard correctness.

A live sampler (`samply`/`cargo flamegraph` driving the real TUI) would add the disk-walk / `ps`-fork / terminal-flush costs the headless harness can't see — worth it only if you want real-world idle-CPU numbers.

Want me to implement **#1 + #2**? I'd do it golden-safe with TUI snapshot tests, in a worktree, same as before.

```text
## Summary

Both optimizations applied to `/tmp/dr-tuifix/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` only. I added one import (`use std::cell::RefCell;`) and added `Clone` to the `AttachLiveInventory` derive so the cache can hand back a clone. Output is byte-identical between refreshes (same walk/sort/`ps` logic, just memoized).

### #4 — `attach_live_inventory`
- **Before** (was at ~main.rs:11356): `fn attach_live_inventory(root: &Path)` walked, sorted, and truncated unconditionally on every call.
- **After** (main.rs:11365): the public `attach_live_inventory` now checks a thread-local cache first; the original body moved verbatim into a new `attach_live_inventory_walk` (main.rs:11400). Added const `ATTACH_LIVE_INVENTORY_FRESHNESS` (main.rs:11357) and a tiny `AttachLiveInventoryCacheEntry` struct (main.rs:11359).
- **Cache key:** the `working_dir` path (`root`), in `thread_local! { static ATTACH_LIVE_INVENTORY_CACHE: RefCell<BTreeMap<PathBuf, AttachLiveInventoryCacheEntry>> }`. Each entry holds the computed `AttachLiveInventory` + an `Option<Instant>` (`walked_at`).
- **TTL:** 1 second. If `now - walked_at < 1s`, returns the cloned cached inventory; otherwise re-walks and refreshes the entry. (Used `BTreeMap` since it's already imported and the task only said HashMap for #5; behavior is identical.)

### #5 — `live_pid`
- **Before** (was at ~main.rs:11599): forked `ps -p <pid>` inline on every tick whenever `alive`.
- **After** (main.rs:11645): `live_pid` still calls the non-forking `deadreckon_core::pid_is_alive(pid)` every tick (death stays prompt), and the `"not running"` branch is unchanged and never forks. The `ps` fork moved into a new `live_pid_command(pid)` (main.rs:11663) behind a TTL cache. Added const `LIVE_PID_COMMAND_FRESHNESS` (main.rs:11643).
- **Cache key:** `pid`, in `thread_local! { static LIVE_PID_COMMAND_CACHE: RefCell<HashMap<u32, (String, Instant)>> }`. Value is `(cached ps command string, fetched_at)`.
- **TTL:** 1 second — `ps` is forked at most once per second per pid; the cached string is reused otherwise.

### Risks (low)
- **Staleness ≤1s:** new files / changed `ps` detail (etime, command) lag by up to 1s. Matches the existing provider-log-scan throttle philosophy and the prompt's intent.
- **Inventory cache memory:** keyed by `working_dir`, so effectively one entry per attached run for the process lifetime — no unbounded growth in practice. The `live_pid` map holds one small entry per supervised pid; stale dead pids linger as entries but are never *read* once dead (the dead branch skips the cache), so it's bounded by distinct pids seen and trivially small. Neither is pruned, which is fine for a TUI process lifetime; could add eviction if ever needed.
- **Per-thread caches:** `thread_local!` means a miss on first use per thread; the attach draw loop runs on a single thread, so this is the intended scope and avoids any locking.
- Liveness (`alive`) and the death transition are never throttled, so the displayed alive/dead state and the `"not running"` text remain frame-accurate.
```

## Summary

Both optimizations applied to `/tmp/dr-tuifix/crates/deadreckon/src/main.rs` only. I added one import (`use std::cell::RefCell;`) and added `Clone` to the `AttachLiveInventory` derive so the cache can hand back a clone. Output is byte-identical between refreshes (same walk/sort/`ps` logic, just memoized).

### #4 — `attach_live_inventory`
- **Before** (was at ~main.rs:11356): `fn attach_live_inventory(root: &Path)` walked, sorted, and truncated unconditionally on every call.
- **After** (main.rs:11365): the public `attach_live_inventory` now checks a thread-local cache first; the original body moved verbatim into a new `attach_live_inventory_walk` (main.rs:11400). Added const `ATTACH_LIVE_INVENTORY_FRESHNESS` (main.rs:11357) and a tiny `AttachLiveInventoryCacheEntry` struct (main.rs:11359).
- **Cache key:** the `working_dir` path (`root`), in `thread_local! { static ATTACH_LIVE_INVENTORY_CACHE: RefCell<BTreeMap<PathBuf, AttachLiveInventoryCacheEntry>> }`. Each entry holds the computed `AttachLiveInventory` + an `Option<Instant>` (`walked_at`).
- **TTL:** 1 second. If `now - walked_at < 1s`, returns the cloned cached inventory; otherwise re-walks and refreshes the entry. (Used `BTreeMap` since it's already imported and the task only said HashMap for #5; behavior is identical.)

### #5 — `live_pid`
- **Before** (was at ~main.rs:11599): forked `ps -p <pid>` inline on every tick whenever `alive`.
- **After** (main.rs:11645): `live_pid` still calls the non-forking `deadreckon_core::pid_is_alive(pid)` every tick (death stays prompt), and the `"not running"` branch is unchanged and never forks. The `ps` fork moved into a new `live_pid_command(pid)` (main.rs:11663) behind a TTL cache. Added const `LIVE_PID_COMMAND_FRESHNESS` (main.rs:11643).
- **Cache key:** `pid`, in `thread_local! { static LIVE_PID_COMMAND_CACHE: RefCell<HashMap<u32, (String, Instant)>> }`. Value is `(cached ps command string, fetched_at)`.
- **TTL:** 1 second — `ps` is forked at most once per second per pid; the cached string is reused otherwise.

### Risks (low)
- **Staleness ≤1s:** new files / changed `ps` detail (etime, command) lag by up to 1s. Matches the existing provider-log-scan throttle philosophy and the prompt's intent.
- **Inventory cache memory:** keyed by `working_dir`, so effectively one entry per attached run for the process lifetime — no unbounded growth in practice. The `live_pid` map holds one small entry per supervised pid; stale dead pids linger as entries but are never *read* once dead (the dead branch skips the cache), so it's bounded by distinct pids seen and trivially small. Neither is pruned, which is fine for a TUI process lifetime; could add eviction if ever needed.
- **Per-thread caches:** `thread_local!` means a miss on first use per thread; the attach draw loop runs on a single thread, so this is the intended scope and avoids any locking.
- Liveness (`alive`) and the death transition are never throttled, so the displayed alive/dead state and the `"not running"` text remain frame-accurate.

I did not run cargo, per instructions.

Done — all six landed on `main` (`83256d3`), release binary rebuilt and installed at your aliased path, worktree cleaned up, tree clean.

## What shipped (all golden-safe — byte-identical TUI output)

| # | Fix | File | Effect |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cap run Activity event history at 1000 (like the plan loop) | `commands/attach.rs` | per-frame line-build is O(window), not O(run length): **~9 ms → <0.4 ms** at 50k events |
| 2 | `find_run_state_path` bounded to `max_depth(4)` (matches `list_runs`) | `core/state.rs` | resolving a run no longer descends into sibling worktree/artifact trees every tick |
| 3 | `latest_trace_line` reads only the **last** JSONL row (file-tail) | `main.rs` + `render.rs` | stops parsing the whole `traces.jsonl` every frame |
| 4 | `attach_live_inventory` 1 s freshness window (`thread_local` cache) | `main.rs` | working-dir walk+stat+sort runs **~1×/s instead of ~5×/s** idle |
| 5 | `live_pid` 1 s TTL cache | `main.rs` | `ps -p <pid>` forks **≤1×/s/pid**; non-forking liveness stays frame-accurate |
| 6 | Drop the redundant immediate redraw on manual `r` refresh (run + plan) | `commands/attach.rs` | saves one full-frame render per `r` |

## How I built it

- **#1, #2, #3, #6** myself (output-correctness-critical / trivial). #3 ships a byte-identical `read_last_jsonl` (scans from the file end, skips a partial trailing write — exactly matching `read_jsonl(...).last()`).
- **#4, #5** via a subagent (localized `thread_local` cache changes, since they don't alter output) — reviewed and folded in.

## Verification (combined state on `main`)

- build ✓ · **lib 12** ✓ · **bins 340** ✓ — the `tui_tests` snapshot tests are the byte-exact contract, and they all pass → **the perf fixes changed zero rendered output**
- characterization: only the 2 known temp-dir goldens (baseline) ✓
- `fmt --check` ✓ · clippy clean in all my changed code ✓

(Note: `cargo clippy --all-targets` reports pre-existing `expect_used` errors in the **test** files — unrelated to this work and not a CI gate here, which is fmt+build.)

## Net effect

The TUI was already fine for normal runs; these make it **bounded** — Activity rendering no longer grows with run length, run resolution no longer scales with total disk history, and idle ticks stop re-walking the working dir / re-forking `ps` / re-parsing trace logs every frame. Same pixels, far less work behind them.

Status: **local `main`** (`83256d3`), binary installed, **not pushed**. Want me to push, or is there anything else on the TUI?

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-8 2026-06-05 21:57:53Z)**_

Fair question to pin me on — I kept saying "byte-identical output," so here's the honest translation of that into what you'd actually notice.

**Visible change: none.** Same pixels, same layout, same colors. That was deliberate (the snapshot tests enforce it).

**Felt change in normal use: also essentially none.** The profiling was clear that for typical runs the TUI was already sub-millisecond per frame. So if you attach to a normal run, it feels exactly the same as before. This was **preventative/robustness work, not a visible feature** — I want to be straight about that.

Where it actually shows up:

- **Long sessions / huge runs** — a multi-hour run with tens of thousands of events was on a path to ~9 ms/frame (visible jank on keypress and scroll); now the Activity view stays responsive regardless of run length. You'd only have felt the *old* behavior on an unusually long-lived attach.
- **Big run history on disk** — if you've accumulated lots of runs, resolving/attaching to one no longer slows down as that pile grows (it used to walk sibling runs' worktree trees). Most people won't have enough history to have noticed.
- **Idle CPU while attached** — this is the one a normal user *might* perceive: while sitting in the TUI, it was re-walking the working directory and forking `ps` ~5×/second. Now ~1×/second. On a laptop that's a bit less fan/battery during a long attach. Subtle, but real and continuous.

**One genuine behavior change:** the Activity panel's scroll-back is now capped at the last ~1000 events on very long runs (it was unbounded; this matches what plan-attach already did). Full history is still on disk in `events.jsonl` — only the in-TUI scrollback is bounded.

So: net-net, you didn't get a "feels snappier" win for everyday use, because there wasn't one to get — the TUI was already fast. What you got is that it **stays** fast on the extremes and stops doing wasteful background work every tick. If you were hoping for a visible improvement in normal use, the honest answer is there isn't one, and the profiling is why I flagged up front that it was "already fine for normal runs."

```rs
use crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent};

/// Shared navigation core for every attach surface (run, plan, campaign, chain).
///
/// The run panel's key semantics are the reference. Each surface implements the
/// movement hooks for its own content model (multi-panel scroll, list selection,
/// step graph, …) and supplies `mode_key` for its mode-specific keys. The common
/// navigation keys — arrows/`jk`, `Tab`/`BackTab`, `PgUp`/`PgDn`, `Home`/`End`,
/// `g`/`G` — are routed identically for everyone by [`dispatch_navigation`].
pub(crate) trait NavigableSurface {
    /// `Tab`: move focus to the next panel (no-op for single-panel surfaces).
    fn focus_next(&mut self) {}
    /// `BackTab`: move focus to the previous panel.
    fn focus_previous(&mut self) {}
    /// `Up`/`k` (delta -1) and `Down`/`j` (delta +1).
    fn scroll_lines(&mut self, delta: isize);
    /// `PgUp` (direction -1) and `PgDn` (direction +1).
    fn scroll_page(&mut self, direction: isize);
    /// `Home`/`g`.
    fn scroll_to_start(&mut self);
    /// `End`/`G`.
    fn scroll_to_end(&mut self);
    /// Handle a key the shared core does not own. Return `true` if consumed.
    fn mode_key(&mut self, _key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
        false
    }
}

/// Route `key` through the shared navigation keys, falling back to the surface's
/// mode-specific hook. Returns `true` if the key was handled.
pub(crate) fn dispatch_navigation<S: NavigableSurface + ?Sized>(
    surface: &mut S,
    key: KeyEvent,
) -> bool {
    // STUB (P1, pre-implementation): no common-key routing yet — everything falls
    // through to the surface's mode hook so the routing test starts red.
    surface.mode_key(key)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crossterm::event::{KeyCode, KeyEvent, KeyModifiers};

    #[derive(Default)]
    struct Recorder {
        log: Vec<&'static str>,
        mode_keys: Vec<KeyCode>,
    }

    impl NavigableSurface for Recorder {
        fn focus_next(&mut self) {
            self.log.push("focus_next");
        }
        fn focus_previous(&mut self) {
            self.log.push("focus_previous");
        }
        fn scroll_lines(&mut self, delta: isize) {
            self.log.push(if delta < 0 { "line_up" } else { "line_down" });
        }
        fn scroll_page(&mut self, direction: isize) {
            self.log
                .push(if direction < 0 { "page_up" } else { "page_down" });
        }
        fn scroll_to_start(&mut self) {
            self.log.push("to_start");
        }
        fn scroll_to_end(&mut self) {
            self.log.push("to_end");
        }
        fn mode_key(&mut self, key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
            self.mode_keys.push(key.code);
            false
        }
    }

    fn key(code: KeyCode) -> KeyEvent {
        KeyEvent::new(code, KeyModifiers::empty())
    }

    #[test]
    fn shared_dispatcher_routes_common_navigation_keys() {
        for (code, expected) in [
            (KeyCode::Tab, "focus_next"),
            (KeyCode::BackTab, "focus_previous"),
            (KeyCode::Up, "line_up"),
            (KeyCode::Char('k'), "line_up"),
            (KeyCode::Down, "line_down"),
            (KeyCode::Char('j'), "line_down"),
            (KeyCode::PageUp, "page_up"),
            (KeyCode::PageDown, "page_down"),
            (KeyCode::Home, "to_start"),
            (KeyCode::Char('g'), "to_start"),
            (KeyCode::End, "to_end"),
            (KeyCode::Char('G'), "to_end"),
        ] {
            let mut surface = Recorder::default();
            assert!(
                dispatch_navigation(&mut surface, key(code)),
                "{code:?} should be handled by the shared core"
            );
            assert_eq!(surface.log, vec![expected], "{code:?} routed to the wrong hook");
        }

        // A non-navigation key falls through to mode_key and is reported unhandled.
        let mut surface = Recorder::default();
        assert!(!dispatch_navigation(&mut surface, key(KeyCode::Char('x'))));
        assert_eq!(surface.mode_keys, vec![KeyCode::Char('x')]);
        assert!(surface.log.is_empty());
    }
}
```

```text
563	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Char('r') && key.modifiers.is_empty() => {
564	                    view = AttachViewMode::Narrative;
565	                    let stage_started = Instant::now();
566	                    let refresh_input = PlanNarrativeRefreshInput {
567	                        paths,
568	                        plan: &plan,
569	                        messages: &messages,
570	                        plan_events: &plan_events,
571	                        feed_events: &feed_events,
572	                        selected,
573	                        config: &narrative_config,
574	                    };
575	                    narrative_notice = Some(start_or_coalesce_plan_narrative_refresh_job(
576	                        &mut narrative_refresh_job,
577	                        plan_narrative_refresh_request(
578	                            &refresh_input,
579	                            NarrativeRefreshKind::Manual,
580	                        ),
581	                        Utc::now(),
582	                    ));
583	                    tick.record_since(AttachLoopStage::ProviderNarrativeRefresh, stage_started);
584	                    // No redundant immediate redraw: the loop redraws at the top of the
585	                    // next iteration (which begins right after input handling), and the
586	                    // background refresh job invalidates the narrative cache on completion.
587	                }
588	                Event::Key(key)
589	                    if matches!(
590	                        key.code,
591	                        KeyCode::Right | KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Tab | KeyCode::Char('j')
592	                    ) =>
593	                {
594	                    selected = (selected + 1).min(plan.tasks.len().saturating_sub(1));
595	                }
596	                Event::Key(key)
597	                    if matches!(key.code, KeyCode::Left | KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k')) =>
598	                {
599	                    selected = selected.saturating_sub(1);
600	                }
601	                Event::Key(key) if key.code == KeyCode::Enter => {
602	                    if let Some(run_id) = plan
603	                        .tasks
604	                        .get(selected)

609	                        }
610	                        let parent_plan = plan.tasks.get(selected).map(|task| AttachParentPlan {

612	                            task_id: task.task_id.clone(),
613	                            campaign_parent: parent_campaign.clone(),
614	                        });
615	                        if cancel_plan_narrative_refresh_job(&mut narrative_refresh_job) {
616	                            narrative_notice = Some(
617	                                "plan refresh cancelled while opening child attach".to_string(),
618	                            );
619	                        }
620	                        suspend_tui(&mut terminal)?;
621	                        let child_result = attach_tui_with_parent(
622	                            paths,
623	                            run_id,
624	                            show_hints,
625	                            parent_plan,
626	                            view,
627	                            visual,
628	                            narrative_config.clone(),

630	                        .await;
631	                        if let Err(err) = &child_result {
632	                            print_error(err);
633	                            let _ = prompt::open("press Enter to return to plan attach...", None);
634	                        }
635	                        resume_tui(&mut terminal)?;
636	                    }
637	                }
638	                _ => {}
639	            }
640	        }
641	    };
642	
643	    cancel_plan_narrative_refresh_job(&mut narrative_refresh_job);
644	    disable_raw_mode()?;
645	    execute!(
646	        terminal.backend_mut(),
647	        DisableMouseCapture,
648	        LeaveAlternateScreen
649	    )?;
650	    terminal.show_cursor()?;
651	    result
652	}
```

```text
155	pub(crate) fn handle_campaign_key(
156	    state: &mut CampaignAttachState,
157	    key: KeyEvent,
158	) -> CampaignAttachKeyAction {
159	    match key.code {
160	        KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') => {
161	            state.selected = state.selected.saturating_sub(1);
162	            CampaignAttachKeyAction::None
163	        }
164	        KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Tab => {
165	            let max = state.campaign.sub_goals.len().saturating_sub(1);
166	            state.selected = (state.selected + 1).min(max);
167	            CampaignAttachKeyAction::None
168	        }
169	        KeyCode::Enter => state
170	            .selected_sub_plan()
171	            .map(|(sub_id, plan_id)| CampaignAttachKeyAction::DrillInto { sub_id, plan_id })
172	            .unwrap_or(CampaignAttachKeyAction::None),
173	        KeyCode::Char('r') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => CampaignAttachKeyAction::Refresh,
174	        KeyCode::Char('b') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => CampaignAttachKeyAction::Back,
175	        KeyCode::Backspace | KeyCode::Esc => CampaignAttachKeyAction::Back,
176	        KeyCode::Char('q') if key.modifiers.is_empty() => CampaignAttachKeyAction::Quit,
177	        KeyCode::Char('d') if key.modifiers.contains(KeyModifiers::CONTROL) => {
178	            CampaignAttachKeyAction::Quit
179	        }
180	        _ => CampaignAttachKeyAction::None,
181	    }
182	}

184	pub(crate) fn note_tui_suspended() -> usize {
185	    TUI_SUSPEND_DEPTH.fetch_add(1, Ordering::SeqCst) + 1
186	}

188	pub(crate) fn note_tui_resumed() -> usize {
189	    loop {
190	        let current = TUI_SUSPEND_DEPTH.load(Ordering::SeqCst);
191	        if current == 0 {
192	            return 0;
193	        }
194	        if TUI_SUSPEND_DEPTH
195	            .compare_exchange(current, current - 1, Ordering::SeqCst, Ordering::SeqCst)
196	            .is_ok()
197	        {
198	            return current - 1;
199	        }
200	    }
201	}
```

```text
30	            self.selected_step = 0;

38	        match key.code {
39	            KeyCode::Up | KeyCode::Char('k') => self.scroll(-1, chain),
40	            KeyCode::Down | KeyCode::Char('j') | KeyCode::Tab => self.scroll(1, chain),
41	            KeyCode::PageUp => {
42	                self.events_scroll = self.events_scroll.saturating_sub(8);

45	                self.events_scroll = self.events_scroll.saturating_add(8);

48	                self.selected_step = 0;

51	            KeyCode::End | KeyCode::Char('G') => {
52	                self.selected_step = chain.steps.len().saturating_sub(1);
53	            }
54	            _ => {}
55	        }
56	        self.clamp(chain);
57	    }
```

```text
===== footer_for_state (run, ~1920) =====
fn footer_for_state(state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState, tui_state: &AttachTuiState) -> String {
    let chain_suffix = if read_chain_step_marker(&state.working_dir)
        .ok()
        .flatten()
        .is_some()
    {
        "  [c] Chain"
    } else {
        ""
    };
    if state.run_root.join("abandoned.json").exists() {
        let footer = format!(
            "worktree cleaned or abandoned  |  q detach  |  deadreckon status/list{chain_suffix}"
        );
        return parent_plan_footer(footer, tui_state.parent_plan.as_ref());
    }
    let base = if tui_state.show_completion_actions && state.status == RunStatus::Completed {
        if is_worktree_run(state) {
            if tui_state.docs_open {
                "[d] Activity  [a] Apply  [b] Abandon  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            } else if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
                "[n] Activity  [v] Visual  [r] Refresh  [d] Docs  [a] Apply  [b] Abandon  [s] Show  |  q detach"
            } else {
                "[n] Narrative  [d] Docs  [a] Apply  [b] Abandon  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            }
            .to_string()
        } else {
            if tui_state.docs_open {
                "[d] Activity  [m] Materialize  [e] Extend  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            } else if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
                "[n] Activity  [v] Visual  [r] Refresh  [d] Docs  [m] Materialize  [e] Extend  [s] Show  |  q detach"
            } else {
                "[n] Narrative  [d] Docs  [m] Materialize  [e] Extend  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            }
            .to_string()
        }
    } else if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
        format!(
            "[n] Activity  [v] Visual={}  [r] Refresh  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach",
            tui_state.visual.label()
        )
    } else {
        "Detach: q Esc Ctrl-D  |  [n] Narrative  |  Focus: Tab  |  Scroll: j/k Up/Down PgUp/PgDn mouse".to_string()
    };
    parent_plan_footer(
        format!("{base}{chain_suffix}"),
        tui_state.parent_plan.as_ref(),
    )
}
===== parent_plan_footer hack (~1970) =====
fn parent_plan_footer(footer: String, parent_plan: Option<&AttachParentPlan>) -> String {
    let Some(parent_plan) = parent_plan else {
        return footer;
    };
    let footer = footer
        .replace(
            "q/Esc/Ctrl-D detach",
            "b/Backspace/q/Esc/Ctrl-D back to plan",
        )
        .replace(
            "Detach: q Esc Ctrl-D",
            "Back to plan: b Backspace q Esc Ctrl-D",
        )
        .replace("q detach", "b/Backspace/q back to plan");
    let campaign = parent_plan
        .campaign_parent
        .as_ref()
        .map(|campaign| {
            format!(
                "campaign {} / {} / ",
                run_prefix(&campaign.campaign_id),
                campaign.sub_id
            )
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let parent_label = format!(
        "parent {campaign}plan {} {}",
        run_prefix(&parent_plan.plan_id),
        parent_plan.task_id
    );
    match footer.split_once("  |  ") {
        Some((lead, rest)) => format!("{lead}  |  {parent_label}  |  {rest}"),
        None => format!("{footer}  |  {parent_label}"),
    }
}
===== chain footer full =====
pub(crate) fn chain_attach_footer_text(chain: &Chain) -> String {
    if chain.status == ChainStatus::Paused {
        let surface = chain_paused_attach_footer_surface(chain);
        let reason = chain.paused_reason.as_deref().unwrap_or("paused");
        let evidence = surface
            .explanation
            .evidence
            .iter()
            .map(|(key, value)| format!("{key} {value}"))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("; ");
        let other = surface
            .secondary_actions
            .iter()
            .map(|action| action.command.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
            .join("; ");
        format!(
            "{} | why {reason} | evidence {evidence} | next {} | other {other} | q detach",
            surface.label(),
            surface.primary_action.command
        )
    } else {
        "[Enter] drill  [r] redo  [e] extend  [p] pause  [k] kill  [Ctrl-D/q/Esc] detach  j/k move  PgUp/PgDn activity".to_string()
    }
}
```

```text
fn footer_for_state(state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState, tui_state: &AttachTuiState) -> String {
    let chain_suffix = if read_chain_step_marker(&state.working_dir)
        .ok()
        .flatten()
        .is_some()
    {
        "  [c] Chain"
    } else {
        ""
    };
    if state.run_root.join("abandoned.json").exists() {
        let footer = format!(
            "worktree cleaned or abandoned  |  q detach  |  deadreckon status/list{chain_suffix}"
        );
        return parent_plan_footer(footer, tui_state.parent_plan.as_ref());
    }
    let base = if tui_state.show_completion_actions && state.status == RunStatus::Completed {
        if is_worktree_run(state) {
            if tui_state.docs_open {
                "[d] Activity  [a] Apply  [b] Abandon  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            } else if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
                "[n] Activity  [v] Visual  [r] Refresh  [d] Docs  [a] Apply  [b] Abandon  [s] Show  |  q detach"
            } else {
                "[n] Narrative  [d] Docs  [a] Apply  [b] Abandon  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            }
            .to_string()
        } else {
            if tui_state.docs_open {
                "[d] Activity  [m] Materialize  [e] Extend  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            } else if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
                "[n] Activity  [v] Visual  [r] Refresh  [d] Docs  [m] Materialize  [e] Extend  [s] Show  |  q detach"
            } else {
                "[n] Narrative  [d] Docs  [m] Materialize  [e] Extend  [s] Show  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach"
            }
            .to_string()
        }
    } else if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
        format!(
            "[n] Activity  [v] Visual={}  [r] Refresh  |  Tab focus  j/k scroll  q detach",
            tui_state.visual.label()
        )
    } else {
        "Detach: q Esc Ctrl-D  |  [n] Narrative  |  Focus: Tab  |  Scroll: j/k Up/Down PgUp/PgDn mouse".to_string()
    };
    parent_plan_footer(
        format!("{base}{chain_suffix}"),
        tui_state.parent_plan.as_ref(),
    )
}
```

```text
2056:fn parent_plan_footer(footer: String, parent_plan: Option<&AttachParentPlan>) -> String {
fn parent_plan_footer(footer: String, parent_plan: Option<&AttachParentPlan>) -> String {
    let Some(parent_plan) = parent_plan else {
        return footer;
    };
    let footer = footer
        .replace(
            "q/Esc/Ctrl-D detach",
            "b/Backspace/q/Esc/Ctrl-D back to plan",
        )
        .replace(
            "Detach: q Esc Ctrl-D",
            "Back to plan: b Backspace q Esc Ctrl-D",
        )
        .replace("q detach", "b/Backspace/q back to plan");
    let campaign = parent_plan
        .campaign_parent
        .as_ref()
        .map(|campaign| {
            format!(
                "campaign {} / {} / ",
                run_prefix(&campaign.campaign_id),
                campaign.sub_id
            )
        })
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let parent_label = format!(
        "parent {campaign}plan {} {}",
        run_prefix(&parent_plan.plan_id),
        parent_plan.task_id
    );
    match footer.split_once("  |  ") {
        Some((lead, rest)) => format!("{lead}  |  {parent_label}  |  {rest}"),
        None => format!("{footer}  |  {parent_label}"),
    }
}
```

```text
fn footer_for_state(state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState, tui_state: &AttachTuiState) -> String {
    let mut items: Vec<(String, String)> = Vec::new();
    let push = |items: &mut Vec<(String, String)>, pairs: &[(&str, &str)]| {
        items.extend(pairs.iter().map(|(k, l)| (k.to_string(), l.to_string())));
    };

    if state.run_root.join("abandoned.json").exists() {
        push(
            &mut items,
            &[
                ("worktree", "cleaned or abandoned"),
                ("deadreckon", "status/list"),
            ],
        );
    } else if tui_state.show_completion_actions && state.status == RunStatus::Completed {
        let actions: &[(&str, &str)] = if is_worktree_run(state) {
            if tui_state.docs_open {
                &[("[d]", "Activity"), ("[a]", "Apply"), ("[b]", "Abandon"), ("[s]", "Show"), ("Tab", "focus"), ("j/k", "scroll")]
            } else if tui_state.view.is_narrative() {
                &[("[n]", "Activity"), ("[v]", "Visual"), ("[r]", "Refresh"), ("[d]", "Docs"), ("[a]", "Apply"), ("[b]", "Abandon"), ("[s]", "Show")]
...
    if let Some(parent_plan) = tui_state.parent_plan.as_ref() {
        let campaign = parent_plan
            .campaign_parent
            .as_ref()
            .map(|campaign| {
                format!(
                    "campaign {} / {} / ",
                    run_prefix(&campaign.campaign_id),
                    campaign.sub_id
                )
            })
            .unwrap_or_default();
        items.push((
            "parent".to_string(),
            format!(
                "{campaign}plan {} {}",
                run_prefix(&parent_plan.plan_id),
                parent_plan.task_id
            ),
        ));
        items.push((
            "b/Backspace/q/Esc/Ctrl-D".to_string(),
            "back to plan".to_string(),
        ));
    } else {
        items.push(("q/Esc/Ctrl-D".to_string(), "detach".to_string()));
    }

    footer(&items)
}
```

```text
=== handle_tui_completion_key body ===
async fn handle_tui_completion_key(
    terminal: &mut Terminal<CrosstermBackend<io::Stdout>>,
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    state: &deadreckon_core::PipelineState,
    key: KeyEvent,
) -> Result<Option<AttachActionNotice>> {
    let action = match key.code {
        KeyCode::Char('m') => CompletionAction::Materialize,
        KeyCode::Char('e') => CompletionAction::Extend,
        KeyCode::Char('a') => CompletionAction::Apply,
        KeyCode::Char('b') => CompletionAction::Abandon,
        KeyCode::Char('d') => CompletionAction::Docs,
        KeyCode::Char('s') => CompletionAction::Show,
        _ => return Ok(None),
    };

    suspend_tui(terminal)?;
    let action_result = match action {
        CompletionAction::Materialize => prompt_materialize_action(paths, state),
        CompletionAction::Extend => prompt_extend_action(state).await,
        CompletionAction::Apply => super::lifecycle::apply_command(
            state.run_id.clone(),
            "squash".to_string(),
            None,
            false,
            false,
            false,
            None,
            false,
        ),
        CompletionAction::Abandon => {
            super::lifecycle::abandon_command(state.run_id.clone(), false, false)
        }
        CompletionAction::Docs => {
            Box::pin(super::doc::doc_command(super::doc::DocCommandArgs {
                run_id: state.run_id.clone(),
                kind: CliDocKind::Narrative,
                export: None,
                polish: false,
                no_confirm: true,
                force: false,
                doc_skill: None,
                doc_provider: None,
                budget_cap: None,
            }))
            .await
        }
        CompletionAction::Show => {
            show_command(&state.run_id, None, false, false, false, false, None)
        }
        CompletionAction::Quit => Ok(()),
    };
    if let Err(err) = &action_result {
        print_error(err);
        print_error_hint(err);
    }
    let _ = prompt::open("press Enter to return to attach...", None);
    resume_tui(terminal)?;
    Ok(Some(AttachActionNotice {
        action,
        success: action_result.is_ok(),
    }))
}
```

```bash
feat(tui): confirm-before-destructive on the completion overlay (P8)

Apply and Abandon now require a two-step in-TUI confirm: the action key arms a
pending state (footer shows "confirm apply? y run / any other key cancel") and
only 'y' fires it; any other key cancels. A single mistyped key can no longer
apply or abandon a run. Resolve the key overloads: Abandon moves from 'b' to
'x' (so 'b' is unambiguously "back"), and the dead 'd'->Docs mapping is removed
('d' = docs toggle, Ctrl-D = detach). Pure resolve_completion_key state machine
+ pending_confirm on AttachTuiState.

back_and_abandon_are_distinct_keys.
```

```text
3452	        (ChainStepStatus::Running, false) => "●",

3458	        (ChainStepStatus::Skipped, false) => "↷",
3459	        (ChainStepStatus::Skipped, true) => "~",
3460	        (ChainStepStatus::Applied, false) => "◉",
3461	        (ChainStepStatus::Applied, true) => "*",
3462	        (ChainStepStatus::Undone, false) => "↶",
3463	        (ChainStepStatus::Undone, true) => "<",
3464	    }
3465	}
```

```text
# Changelog

## Uniform Surface - 2026-06-05

- Added one `display_width()` (strip ANSI, then Unicode display width) and routed
  the line and card truncation/padding helpers through it so wide (CJK) and
  zero-width glyphs no longer miscount terminal columns.
- Collapsed the two divergent `Tone` enums into one shared enum with a single
  tone->ANSI table and a derived tone->ratatui::Color table, so a status renders
  the same color on a line and in a frame; replaced the silent status fallback
  with an explicit `Status` classifier where an unknown status stays visible
  rather than being dimmed into the background.
=== V1-CANDIDATES exists? tail ===
- Depth greater than 2 / cycle-safe arbitrary recursion: the campaign cap is a hard `CAMPAIGN_MAX_DEPTH = 2`. Deeper nesting needs a recursion-safe coordinator, cross-level cycle detection, and a blast-radius story before it earns its complexity.
- Cross-sub dependency edges: campaign sub-goals are independent islands. A V1 could model dependencies between sub-orchestrators so later sub-goals can intentionally build on earlier campaign work instead of only reconciling at roll-up.
- Flattened campaign live attach with a true event tree: production `attach <campaign-id>` is a navigated campaign TUI that drills into existing plan/run TUIs. A V1 could extend `PlanEventBus` to a hierarchy and stream the entire campaign -> plan -> run tree in one pane with expansion, filtering, and cross-level event correlation.
- Planner-chosen per-sub breadth and per-sub provider roles: each sub-orchestrator runs a fixed small `--n` today; the planner could size each front and choose its providers.
- Tree-budget strategies beyond even split: weighted allocation by sub size, dynamic reallocation from finished subs, and concurrent (non-sequential) sub launch once aggregate-budget accounting stays correct under concurrency.
- Sharing campaign records across machines.
```

```text
    frame: &mut ratatui::Frame<'_>,
    area: ratatui::layout::Rect,
    input: &RunNarrativeRenderInput<'_>,
) {
    let tui_state = input.tui_state;
    let rows = area.height.saturating_sub(2) as usize;
    let projection = run_narrative_projection_for_render(input);
    let mut lines = run_narrative_lines_from_projection(&projection, tui_state);
    if area.width >= NARRATIVE_SPLIT_WIDTH && tui_state.visual != NarrativeVisualMode::None {
        let chunks = Layout::default()
            .direction(Direction::Horizontal)
            .constraints([Constraint::Percentage(62), Constraint::Percentage(38)])
            .split(area);
        let visual_lines = narrative::graph_ascii_lines(&projection.graph, tui_state.visual);
        lines.retain(|line| !line.starts_with("Visual:"));
        let visible = visible_narrative_items(&lines, tui_state.narrative_scroll, rows);
        frame.render_widget(
            List::new(visible).block(
                Block::default()
                    .borders(Borders::ALL)
                    .border_style(panel_border_style(
                        tui_state.focused_panel,
                        AttachPanel::Activity,
                    ))
                    .title(panel_title(
                        "narrative",

                        tui_state.narrative_scroll,
                        rows,

                    .borders(Borders::ALL),
            ),
            chunks[1],
        );
    } else {
```

```text
=== render_plan_narrative body ===
fn render_plan_narrative_attach(
    frame: &mut ratatui::Frame<'_>,
    paths: &DeadreckonPaths,
    plan: &Plan,
    state: &PlanAttachRenderState<'_>,
    area: ratatui::layout::Rect,
) {
    let projection = state.narrative_projection.cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| {
        narrative::build_plan_projection(&narrative::PlanNarrativeInput {
            paths,
            plan,
            messages: state.messages,
            plan_events: state.plan_events,
            feed_events: state.feed_events,
            selected: state.selected,
        })
    });
    let mut lines = narrative::narrative_plain_lines(&projection, state.visual);
    if let Some(notice) = state.narrative_notice {
        lines.insert(2, format!("[fresh] {notice}"));
    }
    if area.width >= NARRATIVE_SPLIT_WIDTH && state.visual != NarrativeVisualMode::None {
        let chunks = Layout::default()
            .direction(Direction::Horizontal)
            .constraints([Constraint::Percentage(62), Constraint::Percentage(38)])
            .split(area);
        let visual_lines = narrative::graph_ascii_lines(&projection.graph, state.visual);
        lines.retain(|line| !line.starts_with("Visual:"));
        frame.render_widget(
            List::new(lines.into_iter().map(narrative_list_item)).block(
                Block::default()
                    .title("plan narrative")
                    .borders(Borders::ALL)
                    .border_style(Style::default().fg(ui::TUI_PALETTE.border_focused)),
            ),
            chunks[0],
        );
        frame.render_widget(
            List::new(visual_lines.into_iter().map(narrative_list_item)).block(
                Block::default()
                    .title(format!("visual {}", state.visual.label()))
                    .borders(Borders::ALL),
            ),
            chunks[1],
        );
    } else {
        frame.render_widget(
            List::new(lines.into_iter().map(narrative_list_item)).block(
                Block::default()
                    .title(format!("plan narrative / {}", state.visual.label()))
                    .borders(Borders::ALL),
            ),
            area,
        );
    }
```

```text
=== panel_title ===
pub(crate) fn panel_title(
    title: &str,
    focused: bool,
    offset: usize,
    rows: usize,
    total: usize,
) -> String {
    format!(
        "{}{title}{}",
        selection_glyph(focused),
        scroll_indicator(offset, rows, total)
    )
}
=== scroll_indicator ===
pub(crate) fn scroll_indicator(offset: usize, rows: usize, total: usize) -> String {
    if total <= rows || total == 0 {
        return String::new();
    }
    let first = offset.saturating_add(1).min(total);
    let last = offset.saturating_add(rows).min(total);
    if first == last {
        // A panes-based surface (rows = 1) gets a single selection readout.
        format!(" {first}/{total}")
    } else {
        format!(" {first}-{last}/{total}")
    }
}
```

```text
pub(crate) fn narrative_plain_lines(
    projection: &NarrativeProjection,
    visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
) -> Vec<String> {
    let snapshot = &projection.snapshot;
    let mut lines = vec![
        format!(
            "Narrated {}  status {:?}  visual {}",
            snapshot.snapshot_id,
            projection.state.latest_status,
            visual.label()
        ),
        format!(
            "freshness: {} via {}  covered: {}{}",
            narrative_status_label(&projection.state.latest_status),
            projection.state.provider.source,
            coverage_label(&projection.state.latest_covered),
            projection
                .state
                .last_error
                .as_ref()
                .map(|error| format!("  error: {}", one_line(error, 120)))
                .unwrap_or_default()
        ),
        String::new(),
        snapshot.headline.clone(),
        String::new(),
    ];
    push_claim_section(&mut lines, "Current work", &snapshot.current_work);
    push_claim_section(&mut lines, "Architecture", &snapshot.architecture_notes);
    if !snapshot.agent_table.is_empty() {
        lines.push("Agents".to_string());
        for row in &snapshot.agent_table {
            lines.push(format!(
                "- {} [{}] {} {}",
                row.task_id,
                row.status,
                row.provider.as_deref().unwrap_or("-"),
                row.summary
            ));
        }
        lines.push(String::new());
    }
    if !snapshot.coordination_notes.is_empty() {
        push_claim_section(&mut lines, "Coordination", &snapshot.coordination_notes);
    }
    push_claim_section(&mut lines, "Risks", &snapshot.risks);
    push_claim_section(&mut lines, "Next likely", &snapshot.next_likely);
    if visual != NarrativeVisualMode::None {
        lines.push(format!("Visual: {}", visual.label()));
        lines.extend(graph_ascii_lines(&projection.graph, visual));
        lines.push(String::new());
    }
    lines.push("Evidence".to_string());
    for citation in snapshot.citations.iter().take(8) {
        lines.push(format!("- {} {}", citation.id, citation.summary));
    }
    lines
}

pub(crate) fn graph_ascii_lines(
    graph: &ArchitectureGraph,
    visual: NarrativeVisualMode,
) -> Vec<String> {
    if visual == NarrativeVisualMode::None {
        return Vec::new();
    }
    if graph.nodes.is_empty() {
        return vec!["[stale] not enough architecture evidence yet".to_string()];
    }
    match visual {
        NarrativeVisualMode::Agents => graph_agent_lines(graph),
        NarrativeVisualMode::Files => graph_file_lines(graph),
        NarrativeVisualMode::Evidence => graph_evidence_lines(graph),
        NarrativeVisualMode::Architecture => graph_architecture_lines(graph),
        NarrativeVisualMode::None => Vec::new(),
    }
}

pub(crate) fn validate_graph(graph: &ArchitectureGraph) -> bool {
    graph.nodes.iter().all(|node| !node.evidence.is_empty())
        && graph.edges.iter().all(|edge| !edge.evidence.is_empty())
}

pub(crate) fn read_latest_snapshot(narrative_dir: &Path) -> LatestNarrativeSnapshot {
    let path = narrative_dir.join(NARRATIVE_SNAPSHOTS_JSONL);
    let Ok(raw) = fs::read_to_string(path) else {
        return LatestNarrativeSnapshot {
            snapshot: None,
            skipped_malformed_rows: 0,
        };
    };
    let mut latest = None;
    let mut skipped = 0;
    for line in raw.lines().filter(|line| !line.trim().is_empty()) {
        match serde_json::from_str::<NarrativeSnapshot>(line) {
            Ok(snapshot) => latest = Some(snapshot),
            Err(_) => skipped += 1,
        }
    }
    LatestNarrativeSnapshot {
        snapshot: latest,
        skipped_malformed_rows: skipped,
    }
}
```

```text
pub(crate) trait NavigableSurface {
    /// `Tab`: move focus to the next panel (no-op for single-panel surfaces).
    fn focus_next(&mut self) {}
    /// `BackTab`: move focus to the previous panel.
    fn focus_previous(&mut self) {}
    /// `Up`/`k` (delta -1) and `Down`/`j` (delta +1).
    fn scroll_lines(&mut self, delta: isize);
    /// `PgUp` (direction -1) and `PgDn` (direction +1).
    fn scroll_page(&mut self, direction: isize);
    /// `Home`/`g`.
    fn scroll_to_start(&mut self);
    /// `End`/`G`.
    fn scroll_to_end(&mut self);
    /// Handle a key the shared core does not own. Return `true` if consumed.
    fn mode_key(&mut self, _key: KeyEvent) -> bool {
        false
    }
}
```

```text
=== CHANGELOG head ===
# Changelog

## Attach TUI Uniformity - 2026-06-05

- One shared key dispatcher (`tui::navigation::NavigableSurface` +
  `dispatch_navigation`) drives run, plan, campaign, and chain: arrows/jk,
  Tab/BackTab, PgUp/PgDn, Home/End/g/G behave identically everywhere, with each
  surface supplying only a mode hook. Plan and campaign gained the paging keys
  they lacked.
- One selection cursor (`selection_glyph()` -> `>`), one footer builder
  (`footer(items)`, replacing four divergent styles and deleting the
  parent-plan string-`replace()` hack), and one scroll-position indicator
  (`scroll_indicator()`) on every list panel.
- Apply and Abandon now require a two-step in-TUI confirm; a single mistyped key
  can no longer fire them. Abandon moved off `b` (now unambiguously "back") to
  `x`, and the dead `d`->Docs overload was removed.
- Uniform exit/return: the "press Enter to return" prompts accept
  Enter/q/Esc/Backspace, and Enter on an unloadable child shows an "unavailable"
  notice instead of a silent no-op.
- Friendly empty states (no leaked `*-events.jsonl` filenames), one
  `NARRATIVE_SPLIT_WIDTH` breakpoint shared by run and plan, and an ASCII
  fallback + legend for the chain step glyphs.

## Uniform Surface - 2026-06-05

- Added one `display_width()` (strip ANSI, then Unicode display width) and routed
  the line and card truncation/padding helpers through it so wide (CJK) and
  zero-width glyphs no longer miscount terminal columns.
- Collapsed the two divergent `Tone` enums into one shared enum with a single
  tone->ANSI table and a derived tone->ratatui::Color table, so a status renders
=== AS-BUILT §41 (scroll indicator mentions) ===
188:**`deadreckon` (binary crate, `crates/deadreckon/src/`).** Clap parser definitions (`cli.rs`), a root entrypoint/dispatcher and shared helpers (`main.rs`), private command-family modules (`commands/`), private attach render/state modules (`tui/`), and `dr-gate` as a standalone acceptance-marker writer (`bin/dr-gate.rs`). Supporting modules: `narrative.rs` (deterministic + provider-backed narrative projection), `plan_event_bus.rs` (`PlanEventBus`/`PlanEventFeed`), `tui_events.rs` (`TuiEventFeed`), `ui.rs` + `ui_card.rs` + `cards/` (CLI/TUI rendering vocabulary and cards), `setup.rs` (provider/done-contract resolution), `prompt.rs` (confirmation prompts), and `sleep.rs` (sleep-prevention).
447:│               ├── history.json          # narrative tool-call summaries
454:│               └── narrative/            # attach narrative projection (state.json, snapshots.jsonl, architecture-graph.json)
774:Providers return JSON; the loop parses one action per turn. The CLI sub-agent path is detected by `response.trace["kind"] == "cli_subagent"` before action parsing — those providers do their own tool calls inside the subprocess and return a narrative, not an action JSON.
1315:| `doc` | Print run narrative, as-built, implementation decision ledger, or delta; with optional polish pass |
1352:`attach_command` lives in `crates/deadreckon/src/commands/attach.rs`. The terminal loops delegate to the private `tui/` render/state facade for run, plan, chain, and campaign frames; provider refresh and narrative projection stay outside the render path. Historical `main.rs` line numbers for attach are obsolete after the Decompose pass.
1361:`attach <id> --view narrative` adds a calmer operator projection for runs, plans, and plan child refs. The default remains `activity`, so raw tool/provider lines still open first unless the user requests the narrative view. In narrative mode, `n` toggles back to raw activity, `v` cycles `architecture -> agents -> files -> evidence -> none`, and `r` requests a provider-backed refresh when a configured route is available. While the TTY narrative view is open, meaningful run and plan events also request a provider refresh: errors, completions, tool milestones, docs checkpoints, acceptance running/pass/fail transitions, child-run discovery, task terminal states, and merge-repair milestones. Long-running quiet periods request a refresh after the narrative quiet window when the run or plan is still running. Provider refreshes are background jobs: manual/event/quiet refreshes coalesce while one is active, `q`/`Esc`/`Ctrl-D` detach remains immediate, and child drill-in from plan attach cancels or suspends the in-flight narrator before opening the child run. Provider refreshes are bounded: the prompt is built from redacted evidence windows, the provider must return strict cited JSON, graph labels may only target deterministic graph ids, and failures persist a stale deterministic projection instead of breaking attach.
1386:- **Narrative view**: `--view narrative` or `n` swaps the center-left activity pane for prose sections under the `Narrated` operator heading: freshness/coverage, headline, current work, architecture notes, risks, next likely action, and citations. Wide terminals split that pane with a right-side visual map; narrow terminals collapse to prose first. Run narratives cite `proofs/acceptance-progress.jsonl` or `proofs/turn-acceptance.json` when acceptance evidence exists, so failed done criteria point at the durable proof artifact. Plain/off-TTY narrative attach prints the same projection with citations and ASCII map lines when `--visual` is not `none`; `--json --view narrative` emits the structured state, snapshot, and graph objects. Non-TTY narrative attach stays deterministic and does not call a provider unless a future explicit refresh surface opts in. Chain narrative attach currently returns an unsupported response with `try:` lines for run and plan narrative attach.
1387:- **Completed docs view**: pressing `d` toggles the center-left panel from provider activity or narrative view to `RUN-NARRATIVE.md` rendered through `pulldown-cmark` into ratatui `Line`/`Span`s. Headings, bullets, inline code, fenced code blocks, links, task markers, math, and horizontal rules receive terminal styles and remain scrollable. The docs view remains a separate completed-run artifact rather than being merged into the live narrative projection.
1396:Each attach surface runs a budgeted tick loop. The render path is pure: it must not call providers, recurse through provider roots, append narrative snapshots, or reread unbounded JSONL files. Slow or potentially blocking work is either moved into an attach-owned cache/tailer or into a background refresh job whose completion is polled between frames.
1406:Narrative attach writes projection files, not source-of-truth state. Run projections live under `<run-root>/narrative/`; plan projections live under `<plan-dir>/narrative/`.
1412:Plan projections prefer each child run's latest narrative snapshot when one exists. The plan agent table cites that child snapshot and uses its headline as the child summary, then falls back to child run state when no child narrative exists. Plan graphs also roll up file nodes from child narrative graphs so the plan-level files visual can show cross-agent touched file evidence without copying child logs into `plan-events.jsonl`.
1414:Provider-backed narration is an overlay on these projections. Manual `r` refresh, TTY narrative-view event refreshes, and TTY narrative-view quiet-threshold refreshes start an asynchronous off-loop job (`tokio::spawn`); each attach tick only polls the job handle non-blockingly, so the render loop never stalls on a provider call. Provider refresh jobs build a redacted prompt from the deterministic projection, send only bounded evidence summaries to the selected provider route, validate all returned claims against known evidence ids, reject invented graph ids, and persist a new fresh snapshot only after validation. The default narrator route is `cli:claude-code` with model override `sonnet`, which the Claude Code adapter launches as `claude --model sonnet --dangerously-skip-permissions -p <prompt>`; `--narrative-provider` overrides the route and leaves model selection to that provider/config entry, while `--no-narrative-provider` keeps attach deterministic-only. Event refreshes can bypass the ordinary freshness interval for meaningful deltas, while quiet-threshold refreshes still obey the freshness interval; budget, provider availability, JSON validation, citation validation, graph validation, and redaction guards always apply. If the provider is missing, over budget, behind cadence, returns malformed JSON, cites unknown evidence, emits secret-like text, or fails, attach keeps running and persists a stale deterministic snapshot with the error in `state.json`.
1416:The run and plan narrative panes cache projection objects by coverage and feed signature. Redraws reuse the cached projection, stale provider snapshots survive ordinary frame churn, and render helpers fall back to deterministic projection builders instead of `ensure_*` persistence calls. This is the nonblocking attach contract: provider-backed narrative work may improve the next frame after it finishes, but it never owns the current frame.
1506:- **`deadreckon/tests/`** — `agentic_loop.rs` (~2170 lines; end-to-end run/kill/resume/list/attach/import/doctor + acceptance-gate cycling), plus `attach_inline_card.rs`, `audit_harden.rs`, `cards_{exit_summary,friendliness,preview,status}.rs`, `chain.rs`, `codebase.rs`, `coherence.rs`, `detect.rs`, `doc_depth.rs`, `hygiene_config.rs`, `learning_cli.rs`, `lifecycle.rs`, `narrative_attach.rs`, `npm_wrapper.rs`, `orchestrate.rs`, `providers_list.rs`, `public_surface.rs`, `release_plan.rs`, `self_documenting.rs`, `sleep_{linux,macos}.rs`, `smoke_invariant.rs`, `ui_card.rs`, `update_cli.rs`.
1601:- `deadreckon doc`, `list` DOCS status, doc-aware `apply` commit bodies, extend-parent narrative updates, diff coverage retry, the legacy repo/user/project `run-narrator` skill mechanism, and default split polish skills (`narrator-overview`, `narrator-phases`, `narrator-as-built`, `narrator-decisions`).
1605:- `ratatui` attach TUI with spend/context/acceptance telemetry, provider activity, in-TUI Markdown docs rendering, live files, process panel, scrollable panels, campaign sub-plan cards, and completion action footer. Run, plan, chain, and campaign attach now share an explicit responsiveness contract: render paths are provider-free and write-free, JSONL streams are tailed or cached, provider narrative refreshes run in cancellable/coalesced background jobs, stale narrative snapshots survive redraw, and long operations surface a `deadreckoning` ASCII status line in CLI and footer alike.
1642:1. **TUI streaming and responsiveness.** `tui_events.rs` covers broadcast attach, JSONL replay, partial-line handling, and kill visibility. The May 2026 responsiveness slice adds attach tick budgets, background/coalesced narrative refresh, attach-owned JSONL tailers, provider-log scan throttling, narrative projection caches, chain event tailing, and focused slow-narrator/large-worktree/max-chain smokes.
1820:`deadreckon doc <run-id>` prints the narrative by default. `--kind as-built|decisions|delta` selects another run artifact, `--export <path>` writes it to disk, and `--overwrite` overwrites exports or a prior polish result. `--kind decisions` prints the converged implementation decision ledger, not only regex-detected choice points. For orchestration plans, `deadreckon doc <plan-id>` and `deadreckon doc <plan-result-wrapper-run-id>` resolve to consolidated `PLAN-*` docs; `--kind children` prints the plan child index. `--polish` prints a preview for run docs and refreshes provider-backed plan docs for plans, with deterministic fallback if provider output is unavailable or invalid. `--no-confirm` skips the run-doc prompt for scripts. `--doc-provider <route>` overrides the automatic documentation provider route and `--max-spend <usd>` limits the polish pass. The older `--force` and `--budget-cap` spellings remain hidden compatibility aliases.
```

```text
2843	
2844	41.1 The shared dispatcher + per-mode hook (run is the reference)
2845	`tui::navigation::NavigableSurface` + `dispatch_navigation` own the common
2846	navigation keys (arrows/`jk`, `Tab`/`BackTab`, `PgUp`/`PgDn`, `Home`/`End`,
2847	`g`/`G`). Run (`RunNav`), plan (`PlanNav`), campaign (`CampaignNav`), and chain
2848	(`ChainNav`) each implement the movement hooks for their own content model and
2849	supply `mode_key` for mode-specific keys. The run panel's semantics are the
2850	reference; plan and campaign gained the paging keys they lacked, all by routing
2851	through the one dispatcher.
2852	
2853	41.2 One glyph, one footer, one scroll indicator
2854	`selection_glyph()` is the single selection cursor (`>`) at every call site.
2855	`footer(items)` is the single footer builder — a uniform `<keys> <label>` list
2856	joined by one separator — replacing the four prior styles; the brittle
2857	`parent_plan_footer` string-`replace()` hack is gone (the back affordance and
2858	parent breadcrumb are structural, placed first so a narrow terminal cannot
2859	truncate the exit affordance). `scroll_indicator(offset, rows, total)` (shared
2860	with the run `panel_title`) shows a `first-last/total` window on every list
2861	panel; the chain steps panel windows to that range and the plan/campaign
2862	headers show the selected-item position.
2863	
2864	41.3 Confirm-before-destructive and exit/return semantics
2865	`resolve_completion_key` is a pure state machine: Apply and Abandon arm a
2866	`pending_confirm` (the footer prompts `confirm <action>? y run / any other key
2867	cancel`) and only `y` fires them, so a single mistyped key is harmless. Abandon
2868	is `x` (leaving `b` unambiguously "back"); the dead `d`->Docs mapping is removed.
2869	The "press Enter to return" prompts (`wait_for_return` + `return_key_dismisses`)
2870	accept Enter/q/Esc/Backspace, and Enter on an unloadable child raises an
2871	"unavailable" notice instead of a silent no-op.
2872	
2873	41.4 Empty-state and Windows-glyph rules
2874	Empty list panels carry a one-line next step and never print an internal log
2875	filename (`CAMPAIGN_EMPTY_HINT`). Run and plan share one `NARRATIVE_SPLIT_WIDTH`
2876	breakpoint. `chain_step_glyph(status, plain)` substitutes an ASCII fallback
2877	(with an inline legend) under `--plain` / `NO_COLOR` / a non-VT or Windows
2878	terminal, so a step glyph never renders as a missing box. The byte-exact TUI
```
